design.name: Afterglow Blazes: a phosphor trail to new thresholds
design.pitch: The hidden phosphor underprint works as a trail marker, and it shows only where a cell's lamp is dead, failing or sagging. In those cells the paper glows with green chevrons pointing along the current best route to the nearest threshold into a zone you have not visited yet (a door or window). The wall that holds that threshold gets a "through here" bracket. A "stop" bar marks the mouth of a dead-end pocket. When the Relay starts a chase, a lamp-sag wave runs down the corridors and rewrites the marks so they point at doors leading away from it. Lit walls never show anything, so every lit 3 m module stays identical; the hint lives only in the dark. Ground truth from the code shapes the design. Exits are not scarce: tree edges at height changes become doors or windows (FrontRoomsMap.cs:354-355, 609), so a cell is a mean 3.1 cells from a door or window. Zones are small (median 64 cells). About 45% of walkable zone crossings are invisible same-height crossings. So the useful hint is not "where is an exit" but "which threshold is NEW, and which door gets me away from it". Numbers marked SP are starting points for playtest.
design.player_fantasy: You learn to read the building. In the light the maze is mute, but the paper remembers the way, and it can only say so in the dark. You start looking for the dead troffer in the ceiling line, because under it the walls point. You follow the green chevrons through a door, the ceiling drops from 2.9 to 2.4 m, and the counter ticks. When it runs at you, the lights sag down the corridor ahead of you and the walls flare up to show you a door you can shut behind you. The ink knows the building; it does not promise safety.
rules: R1 Visibility. Ink emission = inkB (print B channel) x G(cell) x message weight. G = charge x darkness gate, where the gate is smoothstep(0.55, 0.15, Ls) and Ls is the cell's own lamp level, low-passed. A lit cell (Ls >= 0.55) shows exactly nothing, so lit 3 m modules stay identical (LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC 'every module looks the same' rule).

R2 Who carries ink. Only wallpaper does: Level 0 walls and wallpaper-faced columns (Lobby paper, FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1764). Office zones use drywall (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1773; LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC.md:58), so they are blind zones with no hints. That is 13.6% of cells in simulation (officeShare 0.3, FrontRoomsMap.cs:117).

R3 Four shape-coded messages per cell. GROUND is the neutral, non-directional underprint at weight 0.35. FLOW (with a direction) is chevrons pointing along the wall toward the route, at weight 1.0. HERE means the route leaves through this face's opening: vertical brackets flanking the door or window, weight 1.0. STOP marks this face as the mouth of a dead-end pocket: horizontal bars, weight 1.0. Priority is STOP > HERE > FLOW > GROUND.

R4 Calm target (Relay Dormant/Listen/Wander, or Hunt/Search more than 8 path-cells away) is the nearest NEW THRESHOLD. That is a Door or Window edge whose far cell lies in a zone not in zonesVisited (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:869-877), plus the untaken key of the zone you stand in. Unbroken windows cost +4 cells (SP), because breaking glass is heard at 56 m: GlassNoiseRadius 40 (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:150) x hearing 1.4 (FrontRoomsHunter.cs:32). Broken windows cost 0. With doorsNeedKeys on, the key comes first, then doors (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1695-1699).

R5 Pressure target (Relay in Chase, or in Hunt/Search within 8 path-cells of the player) is an unbroken Door whose far cell is farther from the Relay (by breadth-first search, BFS) than its near cell. Windows are excluded: a 1 s hold (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1676-1689) lets a 4.2 m/s chase close 4.2 m, and broken glass is passable for the Relay. Route costs (SP): +6 per cell within 2 steps of the Relay, +2 per cell on an open straight line from it within 4 cells, so the route bends out of sight.

R6 Only on-route dark cells point. The route is a greedy descent of the target field from the player's cell, up to 24 cells, plus cells 1 step off it at T0-T1. Off-route dark cells show GROUND. Simulation: when every dark cell points, beacon-seeking walkers ping-pong (2.4 new zones per 100 cells, worse than a random walker's 5.6). Showing only on-route beacons gives 8.0.

R7 STOP marks the mouth cell of each dead-end branch: cells removed by iterative leaf pruning, with door and window edges counted as passable and the built-area boundary counted as open. Outside a chase wave only branches of depth >= 2 are marked; inside a wave all of them. A FLOW route never enters a branch unless its target is inside it.
R8 The ink is truthful. It never points into a dead end, through a broken door on the Relay's side, or at the Relay's cell. Lying is a narrative slot, recommended no earlier than T4.

R9 Commit gate. A cell's shown message may change only when (a) the cell has been unseen for >= 0.5 s (the synthesis's visibility BFS), (b) its own Ls >= 0.8 (ink invisible under light), or (c) a sag or wave front is at that cell (a deliberate beat). Each cell changes at most once per 2 s.
R10 The ink does not move with the visible print. B holds the same GROUND in every rest and motion keyframe; only glyph slices differ in B. A print jump or crawl never changes what glows.
R11 Three delivery channels. Natural dark cells are always on (failing 9.5%, dead 5.0%, dim 3.1% of cells). Calm power sags are local and periodic. The chase wave is travelling and rare.
R12 Dark is never cover. The Relay's sight is a 12 m raycast that ignores light (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:926-931), and nothing in the ink or its fiction may imply that darkness is safe.

R13 Tall halls are not slower; the ink must not advertise them as refuges. Relay speeds have no ceiling term (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:213, 220, 238-239, 352). The rig only receives CeilingHeight for animation (FrontRoomsRelayRig.cs:47, 63).
design.placement_and_generation:
Nothing is hand-placed. Every message is derived per cell from map data, so it works in the endless procedural maze and survives the revisit shift. Targets use only features that do not change with revision: zones, border edges and keys are pure functions of the seed (MAP_GENERATION.md:97). The route is recomputed when a chunk is rebuilt (at least 24 m away, FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:612).

Where beacons come from:
1. Natural lamp temperament. It is rolled from Hash(seed, cell, 211) (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1087, 1128), so it is fixed per cell and known even for unbuilt cells. A Python port of the generator over 12 seeds measured 62.3% steady, 20.1% stutter, 9.5% failing, 5.0% dead and 3.1% dim. Effective beacon cells, where the gate can open, are failing (breathes), dead (steady glow) and dim (faint): 17.6%. Stutter cells barely register after low-pass.
   - From any cell, the nearest failing or dead lamp is a mean 1.84 cells away (p90 4).
   - Of the cells beside a door or window, 44% have a failing or dead lamp within 1 step, 73% within 2.
   - On the walker's route, a readable beacon came every ~6 cells (18 m).
2. Room modules. Level Designer modules can author ModuleLamp Dead/Failing/Off per cell (FrontRoomsRoomModuleData.cs:30; FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1130) to make deliberate dark reading rooms. Recommended module tier: no more than 1 dark reading room per 4 chunks.
3. Start beat. The map forces mode 3 (dead) on the 3rd walk-in cell past startDoorCell. The cell ahead of the door is guaranteed open for 150+ cells (MAP_GENERATION.md:19).
4. Optional "border dusk" lever. Cells beside door/window edges roll failing 25% / dead 10% instead of 10% / 5%. Use it only if playtests show HERE too rare (naturally only 14% of exit-adjacent cells are dark themselves). It needs visual-chat sign-off, because flicker odds are their numbers (LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC.md:76).

Densities from the simulation (5x5-chunk built area, about 1,600 cells, about 25 zones):
- Thresholds are plentiful. Exits per zone (mean): Low 14, Standard 10, Tall 20.
- Nearest door: median 4 cells, 55% of cells within 4.
- Nearest new threshold: typically 3-7 cells.
- Dead-end branches: 31 per 1,000 cells, 70% of them 1-cell alcoves. About 5% of cells are in branches, so roughly 50 branches in range, about 15 of depth >= 2.
- Tall zones are about 12% of cells.

Simulated progress (150-cell walks, 16 seeds), as new zones / new-zone thresholds per 100 cells:

| Walker | New zones | Thresholds |
|---|---|---|
| Random walker | 5.6 | 3.1 |
| On-route ink | 8.0 | 6.1 |
| Perfect knowledge | 15.1 | 12.5 |
| Continuous 3-cell route dimming | 14.7 | — |

So natural beacons make it a hint, at about 2x random and half of perfect. Continuous route dimming makes it a GPS, which is why sags are snapshots and waves are rate-limited.

design.triggers_and_timing:
All numbers are SP.

Glow gate, per cell, every frame:
- L = Fixture.level x held. It is computed for every built fixture, even beyond lightRadius (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1166-1167). A cell with no fixture counts as L = 0.
- Ls = low-pass(L), time constant 0.35 s (-16 dB at 3 Hz).
- Wall light W = min(1, L + 0.2 x sum of the 4 neighbours' L). Unshadowed lamps light through walls (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1137-1140).
- Charge: when W > C, C += (W - C)(1 - e^(-dt/2 s)); otherwise C *= e^(-dt/tau_d), with tau_d = 40 s at T0.
- Initial charge at build: steady/stutter 1.0, failing 0.75, dim 0.5, dead = spill W.
- G = C x smoothstep(0.55, 0.15, Ls). The glyph is visible at G >= 0.08.

What each temperament does (Level() at FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1184-1213):

| Temperament | Lamp level | Ink behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| Failing | 0.25-0.70 with dropouts | Ink breathes at ~0.49 Hz (sin 3.1t): ~1 s reads every ~2 s |
| Dead | 0, blinks 0.8 for 0.06-0.18 s every 8-28 s | Steady glow from spill charge; each blink tops C up by ~0.03 |
| Dim | 0.42 | G ~ 0.25 C, readable only within ~5 m |
| Stutter | bursts | G <= 0.1, effectively silent |

Fields and route:
- The target field is rebuilt on any of these, rate-limited to 2 Hz: ZoneEntered, KeyTaken, DoorMoved/DoorBroken/GlassBroken (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:59-65), relay.StateChanged (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:141), ChunkBuilt/ChunkDropped, or a mode switch.
- The route is re-descended whenever the player changes cell (~every 0.94 s at 3.2 m/s walk).
- Target stickiness: keep the current threshold until it is reached or becomes at least 6 cells worse than the best alternative.

Mode switch:
- Calm to pressure: immediately on Chase, or on Hunt/Search within 8 path-cells.
- Pressure to calm: 8 s after the Relay is in Listen/Wander, or more than 8 cells away in Search.
- Commits still obey R9, so a switch shows first in unseen or lit cells, or under the wave.

Power sag (calm pacing pulse):
- Every 75-120 s at T0.
- Not within 30 s of a wave (the synthesis's 30-45 s quiet after an event, 10_synthesis.md:167). Never while the player stands in an Office zone.
- Shape: BFS radius 4 cells (12 m) around the player; lamps dip to 0.35x; attack 0.6 s, hold 4 s, release 1.5 s.
- All messages in the radius commit at dip start.

Chase wave:
- Fires on StateChanged(Chase) if the cooldown has passed (90 s at T0). It is the synthesis's corridor wave, 10_synthesis.md:143, 166.
- Origin is the Relay's cell. The front moves at 8 m/s (2.67 cells/s) along passable edges, with a 0.5 s delay at shut doors, and reaches 10 cells beyond the player.
- Each cell: lamp dips to 0.3x, attack 0.3 s, hold 2.5 s, release 1.2 s. Pressure messages commit when the front arrives.
- Because the wave outruns the player's 5.5 m/s sprint (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:147), about 20 m of dim, readable corridor sits ahead of a fleeing player for the 5 s of stamina (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:149).
- The wave freezes on Caught.
design.teaching_curve:
1. Seconds 0-3. Space starts the run. The stream door opens once the maze is ready, within 3 s (MAP_GENERATION.md:21). The maze lamps rise in 0.6 s (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:118, 750), so nothing glows at the door itself.
2. Seconds ~4-8. The forced-dead cell, 6-9 m ahead on the walk-in line, is a gap in the troffer line with green chevrons on both side walls and a FLOW or HERE glyph on the end wall facing the player, readable head-on from the door. It points to the nearest new threshold, typically 3-7 cells away. The Relay is still dormant: it is released 3 s after the door shuts once the player is 4 m in, and spawns 9-15 cells away out of sight (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:49; MAP_GENERATION.md:34). This first read is calm.
3. Seconds ~20-40. Following the chevrons ends at a door or window. The ceiling changes height and "ZONE 02" appears (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:1540). This builds the association "green leads to new ground".
4. Seconds 60-120. The first power sag, if no chase has happened yet. All walls within 12 m flare at once for 4 s, teaching that sags give a snapshot and that STOP bars mark pockets.
5. First chase. The wave runs past the player, and the chevrons switch to doors that lead away from the Relay. This teaches the pressure mode and the door verb: shut the door, and it costs the Relay 2.5 + 0.25 s to break (MAP_GENERATION.md:36).

No HUD tutorial text by default. If fewer than 50% of first-time players follow a FLOW within 60 s in playtest, add one Flash line written by the narrative chat on the first beacon read, using the existing Flash card (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:1546-1548). After that, the player's skill is to scan the ceiling line for dead or failing troffers, read end walls at 20 m and side walls within 6-8 m, and choose between the ink's new threshold and safety.
design.escalation_over_run:
The ink escalates by scarcity and by the physics of charge, never by turning untruthful early. Tiers follow the unconfirmed DP08 proposal (tier index from the game); with no tier system, use T0.

| Tier | Route beacons | Decay tau_d | Weight | Sags every | Wave cooldown | STOP outside waves |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T0 | on-route + 1 off | 40 s | 1.0 | 75-120 s | 90 s | depth >= 1 |
| T1 | on-route + 1 off | 30 s | 1.0 | 90-150 s | 120 s | depth >= 1 |
| T2 | on-route only | 25 s | 0.85 | 120-180 s | 150 s | depth >= 2 |
| T3 | on-route only | 18 s | 0.75 | 150-210 s | 180 s | depth >= 2 |
| T4+ | only within 15 cells of the target | 12 s | 0.6 (readable ~12 m head-on) | 180-240 s | 240 s | depth >= 2 |

- T3 also caps the wave at 6 cells ahead of the player.
- At T4+ the ink "loses the thread" far from a threshold. Optional: the narrative 'unreliable ink' variant unlocks.
- The DP08 proposal adds failing lights per tier. That creates more dark cells (more beacons) but less spill light, so charge is lower and glyphs are fainter: more hints, each harder to read. This is consistent with the physics.

What "progress" means for the ink: one new threshold, meaning a door or window into an unvisited zone. The world is infinite, so a target always exists. When most zones in the built 5x5 area are visited, targets fall to the built boundary and the flow points outward. Following the ink always means moving away from the known, and it never leads back.

Coupling to flag for Red and the map chat:
- Following the ink roughly doubles thresholds per minute (simulation: 6.1 vs 3.1 per 100 cells, about 3.9 vs 2.0 per walking minute). Following the ink therefore also speeds up tier escalation. That is a deliberate risk/reward: the ink is help and lure at once.
- DP08's 'every 4 zones' counts zone ids, and 45% of walkable zone crossings are invisible same-height ones. Zones would tick about 3.6 per minute even for a random walker. Suggestion (SP): count tiers by new thresholds, 6 per tier or 2.5 min.
design.interaction_with_relay_and_escapes:
How the ink fits each Relay and escape fact:

**Sight and light.** The Relay's sight is a 12 m ray at eye height with no light term (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:926-931; tuning FrontRoomsHunter.cs:26). Darkness, sags and waves have no mechanical effect on it. The ink only changes what the player knows.

**Doors (the main pressure verb).**
- A wandering Relay will not cross shut doors (Wander searches with throughDoors false, FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:426, 463).
- Hunts and chases plan through doors and break them in 2.5 s plus a 0.25 s leaf fall (MAP_GENERATION.md:36).
- Shutting a door makes noise at 14 x 1.4 = 19.6 m (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:788). Noise is ignored during Chase and BreakDoor (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:281).
- So pressure FLOW leads to a door away from the Relay. HERE brackets the door wall. After the player passes and shuts it, the next commit (unseen, lit, or still in the wave) points onward.
- LoseTrack follows the player into the room behind a door they just used (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:294-301). Pressure routes therefore prefer a door followed by a bend (the +2 sight-line cost), so the player is out of its line when it arrives.

**Windows.**
- The Relay's BFS skips unbroken glass (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:462), and the pane's collider blocks its sight ray.
- A tall zone (no key, FrontRoomsMap.cs:636; exits only by windows, FrontRoomsMap.cs:354) can only be entered by the Relay through windows the player broke.
- Breaking is a 1 s hold and is heard at 56 m. Calm routes may lead through windows (progress, at +4 cost); pressure routes never do.
- Not true and not to be advertised: tall halls slowing the Relay (no ceiling term in its speeds).

**Sprint.** 5 s of stamina at 5.5 m/s against a 4.2 m/s chase (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:147-149). Sprinting is heard at 36 m (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:865). The wave front at 8 m/s stays ahead of a sprinting player, so the dimmed, readable cells are always the next ~20 m.

**Line of sight.** Pressure costs push the route off the Relay's straight lines. Arches block sight (MAP_GENERATION.md:59), so arch edges cost -1 in pressure (SP).

**Dead ends.** STOP marks branch mouths. Catches inside branches are a key metric.

**Relay wake.** Pressure routes add +2 for cells the Relay walked through in the last 10 s. The green trail ('way out') and the reprinted wake ('where it walked') therefore rarely overlap.

**Leash, relay and release.** Unaffected. The ink never reads the Relay's position in calm mode, so calm FLOW can lead straight into a wandering Relay. This is deliberate: the ink knows the building, not the monster. The only leak is the calm-to-pressure switch during Hunt within 8 cells. It is delayed by the commit gate, and Red can restrict pressure to Chase only.

**Keys.** Keys already glow yellow and spin (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1787, 1730-1745). With doorsNeedKeys off (FrontRoomsLevelProfile.cs:31) a key is a score item (Caught overlay, FrontRooms3DGame.cs:1495), so it is just another calm target. With the flag on, the key comes first, because shut doors need the key of the zone you stand in.
design.interaction_with_moving_print:
1. **Opposite masking phases.** The visible print changes in the dark: it slips inside its own cell's lamp-dark window (10_synthesis.md:139-142), because ink colour vanishes when unlit. The glow glyph changes in the light, because phosphor is swamped by its lamp at Ls >= 0.8. A failing lamp therefore gives both systems a legal change window every couple of seconds, in opposite phases. A dead cell has no lit phase, so its glyph changes only when unseen. This is the main reason the ink cannot use the print's flicker-mask rule: in the dark, the ink IS what you see.
2. **B is constant across print keyframes.** It holds GROUND in every rest and motion keyframe, so discrete jumps and crawls never alter the glow. Glyph slices (FLOW+u, FLOW-u, HERE, STOP) carry the R/G of the rest print they replace, so swapping them is invisible under light. Two options for the visual chat:
   - (a) One glyph set per rest-print family. For example, 4 rest prints x 4 glyphs = 16 slices plus 4 rest slices, leaving 12 motion frames in the synthesis's 8x4 sheet.
   - (b) One extra B-only fetch, branched on G > 0, which runs only on the ~18% of wall pixels in dark cells.
3. **Slow crawl** at scripted beats only picks off-route cells, and forces GROUND at 0.35 weight there. Moving ink never carries a message.
4. **Chase wave.** One BFS front at 8 m/s carries three things in lockstep: the synthesis's visible reprint, the lamp dip, and the pressure-mode commit. Behind the front, walls are dim, newly printed and pointing at doors; ahead of it they are still lit and silent. Shared arrival times keep the print wave and the ink exactly in sync. The title-stream rebase caveat (10_synthesis.md:144) applies to its origin.
5. **Subliminal drift** (<= 1-2 mm/s, scale breathing +/-0.3%) also moves B if it shares the fetch. That is imperceptible and fine. Glyphs must otherwise be still to be read.
6. **Per-roll phase** `strip & 3` (10_synthesis.md:80, 193) means every FLOW wall looks identical in every on-route cell. The deliberate beat is that this cell points, not that it looks unique.
7. **Freeze** everything on Caught. While the player is in the title stream rooms, the ink is off (G = 0), and stream-room walls must be masked so they do not read aliased map state (10_synthesis.md:218).
design.readability_and_accessibility:
**Glyph authoring** in the synthesis's Figma frame, 750 x 1125 mm, one roll repeat:
- FLOW: 2 chevrons per 0.75 m repeat, so 8 per cell wall, reading as '>>>>>>>>'. Chevron height 400 mm, stroke >= 100 mm, gap ~175 mm.
- HERE: vertical bars 100 x 900 mm. They land on the ~1 m of wall beside a door (1.0 m opening) and the ~0.8 m beside a window (1.4 m opening), both centred in a 3 m edge (LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC.md:48-49).
- STOP: 2 horizontal bars, 600 x 120 mm.
- GROUND: non-directional vertical dashes, 60 mm.
- Glow appears only in a height band of 0.8-2.0 m (player eye 1.62 m, LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC.md:133). That includes 5.4 m tall-hall walls.

**Distances** (vertical FOV 76°, FrontRooms3DGame.cs:227; 1080p gives about 691/d px per metre):
- Head-on at 20 m: a 0.40 m chevron is ~14 px with 3.5 px strokes. Readable.
- At 1 m it is ~280 px.
- Side walls are only readable within 6-8 m, because foreshortening at 20 m down a 3 m corridor is ~0.075.
- So the decision glyph is the one on the END wall at a T or turn, and the side-wall chevrons confirm it up close.
- Fog is ExponentialSquared at 0.014 (FrontRoomsLook.cs:19, 32), so 92.5% of the glow survives at 20 m.

**Luminance targets for the visual chat.** Meaning is carried by shape and luminance, not hue, so the system is safe for red-green colour-blind players.
- Full charge in a dead cell with at least 2 lit neighbours: glyph-to-paper ratio >= 1.3.
- A failing cell at Ls 0.3: >= 1.15.
- Emission capped at ~12% of a lit wall's luminance, so the ink stays faint.
- Colour about 530 nm yellow-green (ZnS:Cu).

**Photosensitivity:**
- Ls is low-passed at 0.35 s.
- Messages change at most once per 2 s per cell.
- Sags and waves are single slow dips with ramps of at least 0.3 s.
- No glyph may sync to stutter bursts.
- Pre-existing risk to audit together with the ink: stutter mode switches 0.95 <-> 0.05 off Perlin(t x 23) during 0.15-0.85 s bursts (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1188-1196), which can exceed 3 flashes per second. Run the synthesis's P2 flash check with the glow channel included.

**Accessibility settings:**
- Reduce wall motion (required, 10_synthesis.md:197-200): no travelling wave. It is replaced by a static 4 s sag of radius 4 cells at Chase start. The Ls time constant becomes 1.0 s, there is no crawl, and glow comes only from failing, dead and dim lamps plus sags.
- Ink assist: intensity x1.5, GROUND off, strokes +30% via an alternate glyph set.
- The ink is never the only signal. Doors and windows stay visible as geometry.
design.implementation_data_flow:
**CPU (map chat).** A new plain-C# FrontRoomsWayfinding, owned by FrontRoomsMapWorld and ticked in Update after TickFixtures (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:559-575).
1. Lamp input. Per built cell, L = Fixture.level x held (Fixture.level FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:98; computed for all built fixtures at 1166-1167), exposed through a new read-only LampLevel(cell) and LampMode(cell). LampMode is a pure function of the seed (hash 211), so it also works for unbuilt cells. A new LampDip(cell, depth, attack, hold, release, delay) multiplier inside TickFixtures drives sags and waves; it really dims the light.
2. Gate. For each of up to 1,600 cells: Ls, W, C and G as in the triggers. That is about 10 flops per cell, under 0.05 ms.
3. Fields, at most 2 Hz, on events:
   - Target field D_t: bucket Dijkstra over built cells with costs 0-6, using Cache.Edge and PassageBetween (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1030-1050). Doors are passable, glass is passable for the player, walls and failed chunks are not.
   - D_r: BFS from the Relay's cell, in pressure mode only.
   - Leaf pruning for STOP, rerun on ChunkBuilt/Dropped and door/window changes.
   - Route: greedy descent from the player's cell, up to 24 cells. Ties are broken by Hash(seed, x & 63, y & 63).
   - Estimated 0.2-0.4 ms per rebuild.
4. Messages: STOP > HERE > FLOW (cells in the route, plus the cells 1 step off it at T0-T1) > GROUND. Direction is the arg-min neighbour.
5. Commit gate (R9), using the visibility service (seen flags and unseen timers) from 10_synthesis.md:135-138.
6. Pack a 64x64 RGBA8 texture indexed by cell & 63 (world period 192 m; 10_synthesis.md:131):
   - R reserved for the print state (visual chat).
   - G = G x 255.
   - B: bits 0-1 direction (N/E/S/W), bits 2-3 message, bits 4-7 tier/variant.
   - A = Ls x 255, which is also the print's flicker mask.
   - Upload 16 KB per frame with SetPixelData and Apply(false). Point filter, Repeat wrap. Shader.SetGlobalTexture('_FR_CellState') and SetGlobalVector('_FR_Ink', weight, tier, reduceMotion, 0).

**GPU (visual chat**, FrontRoomsSurface ForwardLit under the _FR_PRINT keyword):
1. cell = floor((posWS + nWS x 0.5).xz / 3) & 63, with one point fetch.
2. If G > 0: the face comes from nWS. Compare the stored direction with the face's +u, -u, -n and +n to pick FLOW+u, FLOW-u, HERE, or GROUND (when the route is behind the viewer).
3. Read B at the glyph slice. Emission += inkColour x B x G x weight x band(0.8-2.0 m) x the paper cavity/fibre mask (10_synthesis.md:189). Fog is applied after.
4. An unset global means G = 0, so edit mode, lookdev and the Level Designer fall back to no ink.

**Events in:**
- map.DoorMoved, DoorBroken, GlassBroken, KeyTaken (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:59-65).
- relay.StateChanged (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:141).
- New: ZoneEntered and the visited set from FrontRooms3DGame.cs:869-877; ChunkBuilt/ChunkDropped; Tier.

**Budget (SP):** CPU <= 0.4 ms on average and <= 1.0 ms on field-rebuild frames; GPU <= +0.2 ms against the synthesis perf gate (10_synthesis.md:230); 16 KB of memory plus glyph slices inside the existing print array.

playtest_metrics: Hint strength (ink on/off A/B, same seeds): new-zone thresholds per minute. Target ratio 1.6-2.2; the simulation predicts 2.0. Above 2.5 the ink is a GPS: cut sags or T0 adjacency. Below 1.3 it is noise: raise weight or add border dusk.
Follow rate: share of beacon encounters (FLOW cell within 8 m and in view for >= 0.5 s) after which the player's next 3 cells descend the target field. Target 50-75%.
Teaching: time from first beacon in view to first follow. Target under 20 s for at least 70% of first-time players. Also the share of players crossing their first ink-led threshold within 60 s.
Beacon spacing on routes actually walked: target a readable beacon every 5-8 cells (simulation: 6.2). Also time spent in Office blind zones per run.
Chase outcomes with and without the wave: escape rate (Relay returns to Listen/Wander without a catch). It should rise, but not above 80% at T0. Also doors shut per chase.
Dead-end catches: share of catches inside leaf-pruned branches, ink on vs off. Target at least 50% lower with the ink on.
Truth audit (automated): every FLOW route terminates at a valid target; 0 FLOW into branches; 0 pressure routes through windows.
Change-blindness audit (automated): 0 message commits while a cell is flagged seen, except at sag or wave fronts. Fewer than 1 glyph flip per cell per 2 s.
Flash audit: at most 3 luminance transitions per second over 25% or more of the screen, with glow, stutter, sag and wave combined. Also measured with reduce-motion on.
Readability stills: correct direction call at 6/12/20 m head-on and 6 m grazing. Target at least 90% at 12 m and at least 75% at 20 m, with and without ink assist, plus a colour-blind filter pass.
Pacing: interval between sags and waves actually experienced, and minutes per tier with the ink on vs off. It flags whether the ink accelerates escalation too much.
Perf: wayfinding CPU ms (average and on rebuild frames), upload KB, GPU delta, measured under the synthesis perf gate (seeds 2554/20388 plus a Level 0 flythrough).
Player read (questionnaire): did the green marks feel like help, a lure, or noise? Did players believe darkness was safe? The intended answer is 'no'.
failure_modes_and_exploits: Beacon ping-pong. If every dark cell points, players chase lights instead of routes. Simulated walkers that seek visible beacons dropped to 2.4 new zones per 100 cells against 5.6 for a random walker. Fix: R6 (on-route only, GROUND elsewhere), which gave 8.0.

GPS creep. Continuous route dimming (a 3-cell trail) reached 14.7 against perfect knowledge at 15.1. Fix: sags are local snapshots with long intervals, waves happen only on chase with a cooldown, and the ink on/off ratio is tracked.
Visible glyph swaps. Dead cells have no lit phase, so they commit only when unseen. Failing cells commit in their lit phase. Do not reuse the print's flicker-mask rule for the ink.
Flow flip-flop at equal distances, or when a near target changes. Fix: hash tie-break on (cell & 63), the 6-cell target stickiness rule, and at most 1 commit per 2 s.
Invisible borders. About 45% of walkable zone crossings are same-height Open/Arch edges, so ZONE NN can tick without a threshold. The ink targets thresholds only, and tier counting should follow.

Office blind zones (13.6% of cells): routes through drywall lose the thread. Mitigate with +1 route cost per Office cell (SP), or accept them as deliberate hint-free stretches. The narrative should explain them.
Dark clusters. A dead cell among dead or failing neighbours has little spill charge, so it looks blank. That is intended physics but may read as a bug, so the fiction must say the ink needs light.
Lure into noise. Calm routes into tall zones require breaking glass, heard at 56 m. Mitigation: +4 window cost. Otherwise keep it as the intended risk.
Relay radar. The calm-to-pressure switch leaks that the Relay is hunting nearby. The commit gate delays it; Red can restrict pressure mode to Chase only.
False refuge. Players may assume dark or tall equals safe. Neither is true in code (sight ignores light; speeds have no ceiling term), so the ink and its fiction must never imply it.
Edge of the world. When the target lies beyond the 5x5 built area, use built-boundary cells as fallback targets. Failed chunks (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:672-683) count as walls.

Interior shift after 30 s away (FrontRoomsLevelProfile.cs:29). Routes change on rebuild, but targets are revision-invariant, so the general heading persists and new routes commit at least 24 m away, unseen.

Aliasing. Title stream rooms and Office walls would read the world-periodic cell state, so they must be masked (10_synthesis.md:218). The 192 m rebase must shift the wave origin (10_synthesis.md:144).
Pre-existing stutter flicker (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1188-1196) may already exceed 3 Hz in bursts. The ink must not amplify it: the low-passed gate keeps stutter cells at G <= 0.1.

Glyph clipping on 0.6 m columns (less than one 0.75 m repeat) and between door trims. Accept it: the glyph still reads as part of its cell. Or let the visual chat fade glyphs where a face is narrower than 0.75 m.
narrative_slots: What the phosphor underprint is in the fiction, and who or what printed it. It must be period-plausible copper-activated zinc sulfide (10_synthesis.md:190) and must exist only on wallpaper, not Office drywall.
Why it knows the way to NEW thresholds and never leads back. Is it a previous wanderer's trail, the building's own memory, or a printing-run defect that 'remembers' openings?
Why it reacts to the Relay. Pressure mode points to doors away from it, and the wave starts at it. Do the walls fear it, serve it, or record it?
Whether the ink helps or herds. Following it accelerates escalation; the fiction can frame it as both.

What the GROUND pattern depicts, and the final look of FLOW, HERE and STOP. Constraints: directional asymmetry for FLOW, strokes of at least 100 mm, distinguishable by shape not colour, sized to the 750 x 1125 mm repeat.
What the power sags are: building electrics, the Relay, or something else.
The first-reveal moment at the forced dead lamp past the start door: an optional one-line Flash text, used only if playtest needs it.
Whether and when the ink may lie. Recommended never before T4; Dark Souls-style unreliable messages as a late-run variant.
The Gilman sub-pattern link (The Yellow Wallpaper, 10_synthesis.md:238-240) as the narrative anchor, if wanted.
What dark clusters with blank ink mean in-world (no light to charge), so players read it as a rule, not a bug.
references: Left 4 Dead (Valve, 2008): painted arrows and graffiti pointing survivors toward safe rooms, plus the AI Director build-up/peak/relax pacing already used in 10_synthesis.md:159.
Mirror's Edge (DICE, 2008): Runner Vision. Route objects tinted red at decision points, can be switched off. A model for on-route-only highlighting and an assist toggle.
Dead Space (Visceral, 2008): the locator line. The GPS end of the spectrum the calm mode must avoid (cf. the simulated 3-cell trail matching perfect knowledge).
Ghost of Tsushima (Sucker Punch, 2020): the guiding wind. Diegetic direction with no HUD.
Dark Souls (FromSoftware, 2011): orange soapstone messages on surfaces, sometimes lies. Reference for the 'unreliable ink' late-run slot.
The Exit 8 (Kotake Create, 2023): signage plus a stable baseline with discrete anomalies. Stable lit modules, deliberate dark beats.
Appalachian Trail blazes: 2 x 6 in paint marks spaced so the next is visible from the last. The model for beacon-to-beacon spacing (~5-8 cells).
Kevin Lynch, The Image of the City (1960): paths, edges, districts (zones), nodes (junctions), landmarks (dead troffers).
Romedi Passini, Wayfinding in Architecture (1984): information is needed at decision points, hence end-wall glyphs at T-junctions.

Aircraft floor-proximity escape path marking (FAA rules after the 1983 Air Canada 797 fire), later photoluminescent strips; zinc-sulfide glow-in-the-dark exit signage. Real-world precedent for 'charged ink shows the way when power fails'.
Charlotte Perkins Gilman, The Yellow Wallpaper (1892): the sub-pattern seen only in certain light (10_synthesis.md:238-240).
Haunted Mansion (1969) lightning portraits; Rensink, O'Regan & Clark change blindness (10_synthesis.md:141). The basis for masked commits.

design.name: AFTERGLOW WAKE: the glow ink as the Relay's ledger (threat intel)
design.pitch: The hidden ZnS:Cu ink records the Relay. It never records the player and never shows where the Relay is now. In any cell whose lamp is dead or dying, the wallpaper shows four things: where the Relay walked (a trail that fades with age and gets brighter toward the way it went), where it stopped to listen, where it is heading because it heard you, and which doors it has broken. A single green wave announces each time it re-enters the maze near you. Lit cells show nothing, so every reading costs one to three seconds of standing in the dark, and every reading is already a few seconds old. As tiers rise the ink stays honest about what happened, but it gets stale, then muddled, and at the top tier it can lie, with a tell. Status: proposal only, nothing is implemented. Every number is a starting point for playtest.
design.player_fantasy: I am the tracker, not the tracked. I step under a dead troffer and let my eyes adjust, and the paper tells me what happened. It came through here about half a minute ago, heading left. It stopped at that junction to listen. I sprinted two corridors back, and now that corridor is breathing green: it heard me and it is going there. The far door is scarred, so it will not shut any more. I never know where it is now. I know where it was, and I bet my route on that. Sometimes the answer is a dark shape stepping in front of the glowing wall.
rules: R1 WHERE INK EXISTS: Ink is on Level 0 wallpaper only. That means L0_Wallpaper, L0_Wallpaper_Shift and Exit_Wallpaper, plus the wallpapered 0.6/0.9 m columns (LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC.md:57-59). Office walls are drywall (LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC.md:58). Office is officeShare 0.3 of Standard zones (FrontRoomsMap.cs:117, 294), so 16.5% of zones are ink-blind by design. Doors, trim, glass, floors and ceilings never carry ink.

R2 LIGHT HIDES, DARK REVEALS: per-cell glow = G x D x adapt. D (darkness) is a slewed (1 - L_own)^2 x (1 - 0.5 x mean L of the 4 neighbours). L must be the temperament output Fixture.level (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1168, 1184-1216), not light.enabled. light.enabled is switched off by the 16 m budget (:1172-1175), so using it would make every far cell glow. A steady cell (level .98, :1214) never shows ink.

R3 LAMPS CHARGE, DARK DRAINS, LAMPS NEVER WRITE: the charge C rises toward L_eff = 0.65 x L_own + 0.35 x mean(L of the 4 neighbours) with tau 2 s, and decays with tau 25 s. The neighbour term exists because troffer spill (range 10 m, :1115) lights a dead cell's walls. Charged ink with no mark shows only the BASELINE speckle, about 4% of paper area. That is the 'clean' reading, and it is what makes a missing mark mean something.

R4 ONLY THE RELAY WRITES MARKS: writing tops the cell's energy up (wake 0.9, breach floor 0.6). Marks therefore show even in dead cells (mode 3 is lit only .06-.18 s every 8-28 s, :1204-1210, so it barely self-charges). A wake in a dead cell reads about 3x brighter than that cell's baseline.

R5 WAKE: when the Relay's body leaves a cell (CellOf(Position) changes, FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:167-168), that cell gets a pending WAKE stamped with its passage time. Freshness F = exp(-age / tau_wake), with age measured from the passage, so a late commit already looks old. The extent threshold on the print's B growth field is lerp(0.85, 0.55, F), and brightness is 0.9 x sqrt(F). Read along a corridor, a trail gets brighter toward the way the Relay went.

R6 COMMIT GATE (WAKE, KNOT, BREACH): a mark appears only when the Relay is at least 'lag' cells away (T1: 2 cells = 6 m) AND either (a) the cell has been unseen for at least 0.5 s, or (b) the cell's lamp falls through L = 0.15 in this frame. (b) is the flicker-masked change from synthesis lines 139-142, and the same falling edge the sound chat already turns into its 'Tick' event (FrontRoomsSoundDirector.cs:321-325). Pending marks older than 30 s are dropped. Wander runs at 2.6 x 0.8 = 2.08 m/s (FrontRoomsHunter.cs:23, FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:52), so the trail head is always at least 6 m and about 3 s behind the Relay.

R7 KNOT: a cell where the Relay stood still for at least 1.5 s gets a mark one size larger (threshold 0.45) and no pulse. In practice these are its Listen stops (listenSeconds 2, FrontRoomsHunter.cs:19), which come every 6-14 cells along a wander trail (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:51). Search glances (1.1 s, :55) are too short to leave knots. A knot reads as 'it stopped here, listened and chose a new way'.

R8 EAR: when Noise() is accepted, the source cell and its open (no-door) neighbours bloom with a breathing mark (threshold 0.40, 0.25 Hz +/-25%). Noise() accepts when the source is inside radius x hearing and the Relay is not in Chase or BreakDoor (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:279-286); ListenPoint then takes the source (:123, 283). EAR is the ONLY mark allowed to appear in view: it is the deliberate 'it heard you' beat, a 1.5 s smooth ramp. It holds while ListenPoint still equals that source, then decays with tau 4 s. At most one bloom per 4 s, because sprint steps call Noise every 0.3 s (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:861-865).

R9 BREACH: when the Relay breaks a door (BreakDoor raises DoorBroken, FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1056-1065), both cells of that edge get a permanent mark (threshold 0.30, glow floor 0.6), committed under R6. Broken doors are rebuilt broken (:939) and borders never shift (MAP_GENERATION.md:97), so breaches are the ink's only permanent record. A breach means 'this door will not shut' (Use ignores broken doors, :1609).

R10 OMEN: every Relay arrival is delayed 3.3-5.5 s and announced by one green wave. This covers Arrive at the first release and at the leash (more than 30 cells away and 45 s quiet), FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:182-187, 390-418; the off-map emergency relay is exempt. The wave runs from the arrival cell along passable edges at 8 m/s (0.375 s per cell, synthesis line 167), starts 2 cells out, and stops 3 cells short of the player. Arrival is 9-15 cells away (:49). Each dark cell blooms once (rise 0.6 s, decay tau 2 s). Omens are at least 120 s apart (synthesis line 166).

R11 NEVER WHERE IT IS NOW: no WAKE or KNOT is ever visible within 'lag' cells of the Relay. EAR marks the player's own noise (where it is heading, never where it stands). OMEN skips the arrival cell and its neighbours. Ink is per cell, and each wall face reads only the cell it faces (positionWS + normalWS x 0.5, synthesis line 131), so ink never shows through walls.

R12 READING COSTS EXPOSURE: a global adaptation value A rises (tau 1.2 s) while the player's own cell is dark (L_eff < 0.3) and falls fast (tau 0.25 s) in light. Glow is multiplied by (0.35 + 0.65 x A). From a lit corridor you can see THAT a dark cell is marked; reading age, knots or the hollow tell means standing in the dark for about 1.5-3 s. Darkness never hides the player: the Relay's sight is a 12 m occlusion ray with no light term (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:926-952).

R13 THE HUD STOPS GIVING IT AWAY: today's threat HUD prints 'RELAY nn M' every frame (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:1539-1544), and that perfect intel makes the ink pointless. When the ink ships, remove the distance line and show state text only for Chase and BreakDoor, which the player perceives anyway. The full readout becomes an accessibility assist.

R14 THE 3 m RULE HOLDS: lit, every module is identical, because marks change only emission and the visible R/G print never encodes the Relay. Drop or randomise the synthesis's 'Relay wake reprint' of the visible layer (synthesis line 145). Dark and unmarked, every module shows the same baseline speckle. Marks are the deliberate beats.

R15 PHOTOSAFE BY CONSTRUCTION: no glow modulation above 0.5 Hz. Every bloom is a single ramp. D slews (rise 0.4 s, fall 0.08 s), so the mode-1 stutter's hard on/off (PerlinNoise(t x 23) > .45 gives .95 or .05, FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1196) becomes one swell instead of an antiphase strobe. The omen visits each cell once.
design.placement_and_generation:
Ink is not placed. It is a property of every Level 0 wall face. Intel density = Relay traffic x dark cells x what is in view.

Dark cells come from the existing temperament roll, a hash of seed + cell that does not depend on the revision, so it is stable across shifts (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1087, 1127-1128). T1 uses today's split of 62% steady / 20% stutter / 10% failing / 5% dead / 3% dim. That gives 18% persistently dark cells (failing + dead + dim), plus stutter windows: 20% of cells go dark for .15-.85 s every 5-20 s (:1191-1196).

Coverage at T1:
- Expect about 11.5 dark cells per 64-cell chunk; P(fewer than 4) is about 0.1%, so no placement guarantee is needed.
- The built window is 5 x 5 chunks (40 x 40 cells, buildRadius 2), which holds about 290 dark cells.
- With 10-20 cells inside a 20 m view, about 2-4 dark cells are readable at T1, rising to 3-6 at T5.

By zone (shares in MapSettings, FrontRoomsMap.cs:82-84, 117):
- **Standard Level 0 maze** (38.5% of zones; 82% walls, MAP_GENERATION.md:68). Long corridors make trails read as gradients. Corridor side walls are seen at grazing angles at range, so the far read lives on facing walls at T-junctions, dead ends and room back walls.
- **Low** (35%; 2.4 m; leaky 50/20/30). Short sightlines and many facing walls make this the best near-read zone (3-10 m).
- **Tall halls** (10%; 5.4 m walls). Lamps are x1.6 with range 12 (:1115-1119), so spill is high, D is low and ink is weak. The Relay cannot pass unbroken glass (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:462), so it only reaches a tall hall through inside edges or a window the player broke. Tall halls are 'bright, quiet ink' until you let it in.
- **Office** (16.5%). Blind: drywall carries no ink.

Authoring:
- Level Designer modules already set lamps per cell: Off drops the fixture, and Steady..Dim map to modes 0-4 (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1084-1085, 1129-1130; LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC §9). So a 'reading room' (a cluster of Dead lamps) is an authorable motif.
- Keep dark clusters to 4 cells or fewer so neighbour spill still charges the baseline.
- Tutorial override: one Dead lamp 4 cells (12 m) ahead of the start door, on the guaranteed open run (MAP_GENERATION.md:17), set through MapChunk.lamp (FrontRoomsMap.cs:180).

Dark share by tier:
- Shift the roll thresholds at chunk build only, never on a built chunk: T1 18%, T2 21%, T3 24%, T4 27%, T5 30%.
- For example, the steady cut moves .62 > .59 > .56 > .53 > .50, with the failing and dead bands widened.
- Keep the shift monotone, so a given cell only ever gets darker.

Storage:
- Marks live in a sparse dictionary keyed by GridCoord (cap 512), so they survive chunk drops.
- The shader reads a world-periodic 64 x 64 state texture (one texel per cell, cell & 63).
- The built window is 40 x 40 (56 x 56 at buildRadius 3), which is at most 64, so no two built cells share a texel.
- 64 x 3 m = 192 m = ModuleUnits.WorldPeriod (LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC.md:85).
- Start-area cells (InStartArea, FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:389), Office cells and unbuilt cells always write 'no ink'.
design.triggers_and_timing:
All numbers are playtest starting points. File paths: Assets/Scripts/FrontRoomsMap/FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs (World), FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs (Hunter), Assets/Scripts/FrontRooms3DGame.cs (Game).

1. **Lamp tick** (every frame, every built cell). L = Fixture.level (World:1168).
   - Charge: tau 2 s up, 25 s down.
   - Darkness slew: rise 0.4 s, fall 0.08 s.
   - Falling edge: L crossing 0.15 downward. Mode 1 stutters .15-.85 s every 5-20 s (World:1191-1196). Mode 2 drops to .05 whenever PerlinNoise(t x 1.4) > .72 (World:1199-1202). Mode 3 blinks .06-.18 s every 8-28 s (World:1204-1210).
2. **Relay leaves a cell** (the ledger polls CellOf(relay.Position), Hunter:116, 168). Write a pending WAKE with tPass = now.
   - Skip it when the step is more than 1 cell, or when the Relays counter went up (an Arrive teleport, Hunter:130, 390-418).
3. **Relay still for at least 1.5 s** (Moving false, Hunter:118). Write a KNOT on its cell. These are Listen stops of 2 s (FrontRoomsHunter.cs:19), every 6-14 cells (Hunter:51).
4. **Commit gate** for WAKE, KNOT and BREACH: the Relay is at least 'lag' cells away (T1: 2) AND (the cell has been unseen for at least 0.5 s OR its lamp has a falling edge this frame). A pending mark older than 30 s is dropped.
5. **Noise accepted** (ListenPoint takes a new value, Hunter:123, 283). EAR blooms at once with a 1.5 s ramp.
   - It holds while ListenPoint still equals that source (it is cleared on sight or on a relay), then decays with tau 4 s.
   - At most one bloom per 4 s.
   - Noise sources: sprint steps every 0.3 s at 26 m (Game:861-865), doors at 14 m (Game:785-790), glass at 40 m (Game:792-798). With hearing 1.4 (FrontRoomsHunter.cs:29-32; it is not serialized in the scene, so the default applies) these reach 36 / 20 / 56 m.
   - A door or window source sits on an edge, so both of that edge's cells bloom.
6. **DoorBroken** (World:63, 1064). A pending BREACH on both cells whose shared edge is a Door. The break lands 2.5 s after the Relay starts BreakDoor, with blows at 0.5/1.0/1.5/2.0/2.4 s (MAP_GENERATION.md:36).
7. **Arrival.** Release comes 3 s after the start door shuts (MAP_GENERATION.md:34); a leash relay comes when the Relay is more than 30 cells away and has had 45 s without contact (Hunter:182-187).
   - Pick the cell, then start the OMEN wave.
   - Wave depth = min(12, playerDepth - 3), where playerDepth is the player's breadth-first-search (BFS) distance from the arrival cell.
   - The Relay appears after 0.375 s x depth + 1 s, which comes to 3.3-5.5 s. Re-check that the cell is still unseen at that moment; if not, re-pick.
   - Not used for the off-map emergency relay.
   - At least 120 s between omens.
8. **Chunk shift** (World:612-616, after 30 s away, shiftAfterSeconds in FrontRoomsLevel0.asset). At T1-T2, clear that chunk's WAKE, KNOT and EAR marks. From T3, keep them (stale).
9. **Chase and BreakDoor.** Noise is ignored in these states (Hunter:281), so there is no EAR. Wakes still queue, but they only commit unseen, so a chased player never sees a trail form behind the Relay.
10. **Caught.** Freeze the ledger (synthesis line 169).
11. **Title stream and start rooms.** _FR_GlowMix stays 0 until the start door has shut for good (MAP_GENERATION.md:24).
design.teaching_curve:
No tutorial text is needed. The map stages five first meetings, then lets the system teach the details.

1. **0:00-0:20, 'ink exists'.** The first maze cells are Standard Level 0, and the way ahead is open for 150+ cells (MAP_GENERATION.md:17).
   - The map forces one Dead lamp 4 cells (12 m) ahead on that run, with steady neighbours.
   - The player walks under it and the baseline speckle appears; standing still sharpens it (adaptation).
   - There is no Relay information yet: it stays Dormant until 3 s after the start door shuts (MAP_GENERATION.md:34; Game:883-886).
2. **About 0:15-0:40, 'something came in'.** The release always has an omen at T1.
   - The arrival cell is 9-15 cells away, preferably behind the player (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:404).
   - The wave is paired with the Relay stinger. Green blooms rolling in from one direction are the first threat intel.
3. **By 3:00, 'it walked here'.** At T1, the first Wander (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:424-438) scores candidates x3 when their route crosses a dark cell 4-8 cells from the player that the player cannot see right now. The player meets a fresh trail whose gradient points away from them.
4. **First accepted sprint, 'it heard you'.** The calm hint already says it hears every step (Game:142).
   - EAR blooms around the player's own trail.
   - For the first two blooms at T1: if the source lamp is stutter or failing, force a 1.2 s dropout; otherwise bloom the nearest dark cell within 2 open steps.
   - The lesson: noise means it is coming here, so leave quietly.
5. **First breach, 'that door is dead'.** After its first door break, the player later meets the scar from the far side, in a dark cell.
6. **No staging needed after that.**
   - Knots teach 'it stops to listen'.
   - Brightness and extent teach age.
   - A trail that ends in an open corridor teaches 'it relayed, look behind you'.
   - At T3, the first wake running through a wall teaches staleness.
   - At T5, the first hollow mark teaches the lie.

Optional: one hint card in the existing flash slot (Game:1547), worded by the narrative chat. It shows the first time the player is adapted (A > 0.8) within 3 m of a fresh wake.

Pacing follows the synthesis event tier (lines 159-170):
- Subliminal print motion is always on.
- Marks are 'noticeable', and they only appear unseen or under lamp masking.
- Omens are events, at most one per 2 minutes.
design.escalation_over_run:
Tiers follow the DP08 proposal, which is NOT confirmed: a tier every 4 zones or 2 minutes, 5 tiers. The Relay's chase speed rises 4.2 > 5.4 m/s, hearing 1.0 > 1.6x (the code default is already 1.4), and door break time falls 2.5 > 1.3 s.

The ink's arc is HONEST > STALE > MUDDLED > LYING, while dark coverage grows. The player reads more and trusts less.

**T1, honest:**
- dark share 18%
- tau_wake 25 s (visible, F >= 0.1, for about 58 s)
- lag 2 cells
- EAR on the source cell plus its open neighbours
- omen 100%
- marks cleared on chunk shift
- no lit preference

**T2, honest and wider:**
- dark 21%
- tau 30 s (69 s visible)
- lag 2
- omen 100%
- cleared on shift

**T3, stale:**
- dark 24%
- tau 35 s (81 s visible)
- lag 3 (9 m)
- EAR on the source cell only
- omen 60%
- Marks survive chunk shifts, so some wakes now run through walls the maze grew since.
- Wander destinations weighted toward lit cells 30% of the time (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:424-438), so fewer wakes land where they can be read.

**T4, muddled:**
- dark 27%
- tau 40 s (92 s visible)
- lag 3
- omen 30%
- lit preference 50%
- 20% of wander legs first backtrack 3-6 cells along the Relay's own newest wake. Trails overlap and the gradient reads both ways.

**T5, lying:**
- dark 30%
- tau 45 s (104 s visible)
- lag 4 (12 m)
- omen 0%
- lit preference 60%
- backtrack 30%
- Each arrival writes one HOLLOW decoy trail, 4-8 cells long, in the player's forward half-plane, with a fake 10-20 s-old gradient pointing away. Arrive already prefers cells behind the player (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:404), so the decoy pushes the player back toward the real Relay.
- Tell: decoy marks are hollow rings with no core, readable when adapted at 6 m or less.
- Secondary tell, where a door is present: a real wander wake never crosses a shut, unbroken door, because Wander never routes through shut doors (:426, 463).

**Never escalates:**
- Breach marks are always true and always permanent.
- The darkness-only rule.
- The never-where-it-is-now rule.
- The adaptation cost.

Optional lever, not core: the Relay degrades lamps it passes under (2-5% per cell at T2-T5, needs new map logic, synthesis line 178), so its habitual routes darken over a run.

Gate decoys behind real trust: enable them only if T1-T4 playtests show players act on the ink (see metrics).
design.interaction_with_relay_and_escapes:
**Sprint** (5 s stamina, refills after 1 s, Game:148-151). Every sprint step is a 26 m noise (36 m at hearing 1.4).
- EAR blooms on your own trail, so a sprint now costs stamina, noise and a visible confession.
- The bloom tells you it heard you, and that the place you just left is where it will search: up to 3 spots, 1.1 s each, 15 s at most (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:54-55).

**Breaking line of sight.** LoseTrack sends the Relay to lastSeen, or through the door you just used (:294-302). That is not a Noise, so no EAR is written, and search sweep cells are never marked. The search after a chase stays a blind guess. The ink only pays off later, when you cross its fresh wake and choose a route.

**Shutting a door** (a 14 m noise, 20 m at hearing 1.4). EAR blooms at the door.
- If the Relay comes and breaks it (5 blows, 2.5 s), both sides get a permanent BREACH.
- Read from the far side in the dark, a breach says 'this door will not shut' (Use ignores broken doors, FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1609).
- Over a run the ink becomes a map of dead doors. That matters most at T4-T5, when door break time falls toward 1.3 s and live doors are scarce. Doors exist only on Low/Standard borders (LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC.md:48), so breaches also mark the zone borders it has crossed.

**Breaking a window** (40 m noise, 56 m at hearing 1.4, the loudest in the game).
- EAR blooms at the window. The Relay can follow through afterwards: glass blocks it only while unbroken (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:462; FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1045-1046).
- Breaks the player makes get no breach.
- Tall halls start showing wakes only after you let it in.

**Wander.** It keeps to shut doors (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:426, 463), so an honest wander wake never crosses a shut, unbroken door. This is the secondary tell for T5 decoys.

**Arrivals.** The omen points at where it re-entered, usually behind you. It thins from T3 and is gone at T5. A trail that ends abruptly in an open corridor means it relayed. That is honest, but stale.

**Chase.** The ink deliberately adds nothing during a chase: no EAR (Noise is ignored in Chase, :281), plus the commit lag and the unseen gate. Chases are decided by the existing verbs (sprint 5.5 vs chase 4.2 m/s, LOS, doors, glass). The ink serves the long stretches between chases: route choice, timing and when to make noise.

**Sight and darkness.** Reading never hides you: sight is a 12 m, 360-degree occlusion ray (:926-952), and catch is under 0.7 m with sight. The Relay's dark body (#2B2928, Game:256) sinks into a dead cell, but it silhouettes against glowing paper. That is a free scare beat, not a stealth rule.

**Shadowing.** Walking at 3.2 m/s beats wander at 2.08 m/s. But wake cells you can see never commit, and its sight reaches 12 m in every direction, so following too close gets you seen.
design.interaction_with_moving_print:
**One gate, two systems.** The ledger's visibility set and the lamp falling edges are the same 'unseen or lamp-masked' gate that the print uses for discrete jumps (synthesis lines 135-142). The map chat computes it once per frame, and both consumers read it. A lamp dropout can reveal a print slip and a new mark in the same moment. That is intended, after the Haunted Mansion lightning portraits.

**Same fetch.** The glow lives in the print's B channel, so it rides the existing array fetch (synthesis lines 64-90).
- When a cell's print jumps while unseen, the glyph shape changes with the slice.
- The mark is per cell (extent threshold, energy, tempo) and carries over the jump.
- So meaning must live in extent, brightness and tempo, never in the exact glyph. The glyph shape is the narrative layer, read up close.

**The visible layer must not encode the Relay.** Drop the synthesis's 'Relay wake: cells the Relay walked through get reprinted' (line 145), or reprint random cells instead. Otherwise players read the trail in the light and skip the dark-cost that balances this design.

**Slow crawl beats** (the later _FR_PrintWarp, a UV-only warp). The glyph crawls with the print while marks stay put per cell. This is fine as a scripted beat. Never run a crawl and an omen within the same 30 s.

**Chase wave** (visible print, Relay > Chase, about 8 m/s, synthesis line 167). It does not touch the glow. It counts in the same event budget as omens: at most one event per 2-4 minutes, then 30-45 s of subliminal-only (synthesis 165-168).

**Reduce wall motion.** The print freezes. The ink still records, because it is information, not motion, but the omen has no travel and EAR does not breathe.

**Lighting independence.** The glow is emission added after lighting. Neither print nor glow ever writes normal, smoothness or cavity (synthesis section 3). The paper's cavity and fibre mask the emission, so it reads as ink soaked into paper, not as a projection.

**Frame 0 parity and P0** (synthesis section 9) are unaffected: with _FR_GlowMix = 0 the wall is byte-identical to the print-only path.
design.readability_and_accessibility:
**Distance budget.**
- The camera's vertical FOV is 76 degrees (Game:227), which gives about 691 px per radian at 1080p.
- A 0.25 m feature spans 8.6 px at 20 m and 14 px at 12 m.
- Exp2 fog at density 0.014 (FrontRoomsLook.cs:19, 32) keeps 92.5% of the glow at 20 m. Fog will not hide the ink, and it will not hide a bad commit either.

**Two-scale glyph contract for the B channel.** Author it as a nested 'growth field': the brightest core is the smallest mark, and outer rings add extent.
- FAR read (6-20 m) is how much of the wall is green and how bright. Corridor side walls at 20 m are seen at about 4 degrees, so horizontal detail shrinks x0.075 and vanishes. Far-read structure must therefore be vertical and at least 0.25 m tall.
- Facing walls at junctions, dead ends and room ends carry the far read.
- NEAR read (1-6 m, adapted) is the glyph's shape, knots and the hollow tell.

**Extent bands** (threshold on B):

| Mark | Threshold | Area |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline | .85 | about 4% |
| Wake, fresh to old | .55 to .85 | 15-20% when fresh |
| Knot | .45 | about 30% |
| Ear | .40 | about 30% |
| Omen | .40 | about 30% |
| Breach | .30 | about 45% |

**Luminance, not hue.**
- Adapted glow peaks at about 12% of the same wall's fully lit luminance; unadapted, it shows at 35% of that.
- Target at least 3:1 against the adapted dark paper.
- Ink only exists on dark paper, so protan and deutan players read it by luminance despite green/yellow confusion.
- Colour: ZnS:Cu, about 525 nm green.

**Photosensitivity.**
- No glow modulation above 0.5 Hz; EAR breathes at 0.25 Hz +/-25%.
- Each bloom is a single ramp, and each omen visits a cell once.
- The darkness slew turns lamp stutter into one swell.
- Gate: at most 3 flashes/s, and no reversal above 3 Hz over more than 25% of the screen, measured with fixtures running (synthesis line 228).
- Also measure the existing mode-1 stutter, whose hard on/off at PerlinNoise(t x 23) (World:1196) is a flicker risk in its own right.

**Reduce wall motion** (required, synthesis 197-200): print frozen; omen cells bloom together at 50% for 3 s with no travel; EAR static; every ramp at least 1.5 s.

**High-visibility ink** (assist): adaptation floor 0.7, extent thresholds -0.10, glow x1.5.

**Threat readout** (assist, Off by default at ship): Off / State / State + distance. Today's HUD (Game:1539-1544) moves behind this option.

**Deaf and hard-of-hearing players.** EAR and OMEN are visual first; their sounds are reinforcement only.

**Low-vision players** can combine high-visibility ink with the readout assist.

**Screen budget.** Green covers at most 3% of screen pixels on average (p95 at most 8%), so Level 0 stays yellow.
design.implementation_data_flow:
Per frame, after relay.Tick (Game:885-886):

1. **Lamps.** TickFixtures already computes every built fixture's level (World:1164-1168).
   - Add a GridCoord to the private Fixture (World:85-101), and write L[cell] into the ledger.
   - A cell with no fixture (ModuleLamp.Off, World:1085) reads L = 0.
2. **Visibility** (map chat). Run a BFS from the camera's cell over see-through edges.
   - See-through: Open, Arch (MAP_GENERATION.md:59; treat as see-through to stay conservative), an open or broken door, and a window whether broken or not (Cache.Edge / PassageBetween, World:1030-1050).
   - Search out to the far plane: SightDistance is 46 m, about 15 cells (World:56).
   - Test each cell's AABB with GeometryUtility.TestPlanesAABB, with a 10% margin.
   - The camera cell and its 8 neighbours always count as seen.
   - Set lastSeen[cell] = now. The print-jump logic reads the same set.
3. **Relay poll** (existing public API, Hunter:114-130). No hunter change is needed for WAKE, KNOT or EAR.
   - Cell change: pending WAKE.
   - Moving false for at least 1.5 s: KNOT.
   - New ListenPoint: EAR.
   - New Arriving(cell, seconds) event: OMEN. Precompute wave arrival times by BFS from the arrival cell.
   - World DoorBroken(position) (World:1064): BREACH on the two cells around that position whose shared edge is a Door.
4. **Per built cell** (40 x 40 or fewer).
   - L_eff = .65 L + .35 mean(L of 4 neighbours).
   - C moves toward L_eff (tau 2 s up, 25 s down).
   - D target = (1 - L)^2 x (1 - .5 x mean L4), slewed.
   - Decay F.
   - Commit pending marks through the gate.
   - Energy E = max(C, mark energy), times the EAR breathing or OMEN envelope.
   - Write R = L, G = E x D, B = extent threshold (1 = no ink: Office, start area, unbuilt), A bit 7 = hollow (bits 0-3 left for the print's per-cell slice offset).
   - Output a Color32[4096] at index (x & 63) + 64 x (y & 63).
5. **Adaptation A** (one float): target 1 when the player's cell has L_eff < .3, with tau 1.2 s up and .25 s down.
6. **Upload** (visual chat's driver).
   - Copy into a 64 x 64 RGBA32 linear Texture2D (point filter, Repeat, no mips) with SetPixelData + Apply(false): 16 KB.
   - Set the globals _FR_CellState, _FR_GlowAdapt, _FR_GlowMix and _FR_GlowColor. These stay outside Properties and UnityPerMaterial, per synthesis line 95.
7. **Shader** (wallpaper pixels only, under _FR_PRINT ForwardLit):
   ```hlsl
   int2 c = (int2)floor((positionWS.xz + normalWS.xz * 0.5) / 3.0) & 63;
   half4 s = LOAD_TEXTURE2D(_FR_CellState, c);
   half w = max(fwidth(ink.b), 0.02);
   half m = smoothstep(s.b - w, s.b + w, ink.b);
   if (s.a > 0.5) m -= smoothstep(s.b + .18 - w, s.b + .18 + w, ink.b);   // hollow
   emission += _FR_GlowColor * m * s.g * (0.35 + 0.65 * _FR_GlowAdapt) * _FR_GlowMix * cavity;
   ```
   The cell index assumes the map root sits on a 192 m multiple (MAP_GENERATION.md:16); otherwise pass _FR_MapRoot.
8. **Events out for sound:** EarBloom(pos), Omen(origin, seconds) and StateChanged(Arriving).

State:
- Dense arrays of 4096 entries for L, C, D and lastSeen.
- Dictionary<GridCoord, Mark{kind, tPass, pendingSince, committed}>, capped at 512; evict the oldest non-breach mark.
- HashSet<long> of breach edges, mirroring brokenDoors (World:205).
- Clock: a wrapped double (synthesis line 147).
- No UnityEngine.Random. Decoy and backtrack choices are hashed from (seed, Relays), so the same seed and inputs give an identical ledger timeline (P3 gate, synthesis line 229).
- On chunk build, initialise C to its steady-state L_eff.

Budget: CPU at most 0.3 ms (the cell update is about 0.02 ms; BFS and frustum about 0.1 ms), a 16 KB upload, 16 KB of memory, and GPU about 1 point load + 12 ALU per wallpaper pixel (at most +0.2 ms).
