NARRATIVE: fill the slots listed in narrative_slots. Above all, a reason the Relay can write ink without light while lamps can only charge it, and glyph content that survives being read as 'how much' at 20 m.
playtest_metrics: Ink sightings per minute by tier. A sighting is a marked cell with G x adapt > 0.15 inside the view set. Target: T1 2-4/min, T5 1-3/min.
First wake seen by 3:00: at least 70% of runs.
Read dwell: median time stationary (under 0.5 m/s) in a dark cell with a mark in view. Target 1-3 s. Dwells over 6 s in more than 10% of reads mean camping.
Caught within 10 s after a read dwell: 5-15%. Reading should be risky, not a death trap.
Survival time with ink on vs off, with the HUD distance off in both arms: +10-25% at T1-T2, at most +10% at T4-T5 (the hunt is not trivialised).
Distance to the Relay when it first enters view: +2-4 m with ink. More than +8 m means the ink is too strong.
EAR response: share of blooms followed by the player leaving the bloom cells within 8 s without sprinting. At least 60% by the second exposure.
Wake choice at junctions (from path telemetry): follow vs avoid should both happen, 35-65% each, at T1-T2. Over 80% avoid means the signal is solved and needs more ambiguity.
Omen response: the player turns toward the omen origin within 3 s at least 50% of the time; arrivals that catch the player from behind should fall vs. the no-omen baseline.
T5 hollow decoys: 30-50% followed on first exposure, under 20% by the third.
Comprehension, asked after one run with no text: 'what does the green mean?' At least 70% answer 'where it has been' or 'a trail'; at least 40% mention 'it heard me'.

Technical: 0 WAKE/KNOT/BREACH commits while flagged seen; identical ledger timeline for the same seed and inputs; ledger CPU at most 0.3 ms; GPU at most +0.2 ms; autopilot seeds 2554 and 20388 within the synthesis perf budget (average fps -1, p99 +1.5 ms; synthesis line 230).
Green screen coverage: mean at most 3%, p95 at most 8%.
Flash test: pass with glow, print and fixtures combined (at most 3 flashes/s; no reversal above 3 Hz over more than 25% of the screen).
With and without decoys at T5: if trust in T1-T4 ink falls (follow/avoid decisions drop toward chance), ship T5 without decoys.
failure_modes_and_exploits: HUD redundancy: while 'RELAY nn M' stays on screen (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:1544), players ignore the ink. Fix: R13. The distance readout moves behind an assist.

Locating it by following the trail: walking (3.2 m/s) is faster than wandering (2.08 m/s), so a player can catch up. Mitigations: the trail head lags 2-4 cells; it shows only in dark cells; cells the player can see never commit; and its 12 m, 360-degree sight catches close shadowers. Treat skilled shadowing beyond 12 m as legitimate play, and watch chase rates.

Noise sonar: one sprint tap in a dark cell makes EAR bloom, which proves 'it's within 36 m'. The cost is that it now hunts you. If telemetry shows deliberate taps (sprints under 0.5 s), delay the EAR bloom 2-4 s from T3 on, so the answer arrives when it is already coming.

Dark camping: a player adapts in a dead pocket and waits for omens and trails. Mitigations: omens thin out with tier; nothing in the ledger rewards staying; reading never hides the player from the Relay.

'No marks means safe': lit preference (T3+), Office blindness and the 18-30% dark coverage make absence weak evidence. The baseline speckle still keeps 'clean ink' readable in the cells that are dark.

Visible pop from visibility errors (glass, arch openings, frustum edges, the 46 m far plane where fog still shows about 66%). Mitigations: treat glass and arches as see-through; add a 10% frustum margin; run the BFS to the far plane; automate the 0-commits-while-seen test.
Antiphase strobe: an un-slewed (1 - L) gate would flash the ink at the mode-1 stutter's Perlin x23 rate (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1196). Mitigations: the R15 slew, plus the combined flash test.
Teleport line: Arrive moves the Relay up to 15 cells in one frame. Detect it from the Relays counter or a step longer than 1 cell, and never connect a wake across it.
Ear spam: sprint steps call Noise every 0.3 s, so EAR is coalesced to one bloom per 4 s; otherwise the ledger churns and the corridor strobes.
Stale marks read as a bug ('the trail goes through a wall'): only allowed from T3, after players have learned honest wakes. The narrative chat frames the shifting maze.
Trust collapse from decoys: decoys only at T5, with a consistent near-read tell (hollow) and a secondary door tell. Cut decoys if metric 15 fails.

Aliased reads: stream rooms and start area (synthesis line 217), Office drywall, and unbuilt cells write B = 1. The 64 x 64 periodic texture never sees more than the 40 x 40 (or 56 x 56) built window.
Too much green: Level 0 must stay yellow. Extent caps and the coverage budget enforce this; if over budget, raise thresholds rather than dim the glow.
Tall halls unreadable: x1.6 lamps with range 12 flood the walls with spill. Either accept them as 'bright, quiet' zones or lower the spill weight there after lookdev.
Determinism and replay drift: the ledger never uses UnityEngine.Random or _Time; choices are hashed from (seed, Relays), so autopilot runs and the P3 gate stay reproducible.
Omen seen at the arrival cell: the wave skips depth 0-1, and the arrival re-checks visibility before the Relay appears, re-picking if the cell is now in view.
narrative_slots: What the ink is in the world: who printed a hidden ZnS:Cu layer into a 1990 wallpaper run, and why.
Why the Relay writes the ink without light while lamps can only charge it. The mechanic needs four things: the Relay writes; lamps charge but never write; marks fade; breaches are permanent.

Glyph content for the B channel as a nested growth field: core (baseline and wake), ring (knot, ear, omen), full (breach). What the glyph 'says' up close, given that at range it only reads as 'how much'.
What the breathing EAR mark is doing (the ink listening, or answering?), and why it is the only mark that appears while you watch.
What the omen wave is: the paper feeling it arrive, the building reacting, or something else.
The T5 lie: who writes hollow trails, and why a lie is hollow (for example, it can copy the outline of its own trail but not its weight). Optional: the secondary 'never through a shut door' tell.
In-world names for wake, knot, ear, breach and omen, for the optional hint card and for any Caught-screen stat (for example, marks read or doors scarred).
The one-line hint card shown the first time the player reads a fresh wake while adapted.
Whether the player character knows about the ink, and how that fits the Level 0 / Gilman sub-pattern anchor.
references: Dead by Daylight (Behaviour, 2016): survivors leave fading scratch marks that the killer reads. A decaying trail as partial, stale intel, here with the roles reversed.
Phasmophobia (Kinetic Games, 2020): UV-revealed fingerprints and footprints that fade. Reading needs a light condition and time.
Alien: Isolation (Creative Assembly, 2014): the motion tracker gives partial, imprecise intel that costs attention and exposure, without trivialising the alien.
Hunt: Showdown (Crytek, 2019) Dark Sight: a reveal you can only use while exposed.
Thief: The Dark Project (1998) light gem / Splinter Cell light meter: the light/dark economy, inverted here. Darkness reveals information and never hides you.
Left 4 Dead AI Director (Valve, 2008): Build-Up / Peak / Relax pacing, already adopted in synthesis section 5 for the event tier.
The Exit 8 (Kotake Create, 2023): a stable baseline against which a deliberate anomaly reads. The basis of the 3 m rule.
Disney Haunted Mansion lightning portraits (1969) and Rensink, O'Regan & Clark (1997) change blindness: commit changes on light transients.
Charlotte Perkins Gilman, The Yellow Wallpaper (1892): a sub-pattern that shows only in certain light (synthesis section 8).
Copper-activated zinc sulfide glow paint: period-correct before 1993. Strontium aluminate (1993-94) sits at the edge of the era lock (synthesis section 6.1).
WCAG 2.x SC 2.3.1 Three Flashes and the Harding flash and pattern test: the photosensitivity gate.

design.name: Afterglow Ledger: light is the price of a hint
design.pitch: Every troffer acts as both a battery and a blindfold. A lit wall soaks light into the hidden copper-activated zinc sulfide print but shows nothing. When the wall goes dark it pays that light back as a faint green sign. The sign is legible for about 7–10 s and fades out over about 30–37 s. The signs give level-design facts the player can act on: WAY points along the shortest walk to the nearest door or window into a zone not yet visited, and SHUT marks a dead-end pocket where you can be cornered. Dark is where you are most exposed, for four reasons. The Relay's 12 m sight ray does not care about light, but your sight of it does. It prefers to wander where lamps are dead. Your sprint carries further where no ballast hum covers it. Standing still to read costs time. You can buy a reading spot by pulling the tube out of a troffer you can reach. This is a 1.2 s hold. It is loud, and permanent for the run, and it adds to the dark the Relay is drawn to. Lamps only get worse as tiers rise. The late run therefore gives short bursts of fresh, readable signs in a darker and more hunted maze. The ink's own rules never change, so what the player learns early stays true.
design.player_fantasy: "I read the walls by the light that just died." You are a scavenger of failing light. You stand at the edge of a lit cell and watch a dying ballast gasp, catching the green ladder on the wall in its dropouts. You decide whether a clue is worth killing a lamp over, knowing the noise will bring something that never needed the light. You learn to tell fresh glow, which is bright and still worth reading, from starved glow, which is faint and says nothing. You learn that a glowing corridor is also the best place to see the Relay's pale silhouette coming.
rules: R1 CHARGE (ink remembers light). Each Level 0 wallpaper cell keeps a charge C in 0..1. When the cell's effective light E is above C, C rises toward E with tau 3 s. Otherwise C decays hyperbolically: dC/dt = -C^2/5 s, so C(t) = C0/(1 + C0*t/5 s). This is second-order recombination, the real shape of ZnS:Cu afterglow. A cell that was never lit holds no charge and can never glow. All numbers here are playtest starting points.

R2 EFFECTIVE LIGHT. E = own lamp's LOGICAL level plus spill from each neighbour's logical level, clamped to 0..1. Spill weights: x0.08 through Open, x0.05 through Arch, x0.04 through an open or broken Door, x0.06 through a Window (glass or broken), 0 through Wall or a shut door. The logical level is Fixture.level from the temperament curves (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1184-1216). It is NOT the distance-faded light.intensity (:1172-1175, lightRadius 16 m) and NOT multiplied by the start-area hold (:1171). Otherwise every wall beyond 16 m, and the held lamps by the start door, would glow.

R3 GATE (invisible while lit). G = smoothstep(0.30, 0.10, E) x ramp. The ramp starts after E has stayed below 0.22 for 0.25 s and reaches 1 after another 0.5 s. When light returns the glow washes out over 0.15 s. Visibility V = C x G. Thresholds: V >= 0.33 is legible (the strip code reads); V >= 0.12 is a beacon (a green patch visible to about 20 m); V < 0.05 is off.

R4 WHAT EACH TEMPERAMENT GIVES (follows from R1-R3 and the code). Steady (.98, FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1213-1214): C about 1, V = 0, a full battery. Stutter (5-20 s gaps, 0.15-0.85 s Perlin bursts, :1189-1197): no dark window lasts 0.25 s, so it never shows. Failing ballast (0.25-0.70 at 0.49 Hz with Perlin dropouts to 0.0125-0.035, :1198-1202): C about 0.55-0.6, and V reaches about 0.35 in a corridor dropout of 0.75 s or more, so it reads in gasps. Dead with blinks (0.8 for 0.06-0.18 s every 8-28 s, :1203-1210): starved, about a 0.12 faint glow in corridors (spill-charged) and nothing in sealed pockets. Dim (0.42, :1211-1212): E is too high, so it never shows.

R5 FRESH DARK IS THE PRIZE. Killing a steady lamp (by pull, tier death or beat) leaves C = 1. In a corridor with 2 lit open neighbours (E about 0.16, G about 0.80) the sign is legible for about 7 s and stays a beacon for about 28 s. It then settles to a permanent faint starved glow of about 0.13. In a sealed pocket (E under 0.08, G = 1) it is legible for about 10 s and visible for about 37 s, then goes black.

R6 SIGN GRAMMAR. The level-design data is carried by WHICH of the 4 wallpaper rolls (0.75 m each, 4 per 3 m cell, every cell line a roll seam: LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC.md §2, 10_synthesis.md:128) glow. It is never carried by the glyph shape, which narrative owns. WAY: brightness 0.25/0.5/0.75/1.0 rising toward the first step of the shortest walk to the target. It shows on wall faces that run along that step; faces across it show a flat 0.35. SHUT: only the outer rolls 0 and 3 glow (a bracket). BLANK: a flat 0.5. P2 option RING: only the inner rolls 1 and 2 glow. Priority is SHUT > WAY > BLANK. Roll index is computed from world position (floor(worldAlong/0.75) & 3), not from the possibly mirrored uv, so the ramp points the same world way from both sides of a corridor.

R7 WAY TARGET. Run a multi-source shortest walk over built cells. Passable edges: Open, Arch, any Door except a Relay-broken one, and broken Windows. Sources are cells beside a Door edge into a zone not in zonesVisited (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:162, :873-876), at cost 0, and beside a Window edge into an unvisited zone, at cost +6 cells. If no unvisited target exists, use any exit. If none is within 24 cells, or the search reaches unbuilt cells first, the sign is BLANK. Doors and windows exist only where ceiling heights differ (FrontRoomsMap.cs:348-356), so WAY is a 'way onward' compass that also points at the two escape verbs.

R8 SHUT TARGET. Find the bridges (Tarjan) of the passable built-cell graph, with Doors and Windows counted as passable. A cell is SHUT if it lies on the side of a bridge that has 10 cells or fewer, no Door or Window to another zone, and no edge to an unbuilt cell. A maze carved as a spanning tree (MAP_GENERATION.md:65) gives many such stubs.

R9 SIGNS NEVER CHANGE WHILE SEEN. A new sign code is staged, then committed only after the cell has been unseen for 2 s or more. This uses the same camera BFS-plus-frustum visible set as the print's change-only-when-unseen rule (10_synthesis.md:135-138). Glow brightness (V) may change in view because it is physics; the code (what the sign says) may not.

R10 PULL THE TUBE (new verb, the deliberate darkness). Hold E for 1.2 s aimed at a lit troffer lens within the existing interaction Reach of 2.4 m from the eye (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:150, eye 1.62). That reaches Low (2.4 m) and Standard (2.9 m) ceilings but not Tall: a 5.38 m lens is 3.76 m above the eye. The lamp becomes Dead with no blinks for the rest of the run, persisted per cell like brokenWindows (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:203), so it survives chunk shifts. Noise through relay.Noise: Low 8 m (twisting the tube out), Standard 16 m (a jump strike, the lens clatters). The x1.4 hearing makes these about 11 m and 22 m (FrontRoomsHunter.cs:30-31). A pull within 30 s of your previous pull adds +50% noise radius, stacking.

R11 DARKNESS IS NOT COVER. The Relay's Sees() is a 12 m ray with no light term (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:926-931). Darkness only hides the Relay from you. A glowing wall behind it backlights its pale silhouette.

R12 DARK COSTS (new, map logic). (a) Wander targets are picked with weight 1 + k*D, where D = 1 - E (10 s mean) and k = 1.0 + 0.5 x tier; today the pick is uniform (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:424-438). (b) Sprint noise is x1.25 while the player's own lamp level is below 0.2. Nothing covers it, because fixture hum is already driven by lamp intensity (AUDIO_CONTRACT.md:41). (c) From tier 3, walking in such a cell makes a 4 m noise per step.

R13 LAMPS ONLY GET WORSE. A cell's temperament is the band of one fixed per-cell u, the first xorshift draw from Hash(seed, x, y, 211) (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1087, :1127-1128), against cut points that depend on zone and tier. Cuts only move down, so a lamp can only degrade. A change is applied only to a cell that is unseen, except the deliberate beats in the triggers.
R14 THE INK'S PHYSICS IS CONSTANT. tau 3 s, t0 5 s, the gate thresholds and the grammar never change with tier. Only the lamps, the Relay and the noise escalate. Office (drywall) walls carry no ink.
design.placement_and_generation:
Everything is a function of seed, cell, topology and run history, so it works in the endless streamed maze with no authored rooms.

Where ink exists:
- Every face that uses a print-enabled wallpaper (L0_Wallpaper, L0_Wallpaper_Shift, Exit_Wallpaper per 10_synthesis.md:97). That includes Level 0 columns, which are wallpapered (LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC.md:57, 59).
- Each face reads the cell it faces, sampled at positionWS + normalWS*0.5 (10_synthesis.md:131). Room-interior cells with no wall face show nothing; signs live on corridor and room-perimeter walls.
- Office zones (drywall Office_Wall, LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC.md:58) and the title stream rooms are masked to zero ink.

Per-zone personality at tier 0. The cut points a/b/c split steady / stutter / failing / dead; dim stays fixed at u >= 0.97:
- Low 2.4 m (35% of zones, FrontRoomsMap.cs:82): a .58, b .78, c .89, giving 58/20/11/8/3. The quiet-pull reading zone. Doors live on its borders.
- Standard Level 0 2.9 m (about 38% of zones): .62/.82/.92, giving today's 62/20/10/5/3. Pulling here is loud.
- Office 2.9 m (about 17%, officeShare .3, FrontRoomsMap.cs:117, :294-295): .70/.86/.93, giving 70/16/7/4/3. No ink. Pulling is a decoy only.
- Tall 5.4 m (10%): .52/.66/.80, giving 52/14/14/17/3. Lamps are out of reach. These are 'dark halls' whose perimeter beacons read across 15–21 m spans, and WAY there points to windows (the only exits).
- Module lamps keep overriding (ModuleLamp Auto/Steady/Stutter/Failing/Dead/Dim/Off, FrontRoomsRoomModuleData.cs:30; applied at FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1130). The Level Designer can therefore author 'reading rooms', for example a 3x3 room with a Failing centre and Dead corners. Off cells (:1084-1085) have L = 0 for good: dark, starved, unreadable.

Expected density at T0 Standard:
- About one legible glimpse per 25–35 cells walked (failing cells in a dropout while within 8 m), plus beacons about every 10–15 cells.
- Target cadence: median 20–40 s between legible sightings.

Drought breaker (director, map chat):
- Trigger: no legible sighting for 60 s, and the Relay is not in Chase or Hunt.
- Action: promote one unseen Steady cell 4–8 cells ahead along the player's walk (BFS from the player cell, biased to heading) to Failing. It must be in a Low or Standard Level 0 zone and have at least one wall face. This is consistent with R13's only-worse rule.

State storage: a 64x64 toroidal cell grid indexed (x & 63, y & 63). The period is 192 m, which is larger than the 120 m (buildRadius 2) and 168 m (buildRadius 3, FrontRoomsLevelProfile.cs:25) streamed areas, so no aliasing. Map roots sit on 192 m multiples (LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC.md:85).

On chunk build, C starts at its temperament's steady state: steady 1, stutter .97, failing .55, dead = spill equilibrium, dim .42, Off 0. A pulled lamp restarts from its stored pull time, using the hyperbolic decay.
design.triggers_and_timing:
All values are starting points.

Lamp-driven and per-frame:
- Continuous (per frame): lamp level, then E, then C, then V for every built cell, inside TickFixtures (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1160-1182, called from Update :569).
- Gate opening: 0.25 s of continuous dark, then a 0.5 s rise. Washout: 0.15 s.
- Read windows: fresh-dark corridor legible about 7 s, beacon about 28 s; sealed pocket about 10 s and about 37 s; failing-ballast glimpses last 0.1–0.5 s, roughly every 3–8 s.

Sign updates:
- Sign solve (WAY and SHUT) is event-driven: chunk built or dropped (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:594-631), DoorBroken (:1056-1064), GlassBroken (:1684-1687), new zone visited (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:876), lamp pulled.
- It is throttled to 1 Hz and staged. Commits happen after the cell has been unseen for 2 s or more.

Player-driven:
- Pull: a 1.2 s hold. At completion the lamp drops to 0 with a 0.3 s fade (no strobe), the noise fires, and the ink gate opens on the R3 timing.

Scripted beats:
- First-dark beat: once the start door has shut and the player is 6 or more cells into the maze (door shuts at 4 m, Relay released 3 s later: MAP_GENERATION.md:23-24, 34), and within 45 s. Pick a Steady corridor cell 2–4 cells ahead and in view, whose WAY target is a Door at most 6 cells beyond it. Its lamp dies in view over 1.5 s: three dips at 2 Hz or less, then off, with a ballast pop. The ink blooms at C = 1.
- Tier-up: every 4 zones crossed or 2 min, whichever comes first (proposal). All unseen cells re-cut at once. In-view cells re-cut after being unseen for 2 s or more.
- Tier-up beat: one in-view Steady cell 2–4 cells ahead dies with the same 1.5 s sequence. It is deferred while the Relay is in Chase or BreakDoor, until 5 s of Listen or Wander.

Relay chase wave (StateChanged to Chase, FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:141, :961):
- A BFS front travels from the Relay's cell at 8 m/s, about 2.7 cells/s, matching the print wave (10_synthesis.md:166).
- Each dark cell it reaches with V >= 0.05 flares by +0.4*C for 0.4 s (0.1 s rise), then its charge halves.
- At most one wave per 2–4 min, shared with the print's event budget (10_synthesis.md:166-169).

Freeze: all ink and lamp changes stop on Caught.
design.teaching_curve:
No text tutorial. The ink stays diegetic and every lesson is a beat.

0. Title and start rooms: no ink. The stream walls are masked.

1. FIRST DARK (about 10–40 s into the maze). A lamp 2–4 cells ahead dies in view. A WAY ladder blooms, brightening toward a door the player can reach within 6 cells, then fades over about 30 s. This teaches four things at once: ink appears where light dies, it fades, bright end means go, and it leads to a door. Pass criterion: the player dwells on the cell for 1 s or more and walks the ramp's way.

2. GASPS (first 2 min). Natural failing-ballast cells; the drought breaker guarantees one within 60 s. This teaches that you must wait and watch to read, which is the first risk exposure: stopping.

3. STARVED (natural Dead cells, 5% at Standard, 8% at Low). A faint, unreadable glow next to the memory of beat 1 teaches 'it must have been lit'. Dark alone is not enough.

4. PULL (gated). The 'HOLD E · PULL THE TUBE' prompt (Describe path, FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1589-1605) appears only after 2 legible sightings or 90 s in the maze, and only when aiming at a lit lens. The first pull always reads well, because any lit lamp gives C of about 1. The noise teaches its price.

5. SHUT. Learned naturally. Maze dead-end stubs are frequent, and the bracket is the second sign the player meets.

6. THE RELAY SEES IN THE DARK. Learned through play: the first Relay sighting from a dark cell. If the player is caught in a dark cell, the result screen (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:1495) may add one narrative line; narrative owns the wording.

7. Tier 1 (about 2 min). The tier beat and a darker map show that signs come in bursts after a tier-up and that bursts fade.

8. RING (P2 only, after tier 2). Introduced once SHUT and WAY are fluent.
design.escalation_over_run:
Tier t is capped at 4. Cut points: a_t = a0 - 0.06t, b_t = b0 - 0.055t, c_t = c0 - 0.025t, with a >= 0.30, and the dim band fixed. Standard Level 0 shares (steady/stutter/failing/dead/dim):

- T0: 62/20/10/5/3 (the code today, FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1128)
- T1: 56/20.5/13/7.5/3
- T2: 50/21/16/10/3
- T3: 44/21.5/19/12.5/3
- T4: 38/22/22/15/3

Low, Office and Tall shift by the same deltas from their own T0 cuts. For example, Tall at T4 is 30/14/26/27/3.

What rises with tier:
- Relay dark-wander bias: k = 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0. That is about a 21% chance of a dark wander target at T0 and about 70% at T4.
- Sprint-in-dark noise multiplier: x1.25 at all tiers.
- Walking noise in dark cells: 4 m per step from T3.
- Plus the proposed tier Relay speed and hearing (not mine). Hearing multiplies every noise, pulls included.

What the curve does to the economy:
- Early: dark is rare, and signs come only from gasps and pulls, so they are cheap to reach and pulls are the main source.
- Late: dark is common, but most dead cells are STARVED (no charge). Readable signs come in short post-tier bursts (cells that died while charged, about 30 s of value) and from pulls.
- The player reads less often but more urgently, in a maze where the dark is the Relay's home.

The ink's own physics, gate and grammar never change, so the run escalates without breaking the player's model.

If doorsNeedKeys is later enabled (FrontRoomsLevelProfile.cs:32-33): WAY retargets to the zone key cell (FrontRoomsMap.cs:627-651) until it is held, then to doors. The proposed 'key distance' tier then also stretches how far the signs must lead.
design.interaction_with_relay_and_escapes:
Sight:
- The Relay's 12 m ray (FrontRoomsHunter.cs:25; FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:926-931) ignores light, and it has no facing test.
- In a lit cell you spot it inside the fog, which is about 93% at 20 m (FrontRoomsLook.cs:18-19; ExponentialSquared). In a dead cell, ambient light only (equator .34/.31/.22, FrontRoomsLook.cs:16) cuts that badly.
- Counterplay: an inked wall backlights the Relay's white head and body (LEVELS_AND_ENTITIES.md:57). A glowing corridor is the one dark place where you see it first.

Speed math (why reading is risky):
- Chase 4.2 m/s against sprint 5.5 m/s for 5 s (FrontRoomsHunter.cs:24-26; FrontRooms3DGame.cs:147-149). A full sprint banks only 6.5 m.
- Every second spent standing to read during contact gives up 4.2 m. Reading belongs before contact, or comes free from the chase-wave flare.

Doors (WAY's preferred target):
- Shutting a door forces BreakDoor: 2.5 s plus a 0.25 s fall (FrontRoomsHunter.cs:21; FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:46), roughly 11.5 m bought at chase speed.
- LoseTrack follows through a door only if it was right behind you (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:294-301).
- WAY skips Relay-broken doors, and its new code only commits once the cell is unseen.

Windows (fallback target, +6 cell cost):
- The hold is 1 s (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1676-1689), and breaking makes a 40 m noise, x1.4 = 56 m (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:150).
- The Relay cannot pass unbroken glass but follows through a broken frame. WAY therefore prefers doors.

Line of sight:
- Losing it for 1.5 s (FrontRoomsHunter.cs:27) sends the Relay to lastSeen and then into Search: 3 spots, 1.1 s each, 15 s cap (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:54-55).
- SHUT warns you off pockets where a search corners you. The RING option shows loops for circling.

Noise ladder (radius, then x1.4 hearing):
- Pull Low: 8 m, about 11 m
- Door: 14 m, about 20 m
- Pull Standard: 16 m, about 22 m
- Sprint: 26 m, about 36 m (x1.25 in dark, about 45 m)
- Glass: 40 m, about 56 m
- (FrontRoomsHunter.cs:28-31; FrontRooms3DGame.cs:786-796, 865.)
- A pull therefore summons a Hunt (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:279-286) to the pulled cell. The player has 7–10 s to read and leave.

Wander bias:
- Darkness you create keeps drawing the Relay's Wander picks after the noise is forgotten.
- Emergent use: pull lamps on a branch you will not take, as bait.

Leash:
- After 45 s with no contact and a gap over 30 cells, the Relay relays itself 9–15 cells from you (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:49, 57, 182-187).
- So long, safe reading sessions in a quiet pocket are capped by the system. This is already in the code.

Chase wave:
- On Chase, the wave flares every charged dark cell it crosses (a free, instant read that also points back at the Relay), then halves their charge.
- Reading in the chase is a one-shot. Reading beforehand is what pays.
design.interaction_with_moving_print:
The ink rides on the print, but the information does not:
- Glyph shapes live in the print's B channel, so subliminal drift, strip slips and reprints move or redraw the glyph.
- The sign (WAY ramp, SHUT bracket, RING) is a per-roll emission mask computed from world position and the cell state. Print motion can never move or corrupt the information.
- Narrative glyphs must be left/right symmetric or direction-free. A mirrored, directional glyph would need a second print fetch, which is the visual chat's call.

Flicker reprints:
- The print's 'walls move when the lights flicker' rule (10_synthesis.md:139-142) fires in the same dark windows in which the ink becomes visible.
- Allowed: the glyph shape may change between a failing ballast's gasps. The narrative can use this, for example a message that rewrites itself.
- Forbidden: the sign code changing while seen (R9). Both systems share one visible-cell set and the same 2 s unseen hold.

Per-cell print choice:
- The print system's per-cell frame offset (state A channel) picks which print slice, and so which B glyph variant, a cell shows.
- Narrative can therefore vary glyph content per cell without an extra fetch. The variant changes only through discrete unseen jumps.

Scripted beats and events:
- Slow crawl is reserved for the tier-up and first-dark beats, where the dying cell's print may crawl while its ink blooms.
- The chase wave is one event shared by both layers: the visible print wave and the ink flare-and-drain travel together at about 8 m/s from the Relay.

Kept separate on purpose:
- The Relay wake reprints only the visible print and does not touch the ink.
- The print says 'where it has been'; the ink says 'where to go'.

Accessibility:
- With reduce-motion the print freezes, but the ink still works. Its strips are static, so the ink is the accessible information channel.
design.readability_and_accessibility:
Three reading distances, checked against FOV 76° at 1080p (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:227; about 14 px/deg):
- BEACON, up to about 20–30 m: a green patch at V >= 0.12 marks a dark, charged cell. Fog keeps about 93% at 20 m.
- SIGN, up to about 8 m on corridor side walls: a cell 5–8 m ahead with 1.5 m lateral offset spans about 6°, about 87 px, about 22 px per roll. At 8–11 m it drops to about 10 px per roll, which is marginal.
- SIGN, up to about 20 m on head-on end walls: a 3 m wall at 20 m is about 122 px, about 30 px per roll. WAY ramps on the end wall at a T or L junction read as 'turn this way' from a full corridor away.
- GLYPH, up to about 2 m: narrative detail.

Contrast and colour:
- Contrast targets (visual chat): a Weber contrast of about 1.5 on dark-cell paper at V = 1, about 0.5 at the 0.33 legibility threshold, and about 0.18 at the beacon threshold.
- The code is luminance-coded (which rolls glow), not hue-coded, so deuteranopes read it. The ZnS:Cu green is flavour.
- Settings: 'Ink contrast boost' (x1.5 emission, legibility threshold to 0.25).

Photosensitivity (10_synthesis.md:197-200, P2 gate :228):
- Glow appears over at least 0.75 s, so a cell shows at most about 1.3 appearances per second.
- Stutter lamps never reveal ink, because the gate needs 0.25 s of continuous dark.
- Failing-ballast dropouts come from Perlin at 1.4 (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1201), well under 3 Hz.
- The tier and first-dark death sequences dip at 2 Hz or less. The chase flare is a single travelling front.
- Test the ink, the print and the existing fixture flicker as one combined stimulus: 3 flashes/s or fewer, and no stripe reversal above 3 Hz over more than 25% of the screen.

Reduce motion:
- Ink low-pass tau is 1.0 s both ways.
- Failing cells show a 3 s running mean of V: a steady, faint, readable sign.
- No chase flare; the drain only.
- The death sequence becomes a single 1.5 s fade.
- Ask the visual chat to soften stutter and dropout flicker under the same toggle.

Prompt and HUD:
- Prompt text follows the existing 'HOLD E · …' pattern (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1602).
- No HUD marker for ink, ever.

Rule kept: lit modules look identical. Ink only differs in cells already made different by a lamp temperament, or by a deliberate beat.
design.implementation_data_flow:
1. MAP: FrontRoomsMapWorld.TickFixtures (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1160-1182) already computes f.level for every built fixture.
- New: write the logical level (f.level; 0 if pulled or Off; ignore fade and held) into lamp64[(x&63) + 64*(y&63)].

2. MAP: a new plain-C# FrontRoomsInkField (FrontRoomsMap/, owned by the map chat). It is ticked right after TickFixtures in Update (:569).
- Arrays [4096]: lamp, charge, darkTimer, vis, darkMean; byte code; byte pending; float unseenFor.
- spill[4096 x 4]: rebuilt on chunk build and drop, and on DoorMoved, DoorBroken and GlassBroken (:59-63), from Cache.Edge and PassageBetween (:1030-1050).
- Per frame it computes E, then C (R1), then G and V (R3), then the display low-pass, writing vis[] as bytes.
- Cost: about 1600 cells x a few flops, well under 0.1 ms.

3. MAP: SignSolver. Event-driven and throttled to 1 Hz.
- Multi-source 0-1 BFS for WAY (R7), with zonesVisited passed in from FrontRooms3DGame.
- Tarjan bridges for SHUT (R8).
- Writes pending[]. pending is committed into code[] only where unseenFor >= 2 s (R9).
- Budget: 0.5 ms or less, amortised across frames on chunk-build spikes.

4. VISUAL: the print driver.
- In RenderPipelineManager.beginCameraRendering, compute the visible cell set: BFS over see-through edges plus TestPlanesAABB (10_synthesis.md:136).
- Publish it as a 4096-bit set that the map reads: for unseenFor, sign commits, tier re-cuts and beat placement.

5. VISUAL: pack one RGBA8 64x64 texture per frame.
- Channels: R = lamp level (the print's flicker mask), G = ink V, B = sign code (bits 0-1 direction N/E/S/W, bits 2-3 class Blank/WAY/SHUT/RING, bits 4-7 reserved), A = the print's per-cell state or frame offset.
- Settings: point filter, Repeat, SetPixelData plus Apply(false). Shader.SetGlobalTexture('_FR_CellState').
- Size: 16 KB per frame.

6. VISUAL: FrontRooms/Surface Frag, inside _FR_PRINT.
- One LOAD at cell = floor((positionWS + normalWS*0.5).xz / 3) & 63.
- roll = floor(worldAlong / 0.75) & 3, where worldAlong is z for |n.x| > 0.5, else x.
- w = pattern(class, dir, wallAxis, roll).
- emission += _InkGlow.rgb x V x w x print.b x paperCavity. The B channel comes from the print fetch the shader already does.
- Never touches albedo, normal, smoothness or cavity. Fog applies. Stream-room walls and Office walls are masked.

7. RELAY (map):
- Wander picks weighted by darkMean from InkField (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:424-438).
- The game passes a dark multiplier into the sprint Noise call (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:865).

8. GAME (map chat owns FrontRooms3DGame.cs, LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC.md §10):
- Tier clock, then map.SetLampTier(t), which re-cuts using u and the zone/tier cuts, unseen cells only.
- The beats director: first-dark, tier beat, drought breaker.
- Pull verb: Describe and Hold get a lens branch. The lens collider is removed today (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1094), so either add a DescribeAt(RaycastHit) that tests the lens rect X[1.2,1.8] x Z[1.2,2.4] of the cell at ceiling height, or keep a lens box collider. Then PullLamp(cell) adds to pulledLamps and raises LampDied(cell, cause), and relay.Noise fires.

9. EVENTS out:
- LampDied(cell, cause: Pull/Tier/Beat/Drought), InkLegible(cell) for telemetry, and a ChaseWave(origin) shared with the print.
- Everything is deterministic for a fixed runSeed plus the same inputs.

playtest_metrics: Time between legible sightings (V >= 0.33, within 8 m, on screen 0.5 s or more), per tier. Target at T0: median 20-40 s, p90 75 s or less. Above 90 s means the ink is too rare; under 10 s means it is wallpaper noise.

Dwell: median time stationary (under 0.3 m/s) facing a dark charged cell. Target 2-6 s. Over 10 s means the signs are too hard to read; under 1 s means reading carries no risk.
First-dark beat comprehension: the player looks at the cell for 1 s or more, and then reaches the indicated door. Target 70% or more.
Pulls per run-minute after minute 3. Target 0.3-1.0. 0 means the verb is undiscovered or not worth it; over 2 means the noise is too cheap, so check stacked noise.

Share of catches with the player in a dark cell (own lamp under 0.2), compared with the share of time spent in dark cells. Target: catch share about 1.5-2x the time share. Under 1x means dark is not risky; over 3x means dark is a death trap.
Relay encounters (first Chase) that start while the player is in or beside a dark cell, per tier: should rise with k.
Chase escape rate split by whether the player read a WAY sign in the previous 30 s. Target a gap of at least +15 percentage points. No gap means the sign is not useful.
SHUT efficacy: the share of chase deaths inside pockets that were marked SHUT and seen beforehand, versus unmarked pockets.
Post-tier burst: the number of legible sightings in the 40 s after a tier-up, against the baseline.
Open survey question at the end of the session: 'What does the green mean?' Target 60% or more naming 'way to a door/exit' or 'dead end' correctly. Track misreads of 'dark = hiding'.

Photosensitivity log: the automated flash and stripe check with fixture flicker, print and ink combined. At most 3 flashes/s, and no stripe reversal above 3 Hz over more than 25% of the screen. Run in both normal and reduce-motion.

Performance: ink tick under 0.1 ms on average; SignSolver 0.5 ms or less per call with no frame over 1 ms added on chunk build; state upload 16 KB per frame; GPU median +0.2 ms or less. Use the autopilot seeds 2554 and 20388 plus a Level 0 corridor flythrough, against the 58.7 fps / p99 19.4 ms baseline (10_synthesis.md:230).

Sign flips while the player reads, for example when the Relay breaks the target door. Fix: commit only when unseen. Stale WAY still points onward, through a broken door, so it never lies about direction.
WAY points back through the door just used. Fix: target unvisited zones first.

Players bring the stealth-game belief that dark hides you. Counter: the first Relay contact in the dark, a beat where it plainly sees you in a glowing corridor, and the silhouette rule making 'see it first' the actual reward of glow.

Compass by pull spam. Counters: the 1.2 s hold, noise of 11 m or 22 m, +50% stacked noise per chained pull within 30 s, permanent darkness feeding Wander bias, and Tall zones unreachable. Watch pulls per minute.
Breadcrumbing with pulled lamps (persistent per cell across chunk shifts). Accepted as emergent mapping; bounded by noise and bias.
Bait pulls far from your route to steer Wander. Accepted and intended as double-edged. The noise draws a Hunt to the pull spot first.
Reading from a lit cell into a dark neighbour. Intended skill ('read from the light'); it does not dodge the 12 m sight ray.
Long safe reading in a sealed pocket. Already capped by the leash relay after 45 s of quiet (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:182-187).
Failing-ballast gasps too short to read (0.1-0.5 s). Knobs: the gate delay (0.25 s), and the visual chat's dropout threshold .72 (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1201).
Late-tier starvation: most dead cells unreadable, so the run feels hint-less. The tier beat, the drought breaker and pulls keep a floor. Tune the T4 cut floor (a >= 0.30).
Polarity misread (brighter end = danger). The first-dark beat must put a visible door at the bright end, within 6 cells.

Chunk shift (30 s away, FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:612-616) reshuffles the interior. Signs recompute on rebuild, temperaments are keyed by cell and stable, pulls persist, and charge re-initialises from the steady state, so no pops are seen (rebuilds happen 24 m or more away, in fog).
Tier re-cut visible in view, breaking the 'every module the same' rule. Guard with the shared visible set. Only the single announced beat cell dies in view.
Additive emission visible on lit walls. The gate G is mandatory; do not rely on the lit paper to hide it.
Office zones with no ink feel like dead air. Intentional (lit, furnished, sign-free), but watch dwell and boredom in Office-heavy seeds.
narrative_slots: What the glow ink is and who printed it. A period-plausible 1990 frame: a ZnS:Cu 'night print' run, or emergency egress marking hidden in the wallpaper. Why is it on Level 0 paper but not in Offices?
What WAY means in-world: who laid a ladder of light toward doors into unseen places, and why only toward unvisited zones.
What SHUT means in-world: the bracket as a mark left by someone who was cornered there?
Optional RING meaning, for the P2 loop sign.

The B-channel glyph shapes and their under-2 m content (tallies, words, symbols). They must be left/right symmetric or direction-free, and may vary per print frame, so a glyph can rewrite itself between a failing ballast's gasps.
Why the Relay sees without light and why it drifts toward dead lamps.
Why the chase wave makes the ink flare and then go dim (it drains the stored light).
The fiction of pulling a tube: who the player is to know how. The prompt verb name ('PULL THE TUBE' is a placeholder).
Flavour for the first-dark beat and the tier-up lamp death (the ballast pop as a sign that something has changed).
An optional result-screen line for a catch in the dark, and whether a 'lamps pulled' stat appears.
Why fresh glow is bright and old glow is starved: a line players can remember, along the lines of 'the paper only remembers what it was shown'.
references: Charlotte Perkins Gilman, The Yellow Wallpaper (1892): a sub-pattern visible only in certain light (10_synthesis.md:239). This is the literary anchor for ink that appears when the lamp fails.

Photoluminescent (ZnS:Cu) exit and egress markings that glow when power fails: the real-world model for WAY. Examples: low-location escape-route lighting on passenger ships, required after the 1990 Scandinavian Star fire (IMO guidelines, 1993). Verify the dates before putting this in a deck.
Haunted Mansion (1969) lightning portraits: change revealed in a dark window (10_synthesis.md:242).
Left 4 Dead AI Director: build-up, peak, relax pacing, the model for the tier beats and drought breaker (10_synthesis.md:159).
Amnesia: The Dark Descent (2010): darkness as a risk/reward resource. Inverted here: dark does not hide you, it informs you.
Outlast (2013), camcorder night vision: information bought with a scarce, risky resource.
Alien: Isolation (2014), motion tracker: reading information exposes you to the hunter.
The Exit 8 (2023): reading anomalies against a stable baseline, the 'every module looks the same' rule.
Dark Deception (2018): Red's primary reference. Maze chases where reading the route under pressure is the core skill.

design.name: Afterglow Grammar
design.pitch: The phosphorescent print is a small, fixed written language that only shows in the dark. True marks sit at the mouths of branches and say what each branch does: keeps going, closes, has a door, has glass, or holds the key. The Relay leaves a wake that fades like real afterglow. From tier 2 on, a forger plants fake marks that break the ink's one physical law: they keep glowing under a lit lamp. No save data is kept. The words, the grammar and the order they are introduced are the same in every maze, so what carries from run to run is the player's ability to read.
design.player_fantasy: Run 1: the paper glows faint green where the tubes died, and that is creepy. Run 3: "that branch says BLIND, don't sprint in there." Run 6, mid-chase: you read DOOR then BLIND at a fork, see that the wake behind you is already faint, and slip into the door room to wait. A turn later you stop dead because a THROUGH mark kept glowing while its lamp struck, so a liar wrote it. Fluency in the maze's handwriting is the only progression. Exit 8 asks you to know the corridor; this asks you to know the writing.
rules: R1 PHYSICS (never changes). A cell's ink output is glow = charge × smoothstep(0.6, 0.2, L̃) × plateGain. L̃ is the cell's lamp TEMPERAMENT level after slewing (Fixture.level, FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:98, computed by Level() at :1184-1214). The gate never uses light.enabled: lamps beyond lightRadius 16 m are switched off only for budget (FrontRoomsLevelProfile.cs:35; TickFixtures FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1160-1181), and that must not light up distant ink. Charge rises under light and decays in the dark (numbers in triggers_and_timing).

R2 BASELINE. Every dark Level 0 wallpaper cell shows the same BASE sub-pattern (plate 0, gain 0.35). The 18% of cells that are naturally dark (failing 10% + dead 5% + dim 3%, roll at FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1128) teach 'normal ink' within the first minute. Words are deviations from that baseline, so every module still looks the same unless it carries a deliberate word.

R3 MOUTH RULE. True words appear only in the 1st or 2nd cell of a branch leaving a junction (a cell with 3 or more passable edges). A word describes its branch, read away from the junction. A branch carries at most 2 words, and the second (2-3 cells further in, or just past a door) qualifies the first.

R4 VOCABULARY. 8 plates, 3 bits, fixed forever. 0 BASE. 1 THROUGH: the branch runs at least 16 cells or reaches the chunk border, so it connects onward. 2 BLIND: the branch closes within 16 cells, with no door or window. 3 DOOR: a door within 4 cells. 3+2 DOOR·BLIND: the door opens into a closed room of 8 cells or fewer, a hide-hole. 4 GLASS: a window within 4 cells. 5 WAKE: the Relay crossed this cell. 6 HEART: the zone's key cell is within 3 cells. 7 LURE: a forged THROUGH, mirrored.

R5 AGE. WAKE brightness is age: c = 0.6·e^(−Δ/6 s) + 0.4·e^(−Δ/75 s) after the crossing. Bright (> 0.55) means under 7 s ago, medium means 7-35 s, faint (0.08-0.25) means 35-120 s, then it is gone. The brighter end of a trail is the way it went. Words sit on reader lamps that keep re-charging them, so they breathe with their lamp instead of fading.

R6 CHANGE RULE. A plate may change only when its cell has been unseen for at least 0.75 s, or its glow output has been 0 for at least 0.25 s (the lamp is lit and the ink washed out). A true mark never changes in view. This mirrors the visible print's 'change when unseen or masked' rule (10_synthesis.md §5).

R7 THE LIE. A mark that keeps glowing while its lamp is lit is not ink. Lures are always forged THROUGH marks placed at BLIND mouths. They never imitate BLIND, DOOR, GLASS or WAKE, so the 'stop' words can always be trusted. A lure the player catches is itself information: that branch is closed.

R8 TRUTH CONTRACT. Apart from lures, every word is true when it is written. Only two things make a word stale. A broken door's DOOR word turns to BASE at the next R6 window (BreakDoor FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1056-1066). A revisit shift re-plans the chunk's words while the player is away (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:612-616), so a word that changed tells the player the layout moved.

R9 ILLITERATE PLACES. There is no ink in Office zones (drywall, not wallpaper: ZoneTheme.Office FrontRoomsMap.cs:16, about 30% of Standard zones by officeShare at :117), in the start area (InStartArea FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:389), or on the title stream walls. ModuleLamp.Off cells (FrontRoomsRoomModuleData.cs:30) are never charged by a lamp and glow only from WAKE or the chase wave.

R10 NO SAVE DATA. Plate art, meanings, grammar and the tier order in which words are introduced are constants that do not depend on runSeed (a new random seed every run, FrontRooms3DGame.cs:527). Placement is a pure function of (seed, chunk, revision, tier). There is no codex and no unlock by run count, and the HUD gives no glossary.
design.placement_and_generation:
A new InkPlanner (map chat) runs once per chunk build in FrontRoomsMapWorld.BuildInto, on the Cache.Get(coord) data, before the cell loop reaches BuildFixture (call at FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:759). It is deterministic on (seed, chunk, revision, tier) through MapHash (FrontRoomsMap.cs:201-232) with new salts (for example Ink 79, InkPick 83, Lure 89). Each word sits in the same chunk as its junction, so neighbouring chunks never have to agree.

1. GRAPH. Branches walk through Open and Arch edges inside the chunk (MapChunk.east/north/west/south, FrontRoomsMap.cs:156-160). A Door or Window edge ends a branch and is recorded as a feature. A passable edge on the chunk border counts as 'connects onward': each border has a required opening (BorderEdge FrontRoomsMap.cs:337-345) and every chunk is a spanning tree, so every cell connects to every other (MAP_GENERATION.md:94). The dead-end test is therefore chunk-local and exact.
2. JUNCTIONS. Level 0 cells outside the start area with 3 or more passable edges.
3. BRANCH SCAN. For each junction J and each Open or Arch neighbour M, run a BFS from M that never re-enters J, capped at 16 cells. Record size, touchesBorder, doorDepth, windowDepth and keyDepth (chunk.hasKey and keyCell, FrontRoomsMap.cs:171-173 and :632-656).
4. WORD. Pick the first rule that applies:
   - a window within 4 cells → GLASS;
   - otherwise a door within 4 cells → DOOR. Add a second word, BLIND, in the first cell past the door when the region beyond it (BFS without further doors) closes in 8 cells or fewer and does not touch the border;
   - otherwise a closed branch (size under 16, no border) → BLIND;
   - otherwise the key within 3 cells and tier 2 or higher → HEART;
   - otherwise → THROUGH.
5. MOUTH CELL. Use depth 1 or 2, preferring a cell with a wall that faces J, so the word lands on a frontal wall. The cell must be Level 0, outside the start area and have lamp == Auto, which respects module-authored lamps. Words of different branches stay at least 2 cells apart.
6. SCORE AND PICK. BLIND with size ≥ 3 scores 1.0; DOOR·BLIND 0.9; THROUGH at a junction that also has a BLIND branch 0.8 (it makes a readable choice pair); GLASS 0.7; DOOR 0.6; HEART 0.4; any other THROUGH 0.3. Ties break by hash. Keep the top N(tier) words per chunk: 3, 4, 4, 5, 5 for tiers 0-4.
7. READER LAMP. If the chosen cell's natural temperament (seeded at FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1087, rolled at :1128) is already Failing, Dead or Dim, keep it. Otherwise override chunk.lamp[index] (FrontRoomsMap.cs:180) with a new Guttering mode, or Failing if Guttering is not built. That forces about 3-5 extra dark lamps per chunk on top of the natural 18%.
8. LURES (tier 2 and up). Put a forged THROUGH at a BLIND mouth that has no word. At T2-T3 the lure goes in a cell whose lamp is Steady, so it is plainly lit and still glowing. At T4 it can also sit on a Guttering lamp, mirrored, with a constant glow. Never in the vignette chunk. At most 25% of the THROUGH-shaped marks among built chunks. Never two lures on one route.
9. TEACHING VIGNETTE. In the start-door chunk (StreamFocus, MAP_GENERATION.md:19), find the first junction 3-10 cells from the door cell that has a BLIND branch of 2-5 cells. Give it a BLIND/THROUGH pair on Guttering lamps, outside the tier budget. This happens in every run, with every seed.
10. DENSITY TARGET. Plan for about 20-40 branch mouths per chunk (measure by extending Verify 100 seeds to count mouths, words and forced lamps). Words then cover 5-8% of cells, and BASE shows in about 18-23%.

Runtime writes come from the InkField, not the planner:
- WAKE is written on BASE cells the Relay enters.
- A DOOR word turns to BASE after its door breaks (DoorBroken event, FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:63).
- A revisit shift (FrontRoomsMap.cs:706; FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:612-616) re-plans the chunk's words and keeps its WAKE, which is still true.
design.triggers_and_timing:
All numbers are playtest starting points.

PER-FRAME CELL SIM (CPU, every built Level 0 cell, run after TickFixtures at FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:569):
- Lamp input: L = Fixture.level × the start-area hold factor.
- Slewed lamp: L̃ moves toward dark with τ 0.35 s and toward light with τ 0.08 s, so light washes the ink out quickly.
- Charge uses two stores. While lit, cf += L·(0.6 − cf)·dt/0.6 s and cs += L·(0.4 − cs)·dt/0.6 s. Both always decay: cf by τ 6 s, cs by τ 75 s. Charge c = cf + cs.
- Output: glow = c × smoothstep(0.6, 0.2, L̃) × gain. Gains: words 1.0, WAKE up to 0.9, BASE 0.35. LURE is a constant 0.8 and ignores the gate.
- Output slew: |Δglow| ≤ 2.0 per second, so a full swing takes at least 0.5 s and contrast reverses at 1 Hz or less.
- Glow under 0.08 is written as 0.

What each temperament does to the ink:
- Steady (62%): no ink.
- Stutter (20%): its events toggle 0.95/0.05 on Perlin(t·23) (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1196). The fast-recovering L̃ keeps glow at about 0, so stutter cells never strobe ink and never carry words.
- Failing (10%): fully charged. About 0.25 between dropouts, full during dropouts.
- Dead (5%): each 0.06-0.18 s blink at 0.8, every 8-28 s, adds about 0.1 charge, so dead cells are dark but faint. Rule for players: the blink feeds the ink.
- Dim (3%): steady at about 0.43.

NEW GUTTERING READER LAMP (proposed mode 5):
- Rests at level 0.03.
- Strikes every U(4, 9) s: ramps to 0.7 over 0.12 s, holds 0.4-1.2 s with ±0.05 shimmer at 2 Hz or less, then drops over 0.15 s.
- Words therefore read about 80% of the time and re-charge to 0.6-0.9 at each strike. Flash rate is 0.25 Hz or less.

PLATE WRITES follow R6: unseen for at least 0.75 s, or glow 0 for at least 0.25 s. 'Unseen' is the shared visible-cell set from 10_synthesis.md §5: a BFS over see-through edges from the camera's cell (Open, Arch, open or broken doors, and all windows, since glass is see-through) plus a frustum AABB test.

WAKE:
- Each frame, read relay.Position and take its cell. When the cell changes, log (cell, t).
- If the cell's plate is BASE, a WAKE write is queued under R6 with charge taken from the R5 formula at the passage time, so its brightness is right when it is revealed.
- Relay speeds give the trail's spacing: wander 2.08 m/s (huntSpeed 2.6 × WanderPace 0.8, FrontRoomsHunter.cs:23 and FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:52), search 1.82, chase 4.2.
- A Relay teleport (Arrive/Relays, FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:395-421) leaves a gap in the trail, which is readable.

CHASE WAVE (tier 1 and up):
- Trigger: StateChanged(Chase) (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:141 and :961), at most once per 120 s.
- A BFS from the Relay's cell over passable edges, depth 10 cells or fewer, gives arrival times of 3 m ÷ 8 m/s = 0.375 s per cell. This is the same field as the visible-print corridor wave (10_synthesis.md §5).
- On arrival, each cell's charge ramps to at least 0.9 over 0.6 s. Every word near the chase lights up, travelling outward from the threat. Lit cells stay invisible.

TIER CHANGE: affects only chunks planned from then on. Built chunks keep their words until they are rebuilt.

CAUGHT: freeze the sim and the texture.
design.teaching_curve:
The game teaches through consequences, never through a glossary.

IN EVERY RUN:
- 0:00-0:30. The first dark cells show BASE. Lesson: the paper has a hidden layer in the dark, and lit cells hide it.
- First junction (the vignette). A BLIND/THROUGH pair on Guttering lamps. The Relay is released only 3 s after the start door shuts, 9-15 cells away, and does not know where the player is (MAP_GENERATION.md:34-35). So the player can safely test the BLIND branch, hit the dead end, come back, and see the same shape again two chunks later.
- Tier 1 (about 2 min). DOOR, GLASS and WAKE appear. The first glowing smear on a dark cell is followed by Relay footsteps. The first chase wave lights the words around the player at the moment they matter.
- Tier 2 (about 4 min). HEART appears, and the first lure, which is obvious: it glows green under a fully lit, humming steady lamp. A player who knows R1 spots it. A player who doesn't follows it into a dead end and remembers.
- Tier 4. The subtle lure: mirrored, on a Guttering lamp, and the tell shows only when the lamp strikes and the mark fails to wash out.

ACROSS RUNS (targets to validate, knowledge only):
- Run 1: notices the glow, maybe tells BASE from a word.
- Runs 2-3: BLIND/THROUGH used at forks, and reading becomes route choice.
- Runs 3-5: DOOR·BLIND hiding, reading WAKE age, using GLASS as a vantage point.
- Runs 5-8: lure tells. Lure tells cannot even be seen until the player survives to tier 2, so the curve is gated by skill, not by save data.
- Fluency target: 6-10 runs.

OPTIONAL DIEGETIC LEGEND (visual + narrative chats). One title stream room, which loops like Exit 8's corridor, has a dead lamp. Its far wall shows THROUGH beside its open end door and BLIND on a wall stub. It is the same every run.

HUD FALLBACK, only if playtests show fewer than 50% of first-run players notice the ink by minute 3: a one-time Flash() (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:792-805 pattern) on first exposure, 'THE PAPER GLOWS WHERE THE LIGHT FAILS'. It names no words.
design.escalation_over_run:
The physics never escalates: charge, decay, gate and slew are identical in every tier, so what players learn stays true. Only what is written, and who writes it, changes. Tiers follow Red's unconfirmed DP08 proposal: tier up every 4 zones (zonesVisited, FrontRooms3DGame.cs:162 and :873-876) or every 2 minutes, 5 tiers.

| Tier | Zones / time | Words per chunk | New this tier | Lure rate per chunk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T0 | 0-4 zones, 0-2 min | 3 | BASE, THROUGH, BLIND | 0 |
| T1 | 4-8 zones, 2-4 min | 4 | DOOR, DOOR·BLIND, GLASS, WAKE, chase wave | 0 |
| T2 | 8-12 zones, 4-6 min | 4 | HEART | 0.15, lure-lit |
| T3 | 12-16 zones, 6-8 min | 5 | none | 0.25, lure-lit |
| T4 | 16+ zones, 8+ min | 5 | lure on Guttering lamps, mirrored, tell only at strikes | 0.35 Guttering + 0.10 lit |

Notes on the table:
- Lure-lit means the lure sits in a Steady-lamp cell.
- In T4, DP08's rising failing-light share (natural Failing 10% → 15%, map chat's threshold at FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1128) also adds BASE noise, so the signal-to-noise falls.
- Lure cap at all tiers: at most 25% of THROUGH-shaped marks.

Pressure balance:
- DP08 raises chase speed from 4.2 to 5.4 m/s, which matches the player's 5.5 m/s sprint (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:147), and cuts door break time from 2.5 to 1.3 s. By T4 a sprint alone cannot win, so reading BEFORE the chase decides survival. That is the point of the literacy curve.
- The lures and the extra BASE noise keep fluent players from coasting.
- The 120 s chase-wave cooldown stays fixed, so later tiers do not flash more.
design.interaction_with_relay_and_escapes:
DARKNESS DOES NOT HIDE YOU. The Relay's sight is a 12 m eye-height raycast with no light term (Sees/Visible, FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:926-950; sightRange FrontRoomsHunter.cs:26). Dark word cells are places to read, not places to hide, and time spent reading at a junction is the risk. The fiction must not say otherwise.

SPRINT, 5 s of stamina (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:149). The 5.5 vs 4.2 m/s gap gains about 6.5 m per bar. That only breaks the 12 m sight with corners, which THROUGH branches (16+ cells, onward) have and BLIND branches use up. Being chased into BLIND ends in Caught: catch distance is 0.7 m (FrontRoomsHunter.cs:28). Sprint steps are heard at 26 × 1.4 = 36 m (FrontRoomsHunter.cs:29-32; FrontRooms3DGame.cs:865).

BREAKING LINE OF SIGHT. After 1.5 s out of sight (lostSightSeconds), LoseTrack sends it to the last-seen spot. It then searches 3 spots × 1.1 s inside that room, or within 2 steps that need no door, for 15 s at most (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:294-331 and :55). Words tell the player which side branch lies outside that search footprint.

SHUTTING A DOOR. DOOR·BLIND is the hide-hole, and its meaning flips with context:
- Wander never crosses a shut door (Search(from, 14, false), FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:426 and :463), so a shut door-room is a refuge from a wandering Relay.
- If the player crosses that door between 1 s before and 1.5 s after it last saw them, it follows straight into the room (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:294-300) and breaks the door in 2.5 s + 0.25 s.
- Shutting the door is a noise heard at 14 × 1.4 = 19.6 m (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:785-789).
- So the sentence reads: unseen, and no bright WAKE nearby, means hide; seen means coffin.

BREAKING A WINDOW. GLASS marks a window within 4 cells. The unbroken pane is a non-trigger collider (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:953-961). It blocks the Relay's sight ray, and the Relay cannot path through unbroken glass (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:462), but the player can see through it: a vantage point. Breaking it (hold E for 1 s) is the loudest noise, 40 × 1.4 = 56 m (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:150 and :792-796). After that the edge is open both ways (PassageBetween FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1046). GLASS with a bright WAKE beyond it means it is on the other side and blind to you. Tall zones are left only through windows (MAP_GENERATION.md:91), so GLASS is the word of the halls.

WAKE gives the Relay's recent path and its direction (the bright end). The chase wave reveals the words around the chase at its start.

DEPENDENCY. The prototype HUD shows the Relay's state and distance (MAP_GENERATION.md:32). Unless that readout is removed or hidden in play builds, WAKE is redundant. This is map chat's call, since FrontRooms3DGame.cs is theirs per LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC.md §10.
design.interaction_with_moving_print:
ONE SCHEDULER. Ink plate swaps use exactly the same windows as the visible print's discrete reprints: unseen, or masked by the lamp (10_synthesis.md §5). One visibility set and one BFS wave field serve both.

LAYOUT CONSTRAINT (visual chat's decision; this is a proposal). An ink plate swap must never change R or G, and a visible-print change must never change B. Proposal: the print array becomes 4 visible keyframes × 8 ink plates = 32 slices, which is the 8 × 4 pack sheet already planned (10_synthesis.md:118). The slice index is frame × 8 + plate, and plate k's B channel is identical across the 4 visible frames. Visible jumps, rare crawl beats and per-strip phase (strip & 3) then never move a word, and word writes never change the lit paper.

WORD CELLS ARE NOT SLIPPED. Cells with plates 1-7 are excluded from lamp-dropout strip slips: their visible print changes only while unseen. Without this, the paper would visibly slip under a word at the very moment the word is readable, which breaks R6 and the trust behind it. BASE cells may still slip.

WAVES. The chase-time corridor wave (8 m/s, 10_synthesis.md §5) and the ink charge wave share arrival times, so the visible print and the green words travel together. The synthesis notes that a wave origin must shift with the 192 m title rebase. That cannot happen here, because the ink only exists once the player is in the map.

RELAY WAKE. The synthesis's 'reprint where it walked' and the WAKE plate share the same trigger and the same unseen window.

SAMENESS. Plates are uniform per cell (every face of the cell reads one texel), BASE is identical everywhere, and the print's period-4 roll phase is unchanged. A 3 m module differs only where a deliberate word, lure or WAKE has been written.

EMBOSS. The ghost emboss dial does not interact with the ink.
design.readability_and_accessibility:
SIZES, at FOV 76° on a 1080p display (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:227), about 14 px per degree:
- One glyph per roll strip per vertical repeat, in a box of about 0.45 × 0.55 m inside the 0.75 × 1.125 m repeat (LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC.md §5). That is about 8-10 instances per 3 m wall: 2 rows on Low 2.4 m walls, about 5 on Tall 5.4 m walls.
- Glyph height 0.55 m is about 30 px at 15 m and about 22 px at 20 m.
- Strokes 70-90 mm, about 4 px at 15 m.
- No stroke rhythm under 150 mm, to stay clear of the 37.5 mm print stripe and moiré (10_synthesis.md §7).
- Pre-mirror the art: PlanarFrame's u runs to the viewer's LEFT on every wall (t = cross(up, n), FrontRoomsSurface.shader:157-161).

TWO-LEVEL LEGIBILITY. Words come in families that differ in silhouette topology, not in detail:
- 'go' (open form): THROUGH, and the mirrored LURE;
- 'stop' (closed form): BLIND;
- 'threshold' (frame form): DOOR, GLASS;
- 'trace' (asymmetric smear): WAKE;
- 'radial': HEART.

Target distances:
- 'Something is written here' (a word brighter than BASE): within 30 m frontal.
- The family: within 15 m frontal, or within 6 m on a side wall. In a 3 m corridor the side wall sits at about 13° at 6 m, so the planner prefers frontal walls.
- The exact word and the lure's mirror: within 6 m. Approaching to check costs time, which is deliberate.

FOG. Fog is ExponentialSquared at density 0.014 (FrontRoomsLook.cs:19 and :32), so transmittance is 0.93 at 20 m, 0.84 at 30 m and 0.66 at 46 m (the far edge, BuildRadius × 24 − 2 m). Distant words read as presence.

COLOUR. ZnS:Cu green, about 530 nm. Meaning is carried by luminance contrast against the dark paper, not by hue, so it is safe for protan and deutan players.

OPTIONS:
- Ink brightness, 0.5-2×.
- High-contrast ink, which adds a dark halo.
- Optional ink audio cue (sound chat): a soft paper-tick per family when a word enters view within 8 m. Off by default.

PHOTOSENSITIVITY:
- Ink output is slew-limited on the CPU to at most 2.0 per second, so contrast reverses at 1 Hz or less.
- Stutter-lamp cells never show ink.
- Guttering strikes are at most 0.25 Hz.
- The chase wave ramps each cell over 0.6 s or more, with one wave per 120 s.
- Test the combined stimulus. The existing stutter mode already toggles on Perlin(t·23) (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1196), which can exceed 3 Hz. Visual and map chats must check it no matter what happens with the ink.

REDUCE MOTION:
- Reader lamps become a constant 0.08 instead of Guttering.
- Word charge is pinned at 0.8, so words stay readable without breathing.
- No chase wave: charge ramps over 1.5 s instead.
- WAKE still fades, since that is information, not motion.
- The T4 lure tell falls back to the mirror shape plus the lit-cell lure.
design.implementation_data_flow:
Paths below are relative to /Users/redwang/Desktop/ArtCenter/Fall26T7/EGAM-401A-01 Individual Game Project/Frontrooms3D/Assets.

1. BUILD (map chat). FrontRoomsMapWorld.BuildInto calls InkPlanner.Plan(chunkData, tier, seed, revision) before the cell loop. The planner writes chunk.ink[64] (plate, plus a 'second word' flag) and overrides chunk.lamp[i] (Auto cells only) to Guttering. BuildFixture (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:759 and :1082-1135) then builds those lamps. Add BuiltChunk.fixtureByCell[64] so the field can index lamps. Cost: under 0.1 ms per chunk (BFS over 64 cells or fewer).

2. HOOKUP. An InkField component subscribes to FrontRooms3DGame.MapRunStarted(map, relay) (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:608), so it gets the map and the Relay without new game code. It reads relay.Position, relay.State and StateChanged (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:114-141). It reads lamp levels through a new read-only FrontRoomsMapWorld.LampLevel(cell), or a bulk CopyLampLevels(span). The level is private today (Fixture at FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:85-100).

3. TICK (map chat). Run after TickFixtures (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:569). For each built Level 0 cell (at most 1600 at buildRadius 2, 3136 at radius 3): L̃, charge, glow, slew. Apply queued plate writes when R6 allows. WAKE logging and chase-wave arrivals happen here too. Pack the results into Color32[4096] at texel (cellX & 63) + (cellY & 63) × 64.
   - 192 m / 3 m = 64 cells, and the map root is always a multiple of 192 m (MAP_GENERATION.md:16; ModuleUnits.WorldPeriod, FrontRoomsModuleUnits.cs:29), so world-cell and map-cell indices agree.
   - The 5 × 5 area (40 cells) and the 7 × 7 area (56 cells) never alias.
   - Clear a chunk's texels when it is built and when it is dropped.
   - Cost target: 0.1 ms CPU or less.

4. TEXEL (proposal, agreed with visual chat). One RGBA8 texel per cell:
   - R: final ink glow, already gated on the CPU.
   - G: plate (bits 0-2), visible frame (bits 3-5, visual chat), ink-eligible (bit 6, which masks Office, start area and stream walls).
   - B: smoothed lamp level, for the visible print's flicker masking.
   - A: wave and transition parameter (visual chat).

5. UPLOAD (visual chat's driver). Texture2D 64 × 64, RGBA32, point filtered, Repeat, no mips. SetPixelData + Apply(false) each frame: 16 KB. Bind with Shader.SetGlobalTexture('_FR_CellState'). This is the same state texture the moving print needs, so there is one upload in total.

6. SHADER (visual chat, wallpaper materials with _FR_PRINT only):
   - Cell lookup: floor((positionWS.xz + normalWS.xz × 0.5) / 3) & 63, as ONE point Load.
   - The slice comes from G, and the existing print fetch supplies B.
   - Emission = _InkColor × B × (R / 255) × paper fibre/cavity mask × user gain, applied before fog.
   - Bias jamb faces (normals along the wall line) to avoid a floor() tie at x = 3k.
   - Extra cost: 1 Load and about 10 ALU per wallpaper pixel.

7. VISIBILITY. One per-camera visible-cell set, shared with the moving print (10_synthesis.md §5).

8. LOGGING. Add Event('ink', …) rows through FrontRooms3DGame.Event (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:1578), which already records the Relay's distance, so the metrics below can be measured.
