VISUAL CHAT: glyph art for 8 plates in the family rules, pre-mirrored for u-left, with the stroke and size minimums. BASE sub-pattern. Lure as a mirrored THROUGH. Readability lookdev captures at 1, 5, 10, 15 and 20 m, frontal and grazing.

VISUAL CHAT: Guttering lamp look (strike curve, lens emission), ink colour and intensity calibration against the tonemapper, the brightness/halo/reduce-motion settings, and the optional legend room in the title stream (FrontRoomsRoomStream).

SOUND CHAT (声音设计): a Guttering strike sound (starter tick + ballast catch), so reader cells can be heard 6-10 m before they are seen. Also an ink accent synced to the chase stinger for the wave reveal, and the optional per-family ink audio cue for accessibility. Under AUDIO_CONTRACT.md the print never touches audio files, so all of this goes through FMOD events the sound chat owns.

NARRATIVE CHAT: the slots listed in narrative_slots. The mechanic needs only that true marks are reliable, that WAKE comes from the Relay, and that lures are forged by something that cannot make ink hide in light.
narrative_slots: WHO WRITES THE TRUE MARKS, and how they know the layout beyond a junction and rewrite it after a revisit shift. The mechanic needs an author that knows the maze and keeps up with it.
WHY THE RELAY'S PASSAGE CHARGES PHOSPHOR (WAKE). For example, it carries or emits something that acts like light on the ink.
WHAT THE LURES ARE and why the forger cannot make ink that hides under light. This physical tell is the core of the trap literacy, so the fiction must keep it.
IN-WORLD NAMES for the 8 plates and the BASE sub-pattern (a Yellow Wallpaper 'sub-pattern' link is available, 10_synthesis.md §8). The mechanic only needs the functional meanings.
WHAT HEART MARKS: the zone's site and key. It matters more if doorsNeedKeys is ever turned on (FrontRoomsLevelProfile.cs:31).
WHY OFFICES HAVE NO INK. They are drywall, not wallpaper: illiterate zones as a deliberate contrast.

A DIEGETIC LEGEND: the dead-lamp room in the title stream, or a 1990-plausible artefact (stencilled maintenance marks, 1930s hobo-sign tradition, luminous paint). It is the same every run and teaches at most 2 words.
Period frame: copper-activated zinc sulfide (ZnS:Cu) luminous paint fits the 1990 era lock. Avoid strontium aluminate (1993-94) and anything that reads as a digital display.
playtest_metrics: Notice rate: share of first-run players who look at ink within 8 m by minute 3. Target ≥ 70%; if it is under 50%, add the one-time Flash().
Comprehension card sort after runs 1, 3 and 6: name the meaning of 6 words. Target ≥ 4 of 6 by run 6.

Fork choice at marked junctions during Hunt or Chase: rate of entering BLIND branches vs unmarked dead-end branches of the same size. Target: about equal on run 1, and BLIND entries down ≥ 50% relative by run 4.
Decision dwell: median time at marked vs unmarked junctions. Literate players should decide faster at marked junctions by run 5, without stopping longer than 2 s, because reading is risk.

Lure follow rate by run index and tier (Event('ink','lure_followed')). Target 60-80% at first exposure, under 30% by run 5. Under 10% at first exposure means the tell is too obvious; over 50% after 5 exposures means it is too weak.
Lure poisoning: follow rate of true THROUGH marks after the first lure is caught. Must stay ≥ 50%.
Hide-hole outcomes: DOOR·BLIND entries and whether the Relay found the player, split by whether it saw them within 1.5 s of the door crossing (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:294-300).
WAKE use: rate of entering a branch with bright WAKE (under 7 s) vs faint WAKE vs none. Expect bright < faint < none.

Survival A/B with the inkEnabled toggle, plotted by run index (time, zones and keys from the Caught screen, FrontRooms3DGame.cs:1495). Target: no difference on run 1, +20-30% median zones by run 6 with ink on.
Readability lookdev: glyph-family identification ≥ 90% at 10 m frontal and ≥ 60% at 20 m; exact word ≥ 90% at 6 m.

Photosensitivity: automated flash/pattern analysis of captured frames. Zero frames over 3 flashes per second, and no stripe reversals over 3 Hz across more than 25% of the screen, including the existing stutter lamps.
Performance, autopilot seeds 2554 and 20388 (LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC.md §8): InkField 0.15 ms CPU or less; no change to average fps beyond the synthesis budget (−1 fps, p99 +1.5 ms).
Density audit (Verify 100 seeds): mouths, words, forced lamps and lures per chunk per tier; target words on 5-8% of cells and total dark cells ≤ 25%.
failure_modes_and_exploits: The ink becomes a solved map and fluent players never die. Mitigations: words cover only 5-8% of cells; THROUGH means 'connects onward', not 'safe'; Offices are unreadable; chase speed reaches sprint speed at T4. Watch the survival A/B: if fluent players gain more than about 40%, cut words per chunk.
Lure poisoning: players distrust everything and ignore the ink. Mitigations: lures only ever forge THROUGH, stop-words are always true, the cap is 25%, and the lie is physical and consistent (R1/R7).

Lamp telegraph: players learn 'a Guttering lamp at a mouth means a word' and read lamps instead of ink. Acceptable, since it is still literacy. Natural failing and dead lamps plus the T4 failing increase dilute it. Lures on Steady lamps keep the ink itself worth reading.

Grazing illegibility in 3 m corridors: side walls past about 6 m are foreshortened to slivers. Fix by preferring frontal walls in planner step 5 and by the 'something written' brightness cue at range.

Photosensitivity stacking with the existing stutter lamp (Perlin(t·23), FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1196) and the moving print. The ink is slew-limited and stutter cells never show ink, but the combined test is still required.
The HUD's Relay distance makes WAKE pointless (MAP_GENERATION.md:32). Hide it or accept that WAKE only gives direction.

False safety: players camp in dark cells. The Relay sees by raycast with no light term (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:926-950). Teach this through deaths, and make sure the fiction doesn't promise that darkness hides you.

Stale or aliased texels: a dropped chunk's texels reused 192 m away, start-area or stream walls reading map cells, jamb faces landing on a cell line. Fix with clear-on-build/drop, the ink-eligible bit, and a jamb bias.

Revisit shift rewrites a word the player remembered and it reads as a lie. Intended as a change detector (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:612-616). Measure confusion in the card sort and, if needed, let the shifted chunk's first words appear only after a lamp strike.

Exploit: chaining door-rooms, since Wander never crosses shut doors (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:426 and :463). Bounded by door noise at 19.6 m, the follow-through-door rule, and DP08's faster door breaks (2.5 → 1.3 s).
Exploit: a caught lure marks a dead end. Intended: a caught lie is the reward for literacy.
Determinism in tests: planning depends on the tier, so a fixed runSeed can place different words depending on when chunks build. Tests must pin the tier.
Too few dark mouths in some seeds: the vignette guarantees the first sentence, and the planner forces reader lamps instead of hoping for natural failing ones.
references: The Exit 8 (Kotake Create, 2023) and Platform 8 (2024): a stable baseline, deviations that must be noticed, and knowledge as the only progression. This is the core model for BASE vs words vs lures.

Dark Souls message system (FromSoftware, 2011): a fixed vocabulary of words combined into templates, read across many sessions, and sometimes deceptive. The model for 'small vocabulary, combinable, some are traps'.
Chants of Sennaar (Rundisc, 2023): glyph languages learned purely from context and consequence.
Tunic (2022): an in-world script and manual that become readable through play.
Outer Wilds (Mobius, 2019): progression stored only in the player's head across loops. The 'no save-data power creep' rule.
Return of the Obra Dinn (2018): deduction from consistent, learnable rules.
Hobo signs (US, 1930s on): a real, period-safe folk vocabulary of chalk marks meaning safe, danger, dead end. A model for compact, functional glyphs.
Charlotte Perkins Gilman, The Yellow Wallpaper (1892): a sub-pattern that shows only in certain light (10_synthesis.md §8).
Haunted Mansion lightning portraits (1969), and Rensink, O'Regan & Clark change-blindness studies (1997/1999): changes masked by lamp flicker (10_synthesis.md §5).
Copper-activated zinc sulfide luminous paint: a period-correct phosphor for the 1990 era lock (10_synthesis.md §6).
Left 4 Dead AI Director, with its build-up, peak and relax pacing: the source of the chase-wave cooldown and event-tier pacing (10_synthesis.md §5).
Dark Deception (the project's primary reference): a maze chase in which reading the route under pressure decides survival.
Project docs: Documentation/research/wallpaper_motion/10_synthesis.md, Documentation/LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC.md, Documentation/MAP_GENERATION.md.

strengths: Clearest player promise of the four: green in the dark leads to new ground. A first-time player can learn it in under a minute, and the forced-dead cell 6-9 m past the start door teaches it head-on while the Relay is still dormant.

It is the only design that adds a real decision inside the chase. The chase wave sags the lights ahead of a fleeing player, and the marks re-point to doors leading away from the Relay. Sprint becomes sprint, read the end wall, pick a door and shut it. That uses the door verb (2.5 + 0.25 s break) that today goes underused.

The lamp-sag wave outrunning the player (8 m/s against a 5.5 m/s sprint) is a strong horror image: the building darkens ahead of you while it shows you the way. It sits squarely in the synthesis's event tier.
Help and lure are honest about each other. Calm mode ignores the Relay, so it can lead you into a wandering one, and following it speeds up tier escalation. The ink is a bet, not a safety net.
The hint strength is measured, not guessed. On-route-only marks give about 2x random and about half of perfect knowledge, and the design names and fixes the GPS-creep and beacon ping-pong traps.

Readability is designed for first person: decision glyphs go on end walls at junctions (14 px at 20 m), side walls are confirmation within 6-8 m, and meaning is carried by shape, so it works for colour-blind players.
STOP bars on dead-end mouths cut the cheapest death in a maze chase (getting cornered in a 1-cell alcove), and the design tracks it as a metric.
weaknesses: Always truthful and always helpful at T0-T3. Risk: after a few runs the green reads as UI, not dread. Most of the 'it knows the building, it doesn't promise safety' feeling rests on fiction, not mechanics.

It leaves the HUD 'RELAY nn M' readout alone (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:1544). With exact distance on screen, pressure mode adds little tension, and the calm-to-pressure switch also leaks that the Relay is nearby.
The wave rewrites marks to safe doors during every eligible chase, which may push the chase escape rate high. The only guard is an 80% cap metric and a 90 s cooldown.

Four messages plus GROUND, two modes, sags and tier tables make the authoring and tuning heavy. The calm/pressure mode switch is invisible to the player, so the same chevron means different things at different times.
Office blind zones (13.6% of cells) and dark clusters with blank ink may read as bugs, not rules.
graft_ideas: Use this as the base: on-route-only FLOW, HERE brackets, STOP at dead-end mouths, the forced-dead first read, the chase wave carrying the lamp dip and the pressure commit together, and the 1.6-2.2x hint-strength target.

strengths: Strongest pure horror fantasy: you read where the Relay WAS, never where it IS. Every reading is stale and costs 1.5-3 s standing in the dark, which builds dread instead of comfort.
R13, retiring the 'RELAY nn M' HUD line (confirmed at FrontRooms3DGame.cs:1544), is the most important pacing fix any of the four designs proposes. It makes any ink worth reading.
EAR ('it heard you') is a great beat: the sprint becomes a visible confession. It teaches the noise system diegetically and is the one deliberate in-view change, which respects the noticeable tier.
The OMEN wave delays each arrival by 3.3-5.5 s and shows where the Relay re-entered. It turns the cheap 'it teleported behind me' moment into an anticipation beat.
BREACH marks (a permanent 'this door will not shut') make door scarcity readable over a run as door breaks speed up.
The silhouette of the dark Relay against glowing paper is a free scare. 'Darkness never hides you' is kept rigorously (the sight ray has no light term).
weaknesses: By its own statement it adds nothing during a chase: no EAR in Chase, plus the lag and the unseen gate. The chase stays sprint-only, which misses the brief's key question.

Five mark kinds (wake, knot, ear, breach, omen), plus adaptation, plus a hollow decoy tell. That is a lot to learn from ambiguous green blobs read at range only as 'how much'. The comprehension target is ambitious.
The intel is indirect. Knowing where it walked 30 s ago does not turn easily into a route choice in an endless maze without a map, so many reads may feel like flavour.
Wander and Arrive tweaks (biasing wander routes across dark cells, lit preference, backtracking, decoys) change the Relay's behaviour to serve the ink, which is risky to balance.
T5 decoys push the player back toward the real Relay. Effective, but they may feel unfair given how hard the near-read hollow tell is.
graft_ideas: Retire the HUD distance readout and move it behind an accessibility assist. This is required for any ink design to matter.
EAR bloom on accepted noise (coalesced to once per 4 s) as the one allowed in-view change: 'it heard you, leave quietly'.
Permanent BREACH marks on Relay-broken doors, so the wayfinding ink stops sending players to dead doors and the run's damage stays visible.
OMEN wave plus a delayed arrival at release and leash relays, sharing the wave machinery with the chase wave.
The adaptation scalar (glow x (0.35 + 0.65A)): seeing THAT a cell is marked is free, reading WHAT it says costs standing in the dark.

strengths: BLIND/THROUGH at junction mouths answers the question a fleeing player actually has: does this branch dead-end? It gives the chase a real fork decision, and DOOR·BLIND adds a hide-or-coffin choice.

The lie tell is elegant and physical: a mark that stays lit under a lamp is forged. It rewards understanding the ink's one law. Only THROUGH is ever forged, so the 'stop' words stay trustworthy and lures do not poison trust.
Knowledge-only progression across runs, in the Exit 8 / Outer Wilds mould, fits a repeated-run horror game and keeps the run-to-run power curve flat.
Chunk-local planning is exact and cheap. The teaching vignette guarantees a BLIND/THROUGH pair at the first junction in every run, while the Relay cannot yet know where the player is.
WAKE brightness as age gives readable recent-threat information without saying where it is now.
weaknesses: Learnability is the main problem: 8 plates, no glossary, and fluency targeted at 6-10 runs. First-run players in a class playtest get almost nothing except 'creepy green', and several words (HEART, GLASS, DOOR·BLIND) only appear at T1-T2.
Forced Guttering reader lamps at every word make lamp patterns the real tell. Players will read troffers, not ink, which weakens the 'every 3 m module looks the same' baseline.
Lures arrive at T2 (about 4 min), before most players have the lit-lamp rule. Early betrayal may make the ink feel random rather than learnable.

Identifying the exact word needs 6 m or less and the family needs 15 m frontal. In a chase you will not get close enough to tell DOOR from GLASS, so the chase value rests on the coarse go/stop silhouette families.
With no route sense, a THROUGH says 'connects onward' but not toward anything new, so calm play gets little pull.
graft_ideas: Silhouette families by topology (open = go, closed = stop, frame = threshold) as the glyph-design rule for FLOW, STOP and HERE, so the shape reads before the detail.
DOOR·BLIND hide-hole semantics: mark door-rooms that are closed pockets, as a calm-mode secondary message (Wander never crosses shut doors).
The physical lie tell (glows under a lit lamp) as the late-tier 'unreliable ink' variant for wayfinding R8, forging only the go-type marks.
Exclude word cells from lamp-dropout strip slips, so the visible paper never moves under a readable mark.

strengths: Pull the tube is a genuine new verb with a clear price: a 1.2 s hold, 11-22 m of noise, permanent darkness that draws Wander. Players get a strategic risk/reward decision, and lamps pulled as bait is a nice emergent use.

Darkness gets real costs: Relay wander drifts toward dead lamps, sprint noise is x1.25 where no ballast hum covers it. Dark becomes dangerous ground, which fits Backrooms dread better than any stealth reading.
The fresh-vs-starved charge physics is learnable ('the paper only remembers what it was shown') and stays constant across tiers, so early lessons stay true.
The first-dark beat (a lamp dies in view and a ladder blooms toward a door 6 cells or fewer away) is a strong, legible teaching moment.
Escalating lamp death over tiers makes a darker, more hunted late maze: an atmospheric horror curve.
weaknesses: Reads are scarce and fiddly: failing-ballast gasps of 0.1-0.5 s, legible sightings every 20-40 s at best, and side walls are only readable within about 8 m. Players may find it frustrating rather than tense.
The sign grammar (which of 4 wallpaper rolls glows, as a brightness ramp) is abstract. Polarity misreads (bright end = danger) are a named risk.
Almost nothing is offered during a chase: the pull is too slow and loud to use, and the chase wave is a one-shot flare that then drains charge. The chase stays sprint-only.
It changes the Relay's core behaviour (dark-wander weights) and adds noise multipliers and walking noise at T3: wide balance changes for a hint system.
It leaves the HUD distance readout in place, and a new verb with prompts and a lens collider adds scope for a student project.
graft_ideas: Charge physics with a visible fresh/starved distinction, as a learnable rule for why dark clusters are blank (fixes wayfinding's 'reads as a bug' failure mode).
The in-view first-dark lamp death (3 dips at 2 Hz or less, then a ballast pop) as wayfinding's teaching beat instead of a pre-dead cell. It ties 'light died, ink appeared' together.
The drought breaker: promote an unseen steady lamp ahead to failing after 60 s with no legible read, outside Chase/Hunt.
Optional late-run lever, the pull-the-tube verb, as a loud, permanent way to buy a reading spot. Keep it out of the core loop until playtests show beacon drought.

judged.rationale:
Through the player-experience and horror-pacing lens, Afterglow Blazes (wayfinding) wins.

**Why it wins.** It is the only design that turns the ink into a real chase decision. The chase wave sags the lights ahead of a fleeing player, and the walls re-point to a door that leads away from the Relay. The chase stops being sprint-only: the player now chooses which door to read and shut. It is also the easiest to learn. The first-run lesson is a single idea (green in the dark leads to new ground), taught at a forced dead lamp while the Relay is dormant. Its hint strength is measured, about 2x random and half of perfect knowledge, and it explicitly guards against GPS creep. It keeps the subliminal / noticeable / event tiers intact: lit modules stay mute, commits happen only when unseen, and the wave is the rate-limited event.

**Its gaps.** It is too reliably helpful, and it ignores the 'RELAY nn M' HUD readout, which I confirmed still renders every frame at FrontRooms3DGame.cs:1544. That readout undercuts any intel-based tension.

**The other three:**
- **Afterglow Wake (threat_intel)** has the best dread: you read stale intel at the cost of standing in the dark. It also has the single most important fix: retire the HUD distance. But it adds nothing during a chase, and its five mark types are hard to learn from green blobs.
- **Afterglow Grammar (anomaly_literacy)** has the best chase-fork semantics (BLIND/THROUGH) and an elegant lie tell. But it needs 6-10 runs to become fluent, and first-run players get little from it.
- **Afterglow Ledger (light_economy)** adds a real verb and makes darkness costly. But its reads are scarce and fiddly, it offers nothing in a chase, and it changes Relay behaviour broadly.

**Recommended grafts onto the wayfinding base:**
- Remove the HUD distance (move it behind an assist).
- Add an EAR bloom ('it heard you') and permanent BREACH marks, so routes skip dead doors.
- Add the OMEN wave on arrivals and the adaptation cost on reading.
- Use topology-coded glyph families (go, stop, threshold).
- Add DOOR·BLIND hide-hole marks.
- Use the physical 'glows under a lit lamp' lie tell as the late-tier unreliable-ink variant.
- Add the fresh-vs-starved charge rule, so blank dark clusters read as a rule, not a bug.
- Add the in-view first-dark lamp death as the teaching beat, plus the drought breaker.

The project was not modified.

strengths: The core marks (WAKE, KNOT, EAR, BREACH) run entirely on public hunter API I checked: Position, Moving, ListenPoint, Relays and StateChanged (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:114-141), plus the public DoorBroken event (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:63, raised in BreakDoor at :1056-1065). A new ledger class can poll these with no hunter edits.

Its only required private-API change is the one every design needs: Fixture.level, which is computed for all built fixtures every frame (TickFixtures, FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1164-1168). It correctly warns that light.enabled is gated by lightRadius and must not be used.
Cheapest shader of the four: one point LOAD, a threshold on the B growth field, and fwidth anti-aliasing. It needs no extra glyph slices and no per-face direction logic.
Storage is sparse (a 512-entry Dictionary) and survives chunk drops. Breaches map 1:1 onto brokenDoors. It is deterministic (choices hashed from seed and Relays), which fits the P3 gate.
It is robust for every seed because it is driven by traffic, not topology. It does not depend on the maze's loop structure or zone layout.
The slewed darkness gate turns the mode-1 Perlin(t*23) stutter (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1196, verified) into one swell, so the ink cannot become an antiphase strobe.
weaknesses: OMEN means splitting Arrive (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:390-421) into a choice plus a delayed commit, and appending HunterState.Arriving. That touches release timing (MAP_GENERATION.md:34 and its tests), the sound director and the rig, and the AUDIO_CONTRACT. It is the riskiest change in the package.

Tier hooks in Wander (lit preference, backtracking, the T1 bias) and the T5 decoy writer are more hunter edits, and they change the shared Next() rng sequence. Existing autopilot baselines would move.
It depends on the shared visibility BFS plus frustum service, which does not exist in the project yet. VISUAL_CHAT_TASKS lists it as WG2 and still running.
Its value scales with how often the Relay walks through dark cells (about 18%), so some seeds and stretches give very little intel. Tall halls are spill-flooded, as the design itself admits.
It needs cross-chat changes: removing the HUD's distance line (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:1544, verified) and dropping the synthesis's visible-layer 'Relay wake reprint'.
graft_ideas: Poll the public hunter API from a separate ledger class instead of editing hunter internals.
Gate on a slewed darkness value (rise 0.4 s, fall 0.08 s) so stutter lamps can never strobe the ink.
Threshold a nested B growth field so one glyph art set carries every intensity level.
Keep marks in a sparse dictionary that survives chunk drops, with breaches as permanent edges.
Commit on lamp falling edges, reusing the same edge the sound director already turns into 'Tick'.

strengths: Its code citations are the most accurate of the four. Doors and windows are created only at height changes on tree or gate edges (FrontRoomsMap.cs:354-355, 609). Fixture.level is computed beyond lightRadius. Sight has no light term (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:926-931). Wander does not pass through doors (:426, 463). All of these check out.

Leaf pruning for STOP is the right algorithm for this maze. Non-tree edges roll Open or Arch (Standard about 18%, Low 50%, Tall 70%), so the maze has loops, and pruning stays exact where a branch-BFS would not.

Targets use only features that do not change with revision (zones, border edges, keys), and the per-cell temperament hash also works for unbuilt cells. So it survives the revisit shift and works for every seed. It has a defined fallback to the built boundary.
Field rebuilds are event-driven, rate-limited to 2 Hz, and run over at most 1,600 cells. Explicit CPU and GPU budgets are tied to the synthesis perf gate (58.7 fps, p99 19.4 ms).
It backs its density and progress claims with an offline Python port of the generator (12-16 seeds), which is unusual evidence for a proposal.
An unset global means no ink, so edit mode and the Level Designer stay safe.
weaknesses: It has the largest map-chat surface. Besides target and Relay fields, route descent, a commit gate, mode switching, sags and waves, it needs a new LampDip multiplier inside TickFixtures that really dims lights, which also feeds sound and lighting.
It needs private game state: zonesVisited is a private readonly HashSet (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:162). It also needs new ZoneEntered, ChunkBuilt and ChunkDropped events.

PassageBetween does several dictionary and hash-set lookups per edge. A bucket Dijkstra over about 6,400 edges in Mono could exceed the 0.4 ms estimate. It should cache an adjacency array per chunk, and rebuilds must not land in the same frame as chunk builds, which are already the p99 spike source.
The shader must resolve direction per face and needs either 16 extra glyph slices or a second branch fetch, so the visual ask is moderate.
It depends on the same unbuilt visibility service, and its many tuning interactions (stickiness, mode hysteresis, rate limits) make it harder to test.
graft_ideas: Use leaf pruning for dead-end detection, with the built-area boundary counted as open, because the maze has loops.
Choose only targets that do not change with revision, so routes survive chunk shifts.
Expose LampLevel(cell) and LampMode(cell), where LampMode is a pure seed hash that also works for unbuilt cells.
Ship a debug map overlay plus a 100-seed truth audit, and add an ink-follower autopilot policy.
Keep the ink constant in B across print keyframes, so print jumps never change what glows.

strengths: Its most portable technical idea: the information lives in a per-roll emission mask computed in the shader, with roll = floor(worldAlong/0.75) & 3. This adds no glyph slices, makes mirrored UVs harmless, and fully separates information from narrative art.
It correctly uses logical f.level and ignores the start-area hold and the distance fade, and it cites the lines it relies on (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1171-1175).
The per-frame charge simulation is cheap, under 0.1 ms. The spill table is rebuilt only on door, glass and chunk events.
Monotone tier re-cuts from a fixed per-cell u are deterministic, and darker maps actually turn off more lights, which slightly reduces GPU cost.
weaknesses: It has the most new gameplay code. The pull-tube verb needs a new aim target, because the lens collider is removed in BuildFixture (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:~1094, verified). It also needs per-cell pulledLamps persistence, stacked noise, new prompts and three new sound events.
It changes temperament odds per zone and tier, and re-cuts built fixtures at runtime. That conflicts with the visual chat owning flicker odds (LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC.md:76) and needs sign-off.
Hunter edits (dark-weighted Wander), sprint and step noise multipliers in FrontRooms3DGame, and a beats director with a drought breaker spread the risk across files the map chat owns.
Readability depends on failing-ballast gasps of 0.1-0.5 s against a 0.25 s gate delay. That timing is a fragile tuning surface, and if it fails, the dependency moves to the pull verb.
Tarjan bridges plus a 0-1 BFS at 1 Hz are cheap, but they are a second graph pipeline alongside the visibility BFS.
graft_ideas: Use the world-position roll-mask sign grammar in the shader instead of authored glyph slices.
Ignore the hold and fade when reading lamp level for the ink.
Use the hyperbolic (second-order) decay curve for physically plausible afterglow.
Add a drought breaker that promotes an unseen steady lamp to failing, so readable cells keep a minimum density.

strengths: A build-time, chunk-local InkPlanner on cached MapChunk data is deterministic over (seed, chunk, revision) and costs under 0.1 ms per chunk, with no per-frame graph work.
The single scheduler and shared visibility set with the print's discrete jumps avoid duplicated systems.
It uses MapRunStarted (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:39, 608, verified) to hook up without new game code.
It logs telemetry through the existing Event() path.
weaknesses: Its correctness premise is wrong in this codebase. It claims every chunk is a spanning tree, so dead-end tests are exact. But Resolve turns non-tree edges into Open or Arch at 18-70% (FrontRoomsMap.cs:94-96, 360), so branches loop back. A branch-BFS that never re-enters J can merge sibling branches, and the 16-cell cap can label a closed 16-plus-cell pocket THROUGH. That breaks the 'true words' contract.
Planning depends on the tier, so the same seed can place different words depending on when a chunk builds. That breaks the P3 determinism gate (the design admits this).

It is the heaviest visual ask: 8 plates x 4 keyframes = 32 slices, which takes over the whole planned print sheet and leaves visible motion only 4 keyframes. It needs mirrored glyph art, a new Guttering lamp mode, and a rule that word cells are never slipped by the print.
Forcing 3-5 extra dark lamps per chunk changes the lamp distribution, which the visual chat owns. It also adds work inside BuildInto, the frame that already sets p99.
Words are written at build time, so runtime changes (broken doors, broken glass changing a branch's meaning) need patch-up logic beyond the DoorBroken case.
graft_ideas: Run cheap word or feature placement once per chunk build, keyed on (seed, chunk, revision), with tier pinned for determinism.
Use one shared scheduler and visibility set for print jumps and ink commits.
Prefer frontal walls when placing decision glyphs, because side walls foreshorten too much in 3 m corridors.
Hook up through the MapRunStarted event instead of new game wiring.

judged.rationale: Through the feasibility and cost lens, threat_intel has the cheapest, least-coupled core. WAKE, KNOT, EAR and BREACH can ship as one new map-chat class that polls public hunter API I checked in the code (Position, Moving, ListenPoint, Relays, StateChanged, and DoorBroken in FrontRoomsMapWorld). Its only private dependency is exposing Fixture.level, which all four designs need. Its shader is a single LOAD plus a threshold, with no glyph slices or per-face direction logic. Because it is driven by Relay traffic, it is robust for every seed and zone layout. Its risky parts are optional and can be phased in later: the OMEN Arrive split with a new HunterState, the tier hooks in Wander, and decoys. wayfinding is a close second. It has the best-verified facts, offline simulation evidence, and the right algorithm for a maze with loops (leaf pruning). But it needs the largest map-chat build: target and Relay fields, route descent, mode switching, a LampDip lamp API, sags and waves. It also needs private game state (zonesVisited), and its Dijkstra over dictionary-backed PassageBetween could exceed its 0.4 ms estimate unless adjacency is cached. light_economy's shader grammar (a world-position roll mask) is the best technical idea to graft. Its cost is a new player verb that needs a lens collider the code removes, runtime temperament re-cuts that need visual-chat sign-off, and hunter and noise changes. anomaly_literacy scores lowest. Its 'every chunk is a spanning tree, so dead-end tests are exact' premise is false: Resolve makes non-tree edges Open or Arch at 18-70%. Its planning depends on tier, which breaks determinism, and it uses up the whole 32-slice print sheet. All four depend on the shared visibility BFS and the _FR_PRINT and _FR_CellState work. Neither exists in the main project yet: the print work is still running in a private copy, and VISUAL_CHAT_TASKS lists the visibility system (WG2) as still running. That is the common critical-path risk to schedule first. Files checked: Frontrooms3D/Assets/Scripts/FrontRoomsMap/FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs, FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs, FrontRoomsMap.cs, Assets/Scripts/FrontRooms3DGame.cs, Documentation/research/wallpaper_motion/10_synthesis.md, Documentation/MAP_GENERATION.md and Documentation/VISUAL_CHAT_TASKS.md.

strengths: Best real-world and period anchor of the four. Photoluminescent ZnS:Cu egress marking (FAA floor-path rules after 1983, glow-in-the-dark exit signs) is pre-1990 and reads as plausible building fabric, not magic UI. It fits the 1990 era lock with no stretching.

Leaves the narrative chat a clean hole. The mechanic needs only 'why does the paper know new ground and react to the Relay'. Who printed it, what GROUND depicts and whether it lies are all left open, and lying is parked until T4 or later.

Fits Backrooms tone without breaking 'you are lost'. Lit modules stay mute and identical, and the hint lives only in failing light, which is the Backrooms' signature decay. R8/R12 also rule out the stealth-game myth that dark is safe, so the fiction can't contradict the Relay code.

Most scope-friendly path for weekly deliverables. There is no new player verb and no hunter rewrite. It can be cut into clean weekly slices: (1) glow gate on natural dead/failing lamps, (2) GROUND plus FLOW from a BFS, (3) STOP via leaf pruning, (4) sags, (5) the chase wave. Each slice is shippable and demoable.

Very strong presentation story. In one image, a lit corridor shows nothing and the dead troffer shows green chevrons. The simulation numbers (about 2x random, half of perfect knowledge) are deck-ready proof that it is a hint, not a GPS. That matches Red's 'the deck argues for my game' rule.
The 'opposite masking phases' point (print changes in the dark, ink changes in the light) is an elegant, slide-sized explanation of the sandwich: two layers, two legal change windows.
weaknesses: R10 freezes the ink against the moving print (B is constant across keyframes). The deck then shows two systems side by side rather than one sandwich, which weakens the 'moving print under paper' showcase.

The ink is omniscient: it knows the nearest unvisited zone and which door leads away from the Relay. The narrative chat must justify an all-knowing guide, which pushes the fiction toward 'the building helps you', a softer reading of Backrooms dread.
Following the ink speeds up tier escalation. That is a good risk/reward, but it is a coupling Red must explain and tune.

The spec carries many SP numbers, four message types, sags, waves and a LampDip API (new lamp logic that also touches visual-chat-owned flicker odds). A presentation version must cut hard to stay 'say it once'.
Chevrons echo the old wallpaper chevron relief that the synthesis removes or ghosts. This could confuse the visual story unless it is made deliberate.
graft_ideas: Keep as the spine: on-route-only beacons (R6, backed by the ping-pong simulation finding), the commit gate, and 'dark is never cover'.
Use the simulation table (random 3.1 / ink 6.1 / perfect 12.5 thresholds per 100 cells) as one deck slide proving 'hint, not GPS'.
Use the real egress-marking precedent in the research frame, with original photos per the research rule.

strengths: Best physics fiction. Hyperbolic (second-order recombination) afterglow decay is the real ZnS:Cu behaviour. 'Fresh glow bright, starved glow faint' gives the narrative chat a memorable, true-to-material rule ('the paper only remembers what it was shown').

Leaves the narrative chat the most room. The meaning is carried by which 0.75 m rolls glow, not by glyph shape, so glyph content is completely free for narrative (only symmetric or direction-free). Narrative even gets the option of glyphs that 'rewrite themselves' between gasps.
Pulling the tube is a tactile, period-plausible 1990 office-maintenance verb. It deepens the Backrooms fluorescent-light identity, and lamps that only get worse fit the decay fantasy of Level 0.

Shows the sandwich well in a presentation. 'Light charges, dark reveals' is literally a lighting diagram. Roll strips are the print system's own seams, so ink and print share one structure, and the shared chase wave ties both layers.
The one-line pitch 'light is the price of a hint' is the plain, spoken language Red's deck logic favours.
weaknesses: Largest scope sprawl for a student term. It adds a new interaction verb (lens collider or DescribeAt, persistence, escalating noise), Relay wander weighting, dark-noise multipliers, a tier temperament re-cut, a beats director, a drought breaker and three new sound events. That is several chats' work before the ink itself can be shown.
Changes flicker odds per zone and tier, which are the visual chat's numbers (LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC:76). That is a cross-chat negotiation on the critical path.
Roll-brightness ramps (0.25/0.5/0.75/1.0) are abstract. They are hard to read in a still or on a projected slide, and need video to land.
Failing-ballast gasps of 0.1-0.5 s are a fragile read. The base experience depends on tuning that may not converge in a weekly cadence.
It is still wayfinding (WAY/SHUT) underneath, so it competes with rather than complements the wayfinding direction.
graft_ideas: Graft the hyperbolic decay curve and the 'fresh vs starved' rule into the winner's charge model. This gives a truthful physics slide and narrative hook at near-zero cost.
Graft 'meaning in luminance/roll mask, glyph shape owned by narrative'. It decouples level design from narrative art, so the narrative chat can change glyphs without breaking the mechanic.

Graft the first-dark beat (a lamp dies in view over 1.5 s with a ballast pop and the ink blooms) as the winner's start beat instead of a pre-dead cell. It is a far stronger reveal moment and a better demo clip.
Keep pull-the-tube as a stretch goal or late-term verb, not the core.

strengths: Strongest single presentation asset. An 8-plate glossary sheet (go/stop/threshold/trace/radial families) is perfect for Figma and the deck, and readable from the back of the room.

The lure tell is the most elegant demonstration of the sandwich's law. Real ink must vanish under light, so 'a mark that glows under a lit lamp is a lie' turns the rendering rule into the gameplay rule, and that one image explains the whole layer system.
Exit 8 and hobo signs anchor it well in the Backrooms-adjacent liminal genre and in a period-safe folk vocabulary. The Gilman sub-pattern link is natural.

Scope is cheaper at the core: a chunk-local, deterministic InkPlanner (BFS over 64 cells or fewer) with no global Dijkstra, and the cleanest integration with the print-array layout (4 frames x 8 plates = the planned 8x4 sheet).
The 'no save data, knowledge is progression' rule is clean and honest for an endless run.
weaknesses: Takes over narrative's territory the most. It fixes the vocabulary meanings, implies an author who knows and rewrites the maze, and invents a forger. The narrative chat inherits 'who writes, who forges' as givens rather than open slots.
Its central claim (fluency over 6-10 runs, lure tells only learnable after tier 2) is nearly impossible to validate with student playtesters in weekly cycles. Testers rarely play 6+ runs.
Eight plates of glyph art, a new Guttering lamp mode, lures, a teaching vignette and a title-stream legend room is a lot of authored art and logic for one element.
Forcing 3-5 extra reader lamps per chunk plus lures that glow in lit cells weakens the 'every 3 m module looks the same' rule more than the others. Players may learn to read lamps instead of ink.
A full language with a forger risks feeling like a puzzle game layered on a chase game. It may dilute Dark Deception-style chase pressure.
graft_ideas: Graft the lure physical tell ('glows under a lit lamp means not ink') as the winner's late-tier 'ink may lie' option. It is a consistent, learnable lie instead of an arbitrary one, and it doubles as the best sandwich explainer slide.
Graft the glyph-family silhouette rule (go/stop/threshold differ in topology, not detail) as the readability spec for the winner's FLOW/HERE/STOP glyphs.
Graft the optional title-stream legend room (one dead lamp, the same every run) as a diegetic teaching moment and a presentation shot.
Graft the 'word cells excluded from strip slips' rule so the visible print never slips under a readable message.

strengths: Most horror-forward fiction. The monster leaves a luminous ledger, the paper 'hears' you, and its dark body silhouettes against glowing paper. These are strong Backrooms-entity beats and good scare clips.
Breach marks (permanent, always true) are a neat diegetic record of the run, and EAR is a vivid 'it heard you' teaching beat.
Its MVP can be cheap: WAKE and KNOT only poll public hunter state (Position, Moving, ListenPoint), with no hunter change needed.
Correctly flags that the HUD's 'RELAY nn M' readout makes any threat ink pointless. That is a valuable project-level catch.
weaknesses: Fixes the fiction's core: the Relay writes the ink. The narrative chat must explain why a light-indifferent monster writes phosphor without light while lamps only charge it, which leaves much less room for narrative.
Drops or randomises the synthesis's visible 'Relay wake reprint'. That removes an already-planned sandwich feature and breaks the presented story of the moving print.
Weak in a static presentation. A fading, aging trail and the adaptation mechanic only read in video, and the meaning ('how old, which way') sits in subtle brightness gradients.
Scope reaches into the hunter: an appended HunterState.Arriving, delayed arrivals, tier hooks in Wander, a T5 decoy writer and HUD removal. That is a lot of cross-system change for one element.
An honest/stale/muddled/lying arc over five tiers is hard to playtest within a term. The adaptation dwell mechanic also risks reading as 'stand in the dark to be safe', even though it is not.
graft_ideas: Graft the permanent BREACH mark (broken doors scarred in ink) into the winner. It is cheap, always true and tells the player 'this door won't shut'.
Graft the backlit silhouette beat (the Relay's dark body against glowing paper) as the winner's scare payoff and the answer to 'why linger in a glowing corridor'.
Graft the HUD fix: move 'RELAY nn M' behind an assist, so any diegetic ink has value.
Keep the synthesis's visible Relay wake reprint, rather than this design's removal of it, so 'print = where it walked, ink = where to go' becomes a clean two-layer deck line.

judged.rationale:
I judged the four designs on fit with the fiction and the project: the Backrooms IP and 1990 era lock, how much room each leaves the narrative chat, scope for weekly student deliverables, and how well it shows the sandwich wallpaper in a presentation.

**Afterglow Blazes (wayfinding) wins at 8.** It has the cleanest real anchor: ZnS:Cu egress marking that glows when the power fails, which predates 1990. It leaves the narrative chat the most important slots open: who printed the ink and why it knows the way. It adds no new player verb and no hunter rewrite, and it can be split into demoable weekly slices. It also has the clearest deck argument: one image of a mute lit corridor beside a dead troffer with green chevrons, plus simulation numbers showing it is a hint, not a GPS.

**Afterglow Ledger (light_economy) is second at 7.** It has the truest phosphor physics and leaves narrative the most freedom over glyph shape, because meaning is carried by which rolls glow. But it adds a new verb, Relay wander weighting, noise multipliers and per-tier changes to flicker odds the visual chat owns. That is too much scope sprawl for the core.

**Afterglow Grammar (anomaly_literacy) scores 6.5.** It has the best presentation assets: the 8-glyph sheet and the 'a mark that glows under a lit lamp is a lie' tell, which turns the rendering rule into gameplay. But it takes over narrative's job (a fixed vocabulary, an author and a forger). Its cross-run fluency goal also can't realistically be validated with student playtesters.

**Afterglow Wake (threat_intel) scores 6.** It is the most horror-forward, but it fixes the fiction ('the Relay writes the ink'). It deletes the synthesis's planned visible Relay wake reprint, reaches deep into the hunter, and mostly reads only in video.

The winner should take these grafts:
- **From light_economy:** the hyperbolic afterglow decay and its 'fresh vs starved' rule, the principle that meaning lives in the luminance mask so glyph shapes stay with narrative, and the in-view first-dark lamp death as the start beat.
- **From anomaly_literacy:** the physical lure tell as the late-tier 'ink may lie' rule, and silhouette-family glyph rules for readability.
- **From threat_intel:** permanent BREACH scars, the backlit Relay silhouette, and the HUD distance readout moved behind an assist. Keep the synthesis's visible wake reprint, so the deck can say 'the print shows where it walked; the ink shows where to go'.

# Afterglow Blazes: level design proposal for the phosphorescent wallpaper print

Status: proposal only, 2026-10-02. Nothing is implemented. Owner of this document: level design (关卡设计). Paths are relative to `Frontrooms3D/`. Every gameplay number is marked **SP** (a starting point for playtest). Code facts are given as file:line.

Base design: **Afterglow Blazes (wayfinding)**, which scored highest overall (23 / 30). Grafts taken from the others:
- **threat_intel:** retire the HUD distance readout, permanent BREACH scars, the EAR bloom, and the backlit Relay silhouette.
- **light_economy:** fresh-vs-starved charge physics, a first-dark beat where the lamp dies in view, the drought breaker, and the idea that meaning sits in a world-space mask while narrative owns the glyph substance.
- **anomaly_literacy:** glyph families by silhouette, the physical lie tell, and no strip slips under a readable mark.

---

## 1. Pitch and the player decision it adds

A hidden ZnS:Cu underprint in the Level 0 wallpaper shows only where a cell's own lamp is dead, dying or sagging. Lit walls show nothing, so every lit 3 m module stays identical. In the dark, the paper points:
- **FLOW** (chevrons) lies along the best route to the nearest threshold into a zone you have not visited.
- **HERE** (brackets) frames that door or window.
- **STOP** (bars) marks the mouth of a dead-end pocket.
- **BREACH** (a bracket crossed out) marks a door the Relay broke, which will never shut again.

When the Relay starts a chase, the lamps sag in a wave that runs down the corridors ahead of the player, and the marks in that wave re-point to doors leading away from it.

**The ink knows the building. It does not know the monster.** In calm play it ignores the Relay, so it can lead you straight into a wandering one. Following it also roughly doubles your rate of new thresholds, which speeds up tier escalation.

Decisions it adds:

| When | Decision | Cost of each answer |
|---|---|---|
| Calm | Follow the green to new ground, or go my own way? | Following means faster progress, faster escalation and a blind walk past the Relay. Ignoring it means slower progress and more dead ends. |
| Chase | Which door does the wave point at, and do I spend time reading the end wall? | Reading costs metres at 4.2 m/s. A shut door buys 2.5 s + 0.25 s. |
| Junction | Is that branch a pocket (STOP)? | Entering a pocket during a hunt is the cheapest death in the maze. |
| T4+ (optional) | Is this mark real? It is glowing under a lit lamp. | A forged FLOW leads into a dead end. |

## 2. Rules

1. **Gate.** `G = C × smoothstep(0.55, 0.15, Ls) × weight` (SP).
   - `Ls` is the cell's own lamp level, low-passed with τ 0.35 s (SP). The lamp level is `Fixture.level` (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:98), set from `Level()` at :1168.
   - It must never be read from `light.enabled` or `light.intensity`. Those are cut by the distance fade and the start-area hold (:1171-1174), which would make every cell beyond 16 m glow.
   - A lit cell (Ls ≥ 0.55) shows nothing.
2. **Charge physics. This never changes with tier.**
   - Wall light: `W = min(1, L + 0.2 × Σ L of the 4 neighbours)`. Lamps light through walls (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1137-1140).
   - When W > C, C rises toward W with τ 2 s.
   - Otherwise C decays hyperbolically, `C(t) = C₀ / (1 + C₀·t / 8 s)` (SP). This is the second-order recombination shape of real ZnS:Cu afterglow.
   - **Fresh** dark (a lamp that just died) is bright. **Starved** dark (a dead cell among dead neighbours) is faint or blank. Both follow from the physics, so neither looks like a bug.
3. **Carriers.** Only wallpaper carries ink: Level 0 walls and wallpapered columns (LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC.md:57-59). No ink appears on:
   - Office drywall (:58);
   - doors, trim, glass, floors or ceilings;
   - the start area (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:389);
   - title stream rooms (10_synthesis.md:217-218).
4. **Messages and glyph families** (the shape is told by silhouette, not detail). Priority is STOP > HERE (or BREACH) > FLOW > GROUND.

   | Message | Family | Meaning | Weight (SP) |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | GROUND | neutral | Plain underprint, no direction | 0.35 |
   | FLOW (dir) | go: open chevrons | The route runs this way along this wall | 1.0 |
   | HERE | threshold: frame brackets | The route leaves through this face's door or window | 1.0 |
   | BREACH (a HERE variant) | stop: bracket with a cross bar | The Relay broke this door. It is passable and will never shut. | 1.0 |
   | STOP | stop: closed horizontal bars | This face is the mouth of a dead-end pocket | 1.0 |
   | Pressure variant (FLOW or HERE) | go or threshold, drawn doubled | Chase routing: a door away from the Relay | 1.0 |

5. **Calm target.** The nearest **new threshold**: a Door or Window edge whose far cell is in a zone not in `zonesVisited` (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:162, 869-877).
   - Unbroken windows cost +4 cells (SP), because breaking glass is heard at 40 × 1.4 = 56 m (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:150; FrontRoomsHunter.cs:32).
   - If `doorsNeedKeys` is on (FrontRoomsLevelProfile.cs:31, false today), the zone's key comes first.
   - Calm routes never read the Relay's position.
6. **Pressure target. By default it is used only while the Relay is in Chase** (this fixes the radar leak).
   - The target is an unbroken, unshut-by-Relay door whose far cell is farther from the Relay (by breadth-first search) than its near cell.
   - Route costs (SP): +6 per cell within 2 steps of the Relay; +2 per cell on its open straight line within 4 cells; +2 for cells it walked through in the last 10 s; −1 per arch edge (arches block sight).
   - Windows and BREACH doors are never pressure targets.
   - Pressure ends when the Relay enters Listen or Wander, or 20 s after the Chase ends (SP).
7. **Only on-route cells point.** The route is a greedy descent of the target field, up to 24 cells (SP). At T0-T1 it also covers cells 1 step off the route. Every other dark cell shows GROUND.
   - Simulation of beacon-seeking walkers, in new zones per 100 cells: when every dark cell points, walkers ping-pong (2.4). On-route only gives 8.0. A random walker scores 5.6.
8. **STOP** marks the mouth cell of each dead-end branch.
   - Branches are found by iterative leaf pruning. Door and window edges count as passable, and the built-area boundary counts as open.
   - The maze has loops (non-tree edges roll Open or Arch at 18-70%, FrontRoomsMap.cs:94-96, 360), so pruning is the exact test. A branch BFS is not.
   - A FLOW route never enters a branch unless its target is inside it.
9. **Truth.** Before T4 the ink never lies. It never points into a dead end, through a BREACH on the pressure route, or at the Relay's cell.
   - From T4 (optional, see §6), a **forged FLOW** may appear. It is the only mark that glows under a lit lamp, and only FLOW is ever forged.
10. **Commit gate.** A cell's message may change only when at least one of these holds:
    - (a) the cell has been unseen for ≥ 0.5 s;
    - (b) its own Ls ≥ 0.8, so the ink is invisible;
    - (c) a sag or wave front is at that cell (a deliberate beat).

    Each cell changes at most once per 2 s (SP). The glow *brightness* may change in view (that is physics). The *message* may not.
11. **Shape is procedural; substance is in B.**
    - The message shape is computed in the shader from world position plus the cell's message code.
    - The print's B channel holds the ink *substance*, which narrative authors per print slice. What you see is the shape drawn in that substance.
    - Print jumps can change the substance (read up close). They can never change the message.
    - Cells with a non-GROUND message take no lamp-dropout strip slips; their print changes only while unseen.
12. **Delivery channels.**
    - Natural dark cells (always on).
    - The first-dark beat (once per run).
    - Calm power sags (periodic, local).
    - The chase wave (rare).
    - The drought breaker (a safety net).
    - The EAR bloom (when the Relay accepts a noise).
13. **Dark is never cover, and tall halls are not refuges.**
    - The Relay's sight is a 12 m ray with no light term (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:926-931; FrontRoomsHunter.cs:26).
    - Its speeds have no ceiling-height term.
    - Nothing in the ink or its fiction may imply either.
14. **The HUD stops giving it away.** Today `RELAY nn M` renders every frame (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:1544), and the state text shows HUNT/SEARCH (:1539).
    - Ship with the state text shown only for CHASE and BREAKING DOOR.
    - Move the distance readout behind an accessibility assist.
15. **Photosafe by construction.**
    - Stutter-mode cells are forced to G = 0.
    - Ls is low-passed.
    - Each message changes at most once per 2 s.
    - Sags and waves are single dips with ramps ≥ 0.3 s.
    - Any lamp death in view dips at ≤ 2 Hz.
16. **Deterministic.** All choices are hashed from (seed, cell & 63, event counters). No `UnityEngine.Random`, no `_Time`. The same seed and inputs give the same ink timeline (synthesis P3 gate).

## 3. Placement and generation per zone and tier

Nothing is hand-placed. Every message is derived per cell from:
- **map data that does not change with revision:** zones, border edges and keys (MAP_GENERATION.md:97);
- **the lamp temperament hash:** `Hash(seed, cell, 211)`, rolled at FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1087 and 1127-1128. It is known even for unbuilt cells.

Routes are recomputed whenever a chunk is rebuilt. Rebuilds happen ≥ 24 m away (:612-616).

**Beacon sources, measured in a Python port of the generator (12-16 seeds; it skips modules, columns and the start area):**
- **Lamp temperaments:** 62.3% steady, 20.1% stutter, 9.5% failing, 5.0% dead, 3.1% dim.
- **Effective beacon cells** (failing, dead or dim): 17.6%.
  - The nearest beacon is a mean of 1.84 cells from any cell (p90 is 4).
  - On walked routes, a readable beacon comes every ~6 cells (18 m).
- **Thresholds are plentiful:** a cell is a mean 3.1 cells from a door or window. The nearest *new* threshold is typically 3-7 cells away.
- **Dead-end branches:** 31 per 1,000 cells, 70% of them 1-cell alcoves. That is about 50 in a 5×5-chunk area, about 15 of them with depth ≥ 2.

**Hint strength (150-cell walks, 16 seeds):**

| Walker | New zones / 100 cells | New thresholds / 100 cells |
|---|---|---|
| Random | 5.6 | 3.1 |
| On-route ink | 8.0 | 6.1 |
| Perfect knowledge | 15.1 | 12.5 |
| Continuous 3-cell route dimming (rejected: a GPS) | 14.7 | not measured |

**Per zone** (shares from FrontRoomsMap.cs:82-84, 117):

| Zone | Share of zones | Ink | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Standard Level 0, 2.9 m | ~38% | Full | Long corridors. Decisions are read on end walls at T-junctions. |
| Low, 2.4 m | ~35% | Full | Short sightlines and many facing walls: the best near-read zone. Doors sit on its borders. |
| Tall hall, 5.4 m | ~10% | Full, glow band 0.8-2.0 m | Exits are windows only, so calm HERE marks windows. Lamps run ×1.6 with range 12, so neighbour spill is high: dead cells read bright, and lookdev must check the paper contrast. |
| Office, 2.9 m | ~17% of zones (13.6% of cells) | None (drywall) | Deliberate blind stretches. Routes add +1 per Office cell (SP), so the ink prefers paper. |

**Room modules.** Level Designer modules can author ModuleLamp Dead/Failing/Off per cell (FrontRoomsRoomModuleData.cs:30; applied at FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1130).
- Recommended: at most 1 dark "reading room" per 4 chunks (SP).
- Off cells have L = 0 for good, so they are starved and show no ink.

**Optional "border dusk" lever.** Cells beside door or window edges roll failing 25% / dead 10% instead of 10% / 5%.
- Use it only if playtest shows HERE is too rare: naturally only 14% of exit-adjacent cells are dark themselves.
- It needs visual-chat sign-off, because flicker odds are their numbers (LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC.md:76).

**Storage.**
- 64×64 toroidal arrays indexed `(x & 63) + 64·(y & 63)`, with a 192 m period (10_synthesis.md:131).
- The built window is 40×40 (56×56 at buildRadius 3, FrontRoomsLevelProfile.cs:25), so there is no aliasing.
- A chunk's texels are cleared on build and on drop.
- Persistent per-cell sets survive chunk drops, like `brokenDoors` (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:205). They hold: killed lamps (first-dark beat, drought breaker) and BREACH edges.

Tier effects on placement are in §6.

## 4. Triggers, charge/decay and timing

**Per frame, per built cell (CPU).** Compute L, Ls, W, C and G as in R1-R2.

On chunk build, C starts at its steady state (SP):

| Temperament | Initial C |
|---|---|
| Steady | 1.0 |
| Stutter | 1.0 |
| Failing | 0.75 |
| Dim | 0.5 |
| Dead | W (spill equilibrium) |
| Off | 0 |

Visibility thresholds (SP):
- **Beacon:** G ≥ 0.08, a green patch visible from about 20 m.
- **Legible:** G ≥ 0.25, the shape reads at 12-20 m head-on.

**What each temperament does** (from `Level()`, FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1184-1214):

| Temperament | Lamp level | Ink |
|---|---|---|
| Steady (:1213-1214) | 0.98 | Nothing. A full battery for its neighbours. |
| Stutter (:1188-1196) | 0.95/0.05 bursts on Perlin(t·23) | Forced G = 0, so it never flickers ink. |
| Failing (:1198-1202) | 0.25-0.70 at ~0.49 Hz, Perlin dropouts | Breathes: about 1 s readable every ~2 s. Full reads during dropouts. |
| Dead (:1203-1210) | 0, with 0.8 blinks every 8-28 s | Spill-charged steady glow. With 2 lit neighbours, C ≈ 0.39 (legible). In a dark cluster it is starved (blank). |
| Dim (:1211-1212) | 0.42 | G ≈ 0.2, legible within ~5 m |

**Fields and route.**
- The target field and the STOP pruning are rebuilt on any of:
  - `ZoneEntered`, `KeyTaken`, `DoorMoved`, `DoorBroken`, `GlassBroken` (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:58-64);
  - `relay.StateChanged` (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:141);
  - `ChunkBuilt` / `ChunkDropped`;
  - a mode switch.
- Rebuilds are rate-limited to 2 Hz (SP) and never run in a chunk-build frame (deferred one frame).
- The route is re-descended whenever the player changes cell (~0.94 s at the 3.2 m/s walk).
- Target stickiness: keep the current threshold until it is reached, or until it is ≥ 6 cells worse than the best alternative (SP).

**First-dark beat** (once per run; replaces the pre-dead cell).
- Trigger: after the start door shuts (MAP_GENERATION.md:23-24) and within 45 s.
- Cell: the 3rd-5th cell ahead on the guaranteed open walk-in line (MAP_GENERATION.md:17-19) whose target is ≤ 6 cells beyond it.
- Its message commits while it is still lit (R10b).
- When the player is 6-9 m away and facing it, the lamp dies over 1.5 s: three dips at ≤ 2 Hz, then off. It stays Dead for the run (persistent set).
- C = 1, so it blooms bright, then settles to its spill glow.

**Power sag** (calm pacing pulse).
- Frequency: every 75-120 s at T0 (SP).
- Never within 30 s of a wave (10_synthesis.md:167). Never while the player stands in an Office zone.
- Shape: breadth-first search, radius 4 cells (12 m) around the player. Lamps dip to 0.35× with attack 0.6 s, hold 4 s, release 1.5 s.
- All messages in the radius commit at dip start. It is a snapshot, never a trail.

**Chase wave** (the synthesis's corridor wave, 10_synthesis.md:143-144, 166).
- Trigger: `StateChanged(Chase)`, if the cooldown has passed (90 s at T0, SP).
- The front runs from the Relay's cell at 8 m/s (0.375 s per cell) along passable edges, with a 0.5 s delay at shut doors. It reaches 10 cells beyond the player (SP).
- Each lamp dips to 0.3× (attack 0.3 s, hold 2.5 s, release 1.2 s). Pressure messages commit as the front arrives.
- The front outruns the 5.5 m/s sprint (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:147), so about 20 m of dim, readable corridor stays ahead of a fleeing player for the 5 s of stamina (:149).
- The same front also carries the visible print reprint.

**Drought breaker.**
- Trigger: no legible sighting for 60 s, and the Relay is not in Hunt or Chase (SP).
- Action: promote one unseen Steady cell 4-8 cells ahead on the current route to Failing (persistent per-cell override). At most once per 90 s (SP).
- In the simulation, natural beacons come every ~6 cells, so this should rarely fire. It exists for Office-heavy and starved seeds.

**EAR bloom** ("it heard you"; P2).
- When `ListenPoint` takes a new value (Noise accepted, FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:279-286), the dark cells among the source cell and its open neighbours raise their GROUND weight from 0.35 to 1.0 over a 1.5 s ramp. The bloom holds while `ListenPoint` still equals that source, then decays with τ 4 s.
- At most one bloom per 4 s, because sprint steps call `Noise` every 0.3 s (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:861-865).
- It is the only ink change allowed to start in view.
- No EAR occurs during Chase or BreakDoor, because `Noise` is ignored then (:281).

**BREACH.** On `DoorBroken` (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1055-1065), the faces of that door's wall in both cells get the BREACH variant. It is permanent and committed under R10.

**Caught** freezes everything. In the title stream rooms, G = 0.

## 6. Escalation over a run

The physics, gate and grammar never change, so what the player learns stays true. Escalation comes from scarcity, pacing, the DP08 lamps and Relay tuning, and an optional late lie.

Tiers follow the unconfirmed DP08 proposal. With no tier system, everything stays at T0.

| Tier | Route beacons | Weight (SP) | Sag every | Wave cooldown | Wave reach ahead | STOP outside waves | Forged FLOW |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T0 | on-route + 1 off | 1.0 | 75-120 s | 90 s | 10 cells | all branches | none |
| T1 | on-route + 1 off | 1.0 | 90-150 s | 120 s | 10 cells | all branches | none |
| T2 | on-route | 0.9 | 120-180 s | 150 s | 8 cells | depth ≥ 2 | none |
| T3 | on-route | 0.85 | 150-210 s | 180 s | 6 cells | depth ≥ 2 | none |
| T4+ | on-route, within 15 cells of target only | 0.8 | 180-240 s | 240 s | 6 cells | depth ≥ 2 | ≤ 1 per 4 chunks, gated on metrics |

- The weight floor stays at 0.8, so the 20 m head-on read survives at every tier (a brief constraint).
- **DP08 failing lights** add more dark cells (more beacons) but fewer lit neighbours (more starved cells). The result is more hints, each harder to read. This is consistent with R2.
- **Forged FLOW** (T4+, optional):
  - It sits in a lit Steady cell at an unmarked branch mouth and points into the branch.
  - The CPU writes G = 0.8 regardless of Ls, so it glows under full light. That is the tell.
  - Only FLOW is forged. HERE, STOP and BREACH are always true, so the "stop" words stay trustworthy, and a caught lie itself reveals a pocket.
  - It never appears in pressure mode, and never twice on one route.
- **Escalation coupling** (flagged for Red):
  - Following the ink gives about 2× new thresholds per minute, so ink followers tier up faster. This is deliberate: the ink is help and lure at once.
  - DP08's "every 4 zones" counts zone ids, and about 45% of walkable zone crossings are invisible same-height crossings, so zones tick about 3.6 per minute even for a random walker.
  - Suggestion (SP): count tiers by new thresholds, 6 per tier or 2.5 min, whichever comes first.
- **Never escalates:** truth before T4, BREACH permanence, the dark-only rule, R13.

## 8. Interaction with the moving visible print

1. **Opposite masking phases.**
   - The visible print changes in the dark: it slips inside its own cell's lamp-dark window (10_synthesis.md:139-142), because ink colour vanishes when unlit.
   - Phosphor messages change in the light (R10b), because the glow is swamped there.
   - A failing lamp gives both systems a legal window every couple of seconds, in opposite phases. A dead cell has no lit phase, so its message changes only when unseen.
2. **Message vs substance** (R11). The shape is procedural and constant across print keyframes, so jumps and crawls never move a message.
   - The B substance belongs to each print slice and may change between a failing lamp's gasps. Narrative may use this, for example writing that rewrites itself up close.
   - Message cells take no lamp-dropout strip slips, so the paper never slides under a readable mark.
3. **Discrete jumps** (the default) use the same unseen set as message commits: one visibility service serves both.
4. **Slow crawl** at scripted beats only uses cells showing GROUND. Moving ink never carries a message.
5. **Chase wave.** One BFS front at 8 m/s carries three things in lockstep: the visible reprint, the lamp dip and the pressure commit.
   - The 192 m rebase caveat (10_synthesis.md:144) does not apply, because the ink is off in the stream rooms.
6. **Relay wake.** Keep the synthesis's visible wake reprint (10_synthesis.md:145). It gives the two-layer deck line "the print shows where it walked; the ink shows where to go". Pressure routes add +2 on wake cells, so the two rarely overlap.
7. **Subliminal drift** (≤ 1-2 mm/s, ±0.3% scale) moves the B substance too. That is imperceptible and fine; the shape mask is world-fixed.
8. **Per-roll phase** `strip & 3` (10_synthesis.md:80, 193): every FLOW wall looks the same in every on-route cell. The deliberate beat is that this cell points, not that it looks unique.

## 9. Readability and accessibility

**Shapes** (procedural, world space, in a glow band 0.8-2.0 m above the floor; player eye 1.62 m, LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC.md:133):

| Shape | Geometry (SP) |
|---|---|
| FLOW | Open chevrons 400 mm tall, stroke ≥ 100 mm, pitch 375 mm (8 per 3 m wall) |
| FLOW, pressure | The same chevron, doubled: 2 × 100 mm strokes with a 60 mm gap |
| HERE | 100 × 900 mm vertical bars on the ~1 m of wall beside a door, ~0.8 m beside a window (LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC.md:48-49) |
| BREACH | HERE plus a 100 mm diagonal bar |
| STOP | 2 horizontal bars, 600 × 120 mm, per 0.75 m roll |
| GROUND | The B substance alone at weight 0.35 |

- **Direction** comes from the world axis (z when |n.x| > 0.5, else x), never the mirrored PlanarFrame u (FrontRoomsSurface.shader:157-161). Arrows therefore point the same world way from both sides of a corridor.
- **B substance rule:** the mean B within any 100 mm square must be ≥ 0.6 inside strokes, so strokes read as solid at 20 m. Fine detail is for reading under 2 m.
- **Old relief chevrons:** they were paper geometry seen in light, while these chevrons are emission seen only in the dark. The visual chat should keep proportions distinct. This is accepted as deliberate, and narrative may tie the two together (§12).

**Distances** (vertical FOV 76°, FrontRooms3DGame.cs:227, gives ≈ 691/d px per metre at 1080p):
- A 0.40 m chevron is ~14 px at 20 m, with strokes ~3.5 px.
- Side walls read only within 6-8 m, because foreshortening at 20 m down a 3 m corridor is ~0.075. **The decision read is the end wall at a T-junction or turn**; side walls confirm it up close.
- Fog is ExponentialSquared at 0.014 (FrontRoomsLook.cs:19, 32), so ~92.5% of the glow survives at 20 m.

**Luminance, not hue.**
- Glyph-to-paper ratio ≥ 1.3 in a full-charge dead cell with 2 lit neighbours; ≥ 1.15 in a failing cell at Ls 0.3 (SP).
- Emission is capped at ~12% of a lit wall's luminance, so the ink stays faint.
- Colour is about 530 nm (ZnS:Cu). Meaning is carried by shape and luminance, so it is safe for protan and deutan players.
- Screen budget: green covers ≤ 3% of pixels on average and ≤ 8% at p95, so Level 0 stays yellow.

**Photosensitivity.**
- Gate: R15, plus the P2 gate (≤ 3 flashes/s; no reversal above 3 Hz over > 25% of the screen), measured with glow, print, sags, waves and fixtures combined (10_synthesis.md:228).
- The existing stutter mode (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1196) can exceed 3 Hz in bursts on its own. Audit it regardless of the ink.

**Settings:**

| Setting | Effect |
|---|---|
| Reduce wall motion (required, 10_synthesis.md:197-200) | No travelling wave; a static 4 s sag of radius 4 cells at Chase start. Ls τ 1.0 s. Failing cells show a 3 s running mean (a steady, faint read). No crawl. The first-dark beat becomes a single 1.5 s fade. No EAR ramp shorter than 1.5 s. |
| Ink assist | Intensity ×1.5, GROUND off, strokes +30% |
| Threat readout (Off by default) | Off / State / State + distance. Today's HUD moves here. |
| Deaf and hard-of-hearing | EAR and the wave are visual first; sound only reinforces them. |

The ink is never the only signal: doors and windows stay visible as geometry.

### 10.2 Runtime failure modes

| Failure | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Beacon ping-pong (every dark cell points) | R7, on-route only (2.4 → 8.0 new zones / 100 cells) |
| GPS creep (continuous route dimming reached 14.7 vs a perfect 15.1) | Sags are snapshots; waves are chase-only with a cooldown; the on/off ratio is tracked |
| Visible message swaps | R10; dead cells commit only unseen; the ink never reuses the print's flicker-mask rule |
| Flow flip-flop | Hash tie-break on (cell & 63), 6-cell stickiness, ≤ 1 commit per 2 s |
| Glow beyond 16 m, or glow through the start door | Use logical `f.level`; ignore the hold and fade (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1171-1174) |
| Invisible same-height borders (~45%) tick ZONE without a threshold | The ink targets thresholds only; tier counting should follow |
| Lure into noise (calm route through glass, heard at 56 m) | +4 window cost; otherwise the intended risk |
| False refuge (dark or tall = safe) | R13; the first contact in a glowing corridor shows it sees you |
| Edge of the world | Built-boundary cells are fallback targets; failed chunks (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:672-683) count as walls |
| Interior shift after 30 s away (FrontRoomsLevelProfile.cs:29) | Targets do not change with revision; new routes commit ≥ 24 m away, unseen |
| Aliasing on stream, Office and start walls; jamb faces on cell lines | Ink-eligible mask; clear texels on build and drop; jamb normal bias |
| EAR spam or noise sonar (tapping sprint to probe) | One bloom per 4 s. From T3 the bloom is delayed 2-4 s if telemetry shows sprints under 0.5 s |
| Lure poisoning (players distrust all ink) | Lures only forge FLOW and only at T4+; cut them if the true-FLOW follow rate after the first lure falls below 50% |
| Glyph clipping on 0.6 m columns or between trims | Accepted; or fade where a face is narrower than 0.75 m (visual's call) |
| Starved late game (DP08 darkens the map) | Drought breaker and sags keep a floor |

## 11. Implementation data flow

### 11.1 Pipeline

**Step 1: Lamp API (map chat).**
- Add read-only `LampLevel(cell)` (logical `f.level`) and `LampMode(cell)`, a pure seed hash that also works for unbuilt cells.
- Add a `FixtureChanged` event. The synthesis already requests this (10_synthesis.md:175-178).
- Add `LampDip(cell, depth, attack, hold, release, delay)`, a multiplier applied to `f.level` inside TickFixtures (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:1160-1181).
- Add `KillLamp(cell)` / `PromoteLamp(cell, mode)`, with persistent per-cell overrides applied at `BuildFixture` (:1130).

**Step 2: `FrontRoomsWayfinding` (map chat).** A new plain-C# class in `Assets/Scripts/FrontRoomsMap/`, ticked right after TickFixtures (:569). Each frame:
- (a) L, Ls, W, C, G per built cell (≤ 1,600 cells, ~0.05 ms);
- (b) event-driven fields at ≤ 2 Hz: the target field (bucket Dijkstra, costs 0-6), the Relay BFS (pressure only), and leaf pruning for STOP;
- (c) route descent and message assignment;
- (d) the commit gate (R10);
- (e) sag, wave, first-dark, drought and EAR timers;
- (f) packing into `Color32[4096]`.

**Step 3: Visibility (shared).** A BFS over see-through edges from the camera cell plus `TestPlanesAABB` (10_synthesis.md:135-138). It produces one set, used by both print jumps and ink commits.
- Owner: whoever lands WG2 (VISUAL_CHAT_TASKS.md:70); the map chat consumes it.
- Until then, use the frustum-only fallback.

**Step 4: Pack and upload (visual chat driver).** One 64×64 RGBA8 texture, point filter, Repeat wrap, `SetPixelData` + `Apply(false)`, 16 KB per frame. Globals: `_FR_CellState` and `_FR_Ink` (intensity, reduceMotion, assist).

| Channel | Content | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| R | Print state (frame offset or transition) | Visual |
| G | Ink glow G (weight, EAR, forge already applied) × 255 | Map |
| B | Bits 0-1 direction N/E/S/W; bits 2-3 message GROUND/FLOW/HERE/STOP; bit 4 pressure; bit 5 BREACH; bit 6 forged; bit 7 ink-eligible | Map |
| A | Ls × 255, also the print's flicker mask | Map |

The final layout is agreed with the visual chat.

**Step 5: Shader (visual chat).** In FrontRoomsSurface ForwardLit under `_FR_PRINT`: one point load, about 15 ALU, no extra texture fetch. B comes from the existing print fetch.

```hlsl
int2  c    = (int2)floor((positionWS.xz + normalWS.xz * 0.5) / 3.0) & 63;
half4 s    = LOAD_TEXTURE2D(_FR_CellState, c);
uint  code = (uint)(s.b * 255.5);
float along = abs(normalWS.x) > 0.5 ? positionWS.z : positionWS.x;   // world axis, never mirrored u
float sgn   = FaceSign(code & 3, normalWS);       // +1/-1 along this face; 0 means the route crosses it -> GROUND
float m     = InkShape((code >> 2) & 3, code >> 4, along * sgn, heightAboveFloor);  // includes the 0.8-2.0 m band
emission   += _FR_InkColor * s.g * m * print.b * _FR_Ink.x * paperCavity;          // fog applied after
```

- An unset global means G = 0, so edit mode, lookdev and the Level Designer fall back to no ink.
- The ink never writes albedo, normal, smoothness or cavity.

**Step 6: Events in:**
- `DoorMoved`, `DoorBroken`, `GlassBroken`, `KeyTaken` (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:58-64);
- `relay.StateChanged` and `ListenPoint` (FrontRoomsMapHunter.cs:114-141);
- new: `ZoneEntered`, the visited set, `ChunkBuilt` / `ChunkDropped`, `Tier`.

The run is reached through `MapRunStarted` (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:608).

**Events out:** `LampDipped(cell)`, `WaveStarted(origin)`, `EarBloom(pos)`, `InkLegible(cell)` for telemetry, and `Event("ink", …)` rows (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:1578).

**Budget (SP):**
- CPU ≤ 0.4 ms on average and ≤ 1.0 ms on rebuild frames.
- GPU ≤ +0.2 ms.
- 16 KB per frame upload; 16 KB of memory.
- Measured against the synthesis perf gate (58.7 fps, p99 19.4 ms; seeds 2554 and 20388 plus a Level 0 flythrough; 10_synthesis.md:230).

## 13. Playtest plan and metrics

**Phases:**
1. **Lookdev stills:** direction call at 6/12/20 m head-on and 6 m grazing, with and without assist, plus a colour-blind filter pass.
2. **Automated audits:** 100 seeds and autopilot.
3. **Class playtest:** an A/B test with ink on and off on the same seeds, with the HUD distance off in both arms.
4. **3-run sessions:** 3 runs per player for the teaching curve.

| Metric | Target (SP) | If missed |
|---|---|---|
| Hint strength: new thresholds per minute, ink on / off | 1.6-2.2× (sim: 2.0) | Above 2.5 it is a GPS: cut sags or T0 adjacency. Below 1.3: raise the weight or enable border dusk. |
| Follow rate: FLOW within 8 m in view ≥ 0.5 s, then the next 3 cells descend the field | 50-75% | Revisit the first-dark beat or the shapes |
| Teaching: first beacon in view → first follow | < 20 s for ≥ 70% of first-time players; ≥ 70% cross their first ink-led threshold within 60 s | Add the Flash line |
| Beacon spacing on routes actually walked | One readable beacon every 5-8 cells (sim 6.2); legible sightings every 20-40 s median | Drought breaker interval; border dusk |
| Chase escape rate, wave vs no wave | Rises, but ≤ 80% at T0 and ≤ 60% at T3+ | Shorten wave reach; lengthen cooldown |
| Doors shut per chase | Rises with the wave | Pressure HERE readability |
| Catches inside leaf-pruned branches | ≥ 50% lower with ink on | STOP depth or weight |
| Office time per run; Office-heavy seeds | Track | +1 → +2 route cost |
| Minutes per tier, ink on vs off | ≤ 1.5× faster with ink | Tier counting by thresholds |
| Comprehension, after run 1 with no text: "what does the green mean?" | ≥ 70% say "way on / new area / door"; ≥ 50% name the dead end; < 15% say "dark hides me" | First-contact beat; fiction |
| Survey: help, lure or noise? | A mix of help and lure; noise < 25% | Weight, spacing |
| Forged FLOW (if on) | 30-50% followed on first exposure, < 20% by the third; true FLOW still followed ≥ 50% afterwards | Cut forgeries |
| EAR (P2) | ≥ 60% leave the bloom cells within 8 s without sprinting by the second exposure | Cue clarity |
| Truth audit (automated) | Every route ends at a valid target; 0 FLOW into branches; 0 pressure routes through windows or BREACH | Bug |
| Change-blindness audit | 0 commits while seen, except at sag, wave or EAR fronts; < 1 flip per cell per 2 s | Bug |
| Flash audit (normal and reduce-motion) | ≤ 3 flashes/s; no > 3 Hz reversal over > 25% of the screen | Lengthen ramps; fix stutter |

| Design | Play | Feasibility | Fit | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Afterglow Blazes (wayfinding), chosen** | 8 | 7 | 8 | **23** |
| Afterglow Wake (threat_intel) | 7 | 7.5 | 6 | 20.5 |
| Afterglow Ledger (light_economy) | 6 | 6 | 7 | 19 |
| Afterglow Grammar (anomaly_literacy) | 6.5 | 5 | 6.5 | 18 |

**Afterglow Wake (threat_intel), 20.5.** The ink as a ledger of the Relay: wakes that fade with age, knots where it listened, EAR blooms on accepted noise, permanent breaches, and an OMEN wave before each arrival, all read at the cost of standing in the dark.
- Strengths: the best dread, the cheapest core (it polls public hunter API), and the key catch that the HUD distance makes any intel ink pointless.
- Not chosen because: it adds nothing during a chase; its five mark kinds read at range only as "how much"; it fixes the fiction (the Relay writes the ink); and it deletes the synthesis's visible wake reprint.
- Grafted: HUD retirement, BREACH, EAR (P2), the silhouette beat.
- Rejected:
  - **OMEN:** it needs Arrive split into a delayed commit plus a new `HunterState.Arriving`, which touches release timing, sound and AUDIO_CONTRACT. Kept as a possible P3.
  - **The adaptation cost:** it taxes exactly the 20 m end-wall read that carries this design's decisions. Reading cost comes instead from scarcity and failing-lamp breathing.

**Afterglow Ledger (light_economy), 19.** Light as the price of a hint: hyperbolic charge physics, WAY and SHUT signs coded by which wallpaper roll glows, a pull-the-tube verb to buy darkness, a Relay that wanders toward dark, and lamps that only degrade with tier.
- Strengths: the truest phosphor physics, narrative freedom over glyph shape, and a strong first-dark reveal.
- Not chosen because: reads are scarce and fiddly (0.1-0.5 s gasps); there is little in a chase; and it needs a new verb (the lens collider is removed, FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:~1094), hunter weighting, noise multipliers and runtime changes to flicker odds the visual chat owns.
- Grafted: hyperbolic decay and the fresh/starved rule, constant physics across tiers, meaning in a world-space mask with the substance owned by narrative, the first-dark beat, the drought breaker.
- Pull-the-tube stays a stretch goal, used only if playtests show beacon drought.

**Afterglow Grammar (anomaly_literacy), 18.** An 8-word fixed language at branch mouths (THROUGH, BLIND, DOOR, DOOR·BLIND, GLASS, WAKE, HEART, LURE), learned across runs with no save data, with forgeries that glow under lit lamps.
- Strengths: the best fork semantics and the most elegant lie tell.
- Not chosen because:
  - fluency takes 6-10 runs, which student playtests cannot validate;
  - forced reader lamps make troffers the real tell;
  - its "every chunk is a spanning tree" premise is false (non-tree edges are Open or Arch at 18-70%, FrontRoomsMap.cs:94-96), so its dead-end words could lie;
  - tier-dependent planning breaks determinism, and it consumes the whole 32-slice print sheet.
- Grafted: silhouette families, the physical lie tell (T4+, forging FLOW only), and no strip slips under messages.
- DOOR·BLIND ("a door into a closed pocket", a refuge from a wanderer) is held as an optional POCKET variant (§15).
